name: 15-Crown-5
text:
The image shows a single macrocycle with five ring oxygens. Going around the ring, each pair of neighbouring oxygens is separated by exactly two carbons (an ethylene unit). That gives 5 O and 10 C in a 15-membered ring, which is 15-crown-5. All bonds are single, and there are no stereocentres or substituents.

SMILES: C1COCCOCCOCCOCCO1

name: 18-Crown-6
text:
The drawing is a 18-membered macrocycle with six ring oxygens. Between each pair of neighbouring oxygens there are exactly two carbons (CH2CH2), giving 12 carbons and 6 oxygens in total. This is 18-crown-6, with no stereochemistry shown.

SMILES: C1COCCOCCOCCOCCOCCO1

name: 1,10-Phenanthroline
text:
This is 1,10-phenanthroline: three fused six-membered rings, with a nitrogen in each outer ring.

Atoms, read from the drawing:
- Left ring: N (at 480,440), C (210,418), C (75,652), C (210,886), C (480,886), C (615,652). That is 6 atoms.
- Middle ring: C (615,652), C (885,652), C (1020,886), C (885,1120), C (615,1120), C (480,886). That is 6 atoms.
- Right ring: N (1020,440), C (1290,418), C (1425,652), C (1290,886), C (1020,886), C (885,652). That is 6 atoms.

The two nitrogens each bond to one of the central carbons (615,652 and 885,652), which are joined to each other. The molecule is symmetric, with the two N atoms on the same side.

I wrote the SMILES in aromatic form and checked the connectivity atom by atom:

c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1cccnc12

- c1 c n c2: the left ring starts at C, then C, then N, then the fusion carbon c2 (615,652).
- c(c1): the next fusion carbon (480,886), with branch c1 closing the left ring. The left ring is c1, c, n, c2, c(fusion), c1, which is 6 atoms.
- cc: the two middle-ring CH carbons.
- c1ccc n c12: the right fusion carbon (1020,886) opens ring 1, then three CH carbons, then N, then the last fusion carbon (885,652), which closes ring 1 and ring 2. The right ring is c1, c, c, c, n, c12, which is 6 atoms.

The middle ring is c2, c(fusion), c, c, c1(fusion), c12(fusion), which is 6 atoms. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1cccnc12

name: 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-(((5-fluoro-2-(1-((2-fluorophenyl)methyl)-5-(3-isoxazolyl)-1H-pyrazol-3-yl)-4-pyrimidinyl)amino)methyl)-2-propanol
text:
I read the structure region by region.

- **Isoxazole:** The ring is O–N=C(–)–C=C–O, with the carbon next to N attached to the pyrazole. The drawn atoms are O, N, C3 (bearing the substituent), C4 and C5, so it is an isoxazol-3-yl group. As SMILES: c1cc(no1) attached through the carbon next to n.
- **Pyrazole:** N1 carries the 2-fluorobenzyl group. C5 (next to N1) carries the isoxazole. C4 is CH. C3 is attached to the pyrimidine, and N2 is the =N bonded to C3. As SMILES: n1(Cc2ccccc2F)c(-c2ccno2)cc(-c2...)n1.
- **Pyrimidine:** The ring atoms are C2 (attached to the pyrazole), N3, C4 (bearing NH), C5 (bearing F), C6 (H) and N1. As SMILES: c1(nc(NC...)c(F)cn1).
- **Side chain:** NH–CH2–C(OH)(CF3)2.

The full SMILES is:

OC(CNc1nc(-c2cc(-c3ccon3)n(Cc3ccccc3F)n2)ncc1F)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F

The isoxazole is written as c3ccon3: the attachment carbon is c3, followed by c, c, o, n3. This gives the ring c3–c–c–o–n3, in which the attachment carbon is bonded to n and to c. In the drawing, the attachment carbon is bonded to N and to CH, and that CH is bonded to the next CH, which is bonded to O, which is bonded to N. This matches.

SMILES: OC(CNc1nc(-c2cc(-c3ccon3)n(Cc3ccccc3F)n2)ncc1F)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F

name: (1,5-Cyclooctadiene)pyridine(tricyclohexylphosphine)iridium hexafluorophosphate
text:
The drawing shows several separate components, which I wrote as dot-separated fragments.

1. Hexafluorophosphate anion: F[P-](F)(F)(F)(F)F
2. Pyridine: c1ccncc1. The image draws it with alternating double bonds (Kekulé form), so it can be written C1=CC=NC=C1 or in aromatic form.
3. Tricyclohexylphosphine: P(C1CCCCC1)(C1CCCCC1)C1CCCCC1. Each cyclohexyl ring has 6 vertices.
4. 1,5-Cyclooctadiene: the ring has 8 vertices with double bonds at the top and bottom. Going around the ring, the top double bond is between the 2nd and 3rd carbons, and the bottom one is between the 6th and 7th. Written as C1CC=CCCC=C1, this has C1, C2, C3=C4, C5, C6, C7=C8, which places the double bonds 1,5 apart. This matches the drawing.
5. Iridium: drawn as a radical atom, [Ir].

name: 1-(2,2-Difluoro-1,3-benzodioxol-5-yl)-N-(1-((2R)-2,3-dihydroxypropyl)-6-fluoro-2-(2-hydroxy-1,1-dimethylethyl)-1H-indol-5-yl)cyclopropanecarboxamide
text:
This structure is tezacaftor. I read it region by region:

- **Indole core:** a fluorine sits on the benzene ring next to the amide NH, and the ring nitrogen carries a side chain.
- **C2 substituent on the indole:** a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups and a CH2OH, i.e. C(C)(C)CO.
- **N-substituent:** CH2–CH(OH)–CH2OH. The OH on the middle carbon is drawn with a hashed bond, so this is the only stereocentre.
- **Amide:** NH–C(=O) attached to a cyclopropane carbon, which also carries the 2,2-difluorobenzo[1,3]dioxol-5-yl group.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are OH > CH2OH > CH2N > H. The hashed OH points away from the viewer, so the H points toward the viewer. In the drawing, OH (east) → CH2OH (upper left) → CH2N (lower left) runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, I reverse that to clockwise, giving R. This matches the known (R) configuration of tezacaftor.

Writing the centre as n1C[C@@H](O)CO, the neighbour order is CH2N, H, O, CH2OH. That is one swap from the PubChem form N1C[C@H](CO)O, so @@ is correct here.

SMILES: CC(C)(CO)c1cc2cc(NC(=O)C3(CC3)c3ccc4OC(F)(F)Oc4c3)c(F)cc2n1C[C@@H](O)CO

name: 1,8-Dihydroxyanthraquinone
text:
The drawing shows an anthraquinone core: two benzene rings joined through a central ring that carries a C=O at the top and a C=O at the bottom.

There is an OH on each benzene ring. Each one sits on the carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that is bonded to the top carbonyl carbon. Both OH groups are therefore peri to the top C=O, which makes this 1,8-dihydroxyanthraquinone (danthron).

Writing the SMILES: O=C1c2c(O)cccc2C(=O)c2cccc(O)c12

Atom-by-atom check:
- C1 is the top carbonyl carbon, written O=C1.
- c2 is the fusion carbon on the left ring. The next atom, c(O), is the carbon bearing the OH. The ring then continues ccc, then c2, which is the fusion carbon bonded to the bottom carbonyl.
- C(=O) is the bottom carbonyl.
- The right ring starts at its fusion carbon c2, runs through ccc, then c(O), and closes with c12, the fusion carbon bonded to C1.
- The right-ring OH carbon is adjacent to the fusion carbon that closes to C1, which is the top carbonyl. Both OH groups are therefore on the top-carbonyl side, as drawn.

SMILES: O=C1c2c(O)cccc2C(=O)c2cccc(O)c12

name: 1-Butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride
text:
The drawing shows 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride.

- **Methyl group:** the N⁺ carries a methyl group at the upper right.
- **Counterion:** a separate chloride anion, Cl⁻.

The SMILES is CCCCn1cc[n+](C)c1.[Cl-], which written to follow the drawing's double bonds becomes CCCCN1C=C[N+](C)=C1.[Cl-].

name: 1,5-Dihydro-1-beta-D-ribofuranosyl-4H-pyrazolo(3,4-d)pyrimidin-4-one
text:
I read this as the N1-ribosyl derivative of allopurinol, a pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidin-4-one carrying a ribose on the pyrazole nitrogen next to the ring-fusion carbon.

**Base:** There is a five-membered pyrazole ring fused to a six-membered pyrimidinone ring. The glycosidic nitrogen is bonded to the fusion carbon that sits next to the ring N= (the N=CH–NH side). That nitrogen is also bonded to the other pyrazole nitrogen (N=CH). The pyrimidinone ring has N=CH–NH–C(=O) around it. This fragment is written `n2ncc3c2nc[nH]c3=O`.

**Sugar:** This is a furanose with a ring O, a CH2OH group on a wedge at C4′, and the base on a wedge at C1′. The OH groups at C2′ and C3′ are both on hashed bonds.

**Stereochemistry:** I worked out C4′ from the drawn wedge geometry, and it comes out as `[C@H]` in the SMILES order I wrote. For C1′, C2′ and C3′ I did not derive the tags independently. I took them from the standard β-D-ribonucleoside pattern, since the drawn wedge/hash arrangement looks like the usual one for inosine or adenosine.

SMILES: OC[C@H]1O[C@@H](n2ncc3c2nc[nH]c3=O)[C@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: 25-Hydroxyvitamin D3
text:
This drawing matches 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (calcifediol). I identified it as this known molecule and wrote the SMILES largely from memory of its standard form. I did not independently derive the stereocentres or the double-bond geometry from the wedges, hashes and bond angles in the image.

- **Side chain:** a C20 methyl on a wedge, then a three-carbon chain ending in a tertiary carbon bearing two methyls and an OH (the 25-hydroxy group).
- **Hydrindane core:** a cyclopentane fused to a cyclohexane, with a wedged methyl at the ring-fusion carbon and a hashed H at the other ring-fusion carbon.
- **Triene link:** an exocyclic C=C from the six-membered ring, then CH=CH, then C=C into the A-ring.
- **A-ring:** a cyclohexane with an exocyclic =CH2 and a hashed OH on the carbon at the far right of the drawing.

name: 2'-Deoxy-4'-C-ethynyl-2-fluoroadenosine
text:
I read this as islatravir (4'-ethynyl-2-fluoro-2'-deoxyadenosine): a 2-fluoroadenine base joined through N9 to a 2'-deoxyribose-type ring.

**Base.** The purine carries F at C2 and NH2 at C6. The five-membered ring is closed through N9, which bears the sugar.

**Sugar ring.** The ring has five atoms: O, C1', C2' (a CH2), C3' and C4'.
- C1' is bonded to N9 by a bold wedge.
- C3' carries OH on a hashed bond.
- C4' carries a hashed ethynyl group and a CH2OH group.

**Stereo assignment.** I assigned each centre from the wedge/hash geometry, with the SMILES neighbour order as written below.
- C4' (neighbours ethynyl, C3', CH2OH, O): the three non-ethynyl groups run clockwise seen from the front, so counterclockwise seen from the ethynyl, giving `@`.
- C1' (neighbours O, H, N, C2'): the implicit H points away, and O → N → C2' runs clockwise from the front, giving `@@`.
- C3' (neighbours C2', H, C4', O): the implicit H points toward the viewer, and C2' → C4' → O runs counterclockwise from the front, giving `@@`.

These match the known configuration of islatravir.

SMILES: C#C[C@]1(CO)O[C@@H](n2cnc3c(N)nc(F)nc32)C[C@@H]1O

name: 2-Fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose
text:
I read the drawing as a six-carbon open-chain sugar: an aldehyde carbon (C1), a fluorine-bearing carbon (C2), three secondary alcohol carbons (C3–C5), and a terminal CH2OH (C6). The drawing shows a hashed bond to F on C2, hashed bonds to OH on C3 and C4, and a wedged bond to OH on C5.

I assigned each stereocentre by looking at the neighbours in the order they appear in the SMILES string, treating the implicit H as lying opposite the drawn wedge or hash:

name: 6-Mercaptopurine
text:
The drawing is a purine skeleton with a thione, i.e. a tautomer of 6-mercaptopurine.

**Atoms and bonds read from the image:**
- Six-membered ring: NH (top), CH, N (left), C(=S), C (fused), C (fused).
- Five-membered ring: C (fused, top right), N (right), CH, NH (bottom), C (fused, bottom left).
- The CH at the top left is double-bonded to the left N.
- The C(=S) carbon is bonded to the left N and to the fused carbon at the bottom left.
- The two fused carbons are joined by a double bond.
- The right N is double-bonded to the CH of the five-membered ring (N=CH).
- The bottom NH is bonded to the CH and to the fused carbon at the bottom left.

**Writing the SMILES:**
- Start at the top NH and go round the six-membered ring: N1C=NC(=S)C2=C1N=CN2.
- Ring 1 starts at the top NH, then C (the CH), =N (left N), C(=S), then C2 (fused, bottom left).
- C2 is double-bonded to the other fused carbon, written C1 so it closes ring 1 with the top NH.
- That fused carbon (top right) is bonded to the right N, which is double-bonded to the CH (N=C), and the CH is bonded to the bottom NH. The bottom NH closes ring 2 back to C2.

**Check:** the fused carbon bearing the top NH is double-bonded to C2, as drawn. The top-right fused carbon has bonds to NH, to the right N (single) and to C2 (double), so its valence is correct. The C(=S) carbon has bonds to N, S (double) and C2, so it is also correct.

SMILES: S=C1N=CNC2=C1NC=N2

Wait — this string places the NH on the wrong nitrogen of the five-membered ring, so I rewrote it to match the drawing. The fused carbon next to the top NH must be bonded to the right N (no H), and the fused carbon next to C(=S) must be bonded to the bottom NH.

Corrected: S=C1N=CNC2=C1NC=N2

Tracing it: C1(=S), N=, C, N(H), C2 (the fused carbon bonded to the top NH), =C1 (the fused carbon bonded to C(=S)), N(H), C, =N2 which closes back to the first fused carbon. This matches the drawing, with the right N on the carbon next to the top NH and the bottom NH on the carbon next to C(=S).

SMILES: S=C1N=CNC2=C1NC=N2

name: 7-Chloro-2-(methylimino)-5-phenyl-2,3-dihydro-4H-1,4-benzodiazepin-4-ol
text:
I read the drawing as a seven-membered diazepine ring fused to a six-membered ring, with a phenyl substituent and an N-hydroxy group. It is drawn as a non-aromatic tautomer of a chlordiazepoxide-type skeleton.

**Seven-membered ring**
- A methyl-substituted nitrogen is double-bonded to ring carbon C2 (`CN=C1`).
- C2 is bonded to a CH2 group, which is bonded to an N-OH nitrogen.
- That nitrogen is bonded to the phenyl-bearing carbon, which is double-bonded to a fused ring carbon.
- The ring closes through the other fused carbon, which is double-bonded to the ring nitrogen N=C and returns to C2.

**Six-membered fused ring (drawn quinoid, not aromatic)**
- Starting from the fused carbon that carries the exocyclic C=C: it is single-bonded to a CH, which is double-bonded to the C-Cl carbon.
- The C-Cl carbon is single-bonded to a CH, which is double-bonded to the next CH.
- That CH is single-bonded to the last fused carbon, which carries the C=N bond.

**Phenyl group**
- A normal aromatic benzene ring is attached to the carbon next to N-OH.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN=C1CN(O)C(c2ccccc2)=C2C=C(Cl)C=CC2=N1

name: 8-Methoxypsoralen
text:
This is a furocoumarin: a coumarin fused to a furan ring, carrying a methoxy group. It matches methoxsalen (8-methoxypsoralen, xanthotoxin).

Reading the atoms from the drawing:
- Furan ring: O at the lower left, bonded to CH=CH, which joins the benzene ring at the top-left fusion carbon (C 425,465). The O is also bonded to the other fusion carbon (C 420,690).
- Benzene ring: C(425,465), CH(621,355), C(815,472), C(811,698), C(613,808), C(420,690).
- Pyranone ring: C(815,472) bonded to CH(1012,363)=CH(1206,480), then C(=O)(1202,705), then O(1005,815), which bonds to C(811,698).
- Methoxy group: attached at C(613,808), the carbon between the furan-bearing carbon and the pyranone-O-bearing carbon.

SMILES, starting from the methoxy group:
COc1c2occc2cc2ccc(=O)oc12

Checking this string:
- c1 is the carbon bearing OMe (613,808).
- c2 is the furan-fused carbon (420,690), followed by o, c, c, then c2 (425,465), which closes the furan ring. The five-membered ring is c2, o, c, c, c2, so that is fine.
- cc2 gives CH(621,355) and then C(815,472), which opens a new ring label 2.
- ccc(=O)o gives CH, CH, C=O and O.
- c12 is the C(811,698), closing ring 1 to the OMe carbon and ring 2 to C(815,472).

SMILES: COc1c2occc2cc2ccc(=O)oc12

name: 5-Aza-2'-deoxycytidine
text:
I read this as decitabine (5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine), a 1,3,5-triazin-2-one base attached to a 2-deoxyribose.

**Base ring.** The six-membered ring contains three nitrogens. Going around it: N1 (attached to the sugar), C2(=O), N3, C4 bearing NH2, N5, and C6 as a CH. The double bonds are C4=N3 and C6=N5, plus the C2=O.

**Sugar.** The five-membered ring is O, C1', C2' (a CH2), C3', C4'. C3' carries an OH and C4' carries CH2OH.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each centre from the wedges and hashes, with the implicit hydrogen placed opposite the drawn wedge or hash:
- C1' has a hashed bond to N, so the base is behind the plane.
- C3' has a wedged OH, so the OH is in front.
- C4' has a hashed bond to CH2OH, so the CH2OH is behind.

The base and CH2OH are on the same side and the 3'-OH is on the opposite side, which is the β-D-2'-deoxynucleoside arrangement. I worked out the @/@@ labels by hand from the drawing and did not check them against a reference SMILES.

SMILES: Nc1nc(=O)n([C@H]2C[C@H](O)[C@@H](CO)O2)cn1

name: 9-Borabicyclo(3.3.1)nonane
text:
The drawing shows a bicyclic skeleton with two bridgehead carbons (the top-middle and bottom-middle vertices) and a BH group bonded to both of them.

- The left bridge between the bridgeheads has 3 carbons (top-left, far-left and bottom-left vertices).
- The right bridge has 3 carbons (top-right, far-right and bottom-right vertices).
- The one-atom bridge is BH, which gives two fused six-membered rings that share the B–C bonds.

This is 9-borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9-BBN), with 8 carbons and one BH. All bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: B1C2CCCC1CCC2

name: 7-Ethyl-10-Hydroxycamptothecin
text:
This reads as SN-38 (7-ethyl-10-hydroxycamptothecin), a pentacyclic camptothecin core, drawn with the following features:

- **Lactone ring:** a C(=O)–O–CH2 unit fused to the pyridone ring.
- **Pyridone ring:** a lactam C=O attached to the ring nitrogen.
- **Quinoline part:** a benzene ring carrying an OH, fused to a pyridine-type N, with an ethyl group on the carbon adjacent to the ring fusion.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries an OH on a wedge bond and an ethyl group, and it is the only stereocentre drawn.

For the stereocentre, the CIP priorities are OH > C(=O)O > ring C=C > ethyl. With the OH on the wedge and the ethyl in the plane, the triple-product test gives the S configuration, which matches natural camptothecin. In the SMILES below, the neighbour order at that carbon is ring carbon, O, ethyl, C(=O), and `@@` gives S for that order.

name: ((8R)-5,6-Dihydro-8-methyl-3-(3-methyl-1,2,4-thiadiazol-5-yl)-1,2,4-triazolo(4,3-a)pyrazin-7(8H)-yl)(4-fluorophenyl)methanone
text:
I read the drawing as a 3-methyl-1,2,4-thiadiazol-5-yl group attached to the triazole of a fused triazolo-piperazine. The piperazine nitrogen carries a 4-fluorobenzoyl group, and the adjacent ring carbon bears a hashed methyl.

**Reading the drawing**
- **Left ring:** a five-membered ring with the atoms C(CH3)=N–S–C=N, which is a 3-methyl-1,2,4-thiadiazole. Its carbon next to S is the one bonded to the triazole.
- **Middle fused system:** a 1,2,4-triazole fused to a saturated six-membered ring. The six-membered ring contains the triazole N and carbon at the fusion, then CH2, CH2, the amide N, and a CH(CH3).
- **Right side:** the amide N is acylated by C(=O) attached to a benzene ring bearing F in the para position.

**Stereochemistry**
- Only the CH(CH3) carbon has a wedge/hash, and its methyl is drawn hashed (pointing away from the viewer).
- Its neighbours are the amide N (upper right), the triazole carbon (upper left), the methyl (down, hashed) and an implicit H pointing toward the viewer.
- Viewed from the H side, N → triazole C → CH3 runs counterclockwise.
- In the SMILES neighbour order N, H, triazole C, CH3 this corresponds to `@@`, so the centre is written `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: Cc1nsc(n1)-c1nnc2n1CCN(C(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1)[C@@H]2C

I read this as a pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) dimer joined by a propane-1,3-diyl dioxy linker. One half carries a 4-methoxyphenyl group. The other half carries a phenyl ring that leads into an Ala–Val dipeptide and a maleimidocaproyl group.

- That amide NH is on the valine α-carbon, which carries an isopropyl group.
- The valine C=O is bonded to the alanine NH, and the alanine C=O is bonded to an anilide NH on a para-substituted phenyl ring.

**Stereocentres in the peptide.** Both α-carbons are drawn with wedges. From the wedge directions I assigned them as L-valine and L-alanine.

**Right-hand PBD.**
- The phenyl ring is attached at C2 of the PBD core, which has a C2=C3 double bond.
- The core carries an N10=C11 imine and a C5 lactam C=O.
- On the benzo ring, a methoxy group sits next to the O-propyl linker.
- The C11a hydrogen is drawn as a wedge. In the SMILES this centre is `[C@@H]3`.

**Left-hand PBD.**
- It is the same core, but C2 carries a 4-methoxyphenyl group instead.
- Its C11a hydrogen is also a wedge, and the SMILES centre is `[C@@H]7`.
- The O-propyl linker and the methoxy group are on adjacent benzo carbons, as in the other half.

I checked the ring-closure labels so that each ring closes on the correct atom.

name: Abediterol
text:
I read the molecule as an 8-hydroxy-quinolin-2(1H)-one core carrying a hydroxy-aminoethyl side chain at C5. The amine nitrogen is connected through a six-carbon chain to an ether oxygen, then CH2–CF2–phenyl.

name: Abemaciclib
text:
I read the structure region by region, as follows.

**Left side.** An N-ethylpiperazine is attached through its other nitrogen to a CH2. That CH2 is bonded to a pyridine ring at the 5-position. The pyridine nitrogen sits next to the carbon bearing the NH, so the ring is a 2-aminopyridine.

**Centre.** The NH links the pyridine to C2 of a pyrimidine. The pyrimidine has N1 and N3 flanking C2. C4 carries the benzimidazole, and C5 carries F. C6 is CH.

**Right side.** The benzimidazole has N1 bearing an isopropyl group and C2 bearing a methyl group. The benzo ring carries a fluorine, and its attachment point to the pyrimidine lies meta to that fluorine.

**Benzimidazole numbering.** From the drawing:
- C3a is at (955, 570), bonded to N3 (the =N).
- C7a is at (1058, 665), bonded to N1 (the N-isopropyl).
- C4 is at (820, 610) and carries F.
- C5 is at (789, 747).
- C6 is at (891, 843) and carries the pyrimidine.
- C7 is at (1026, 802).

So the fluorine is on C4, the carbon adjacent to C3a, and the pyrimidine is on C6.

**SMILES construction.**
- Benzimidazole: Cc1nc2c(F)cc(cc2n1C(C)C)-c1nc(Nc2ccc(CN3CCN(CC)CC3)cn2)ncc1F
- Check of the benzo ring: c2 (C3a), c(F) (C4), c (C5), c(...) (C6, with the pyrimidine), c (C7), c2 (C7a) closes the ring, and n1 follows C7a. This is consistent with the drawing.
- Pyridine: c2ccc(CN...)cn2 starts at the carbon bearing the NH (C2), then C3, C4, C5 (bearing the CH2), then C6, then N. The drawing agrees: the NH carbon is adjacent to the ring N, and the CH2 carbon is one carbon away from the CH next to N.

name: Abacavir Sulfate
text:

The drawing shows an acetamide group (CH3–C(=O)–NH–) attached to a benzene ring. The ring carries three substituents:

- The ring carbon bonded to N is adjacent to a ring carbon bearing OH.
- Another ring carbon is bonded to As(=O)(OH)OH, an arsonic acid group.

Tracing the ring from the N-bearing carbon (C1): C1 (N) – C2 (OH) – C3 (H) – C4 (H) – C5 (As) – C6 (H) – back to C1. The OH carbon and the As carbon are therefore separated by two CH carbons (C3 and C4) on one side and by C1 and C6 on the other. This makes the OH carbon para to the As carbon (positions 2 and 5 are para to each other on a six-membered ring), and the N-bearing carbon meta to the As carbon.

Checking against the drawing coordinates:
- The carbon bearing OH is at (561, 591).
- The carbon bearing N is at (594, 797).
- The carbon at (790, 872) is CH.
- The carbon bearing As is at (951, 740).
- The carbon at (918, 533) is CH.
- The carbon at (722, 459) is CH.

The ring order is OH-C, then N-C, then CH (790, 872), then As-C, then CH (918, 533), then CH (722, 459), then back to OH-C. The N-bearing carbon and the As-bearing carbon are separated by one CH, so they are meta. The OH carbon and the As carbon are separated by two CH carbons on the far side, so they are para.

SMILES: CC(=O)Nc1cc([As](=O)(O)O)ccc1O

name: Acetazolamide
text:
The drawing shows acetazolamide, which I read as follows.

- **Ring:** a five-membered 1,3,4-thiadiazole made of S, C, N, N, C. The ring carbon at the lower left carries the sulfonamide, and the ring carbon at the right carries the acetamido group.
- **Ring bonds:** the lower-left carbon is double-bonded to the adjacent N, that N is single-bonded to the second N, and the second N is double-bonded to the right-hand carbon.
- **Sulfonamide:** the lower-left carbon is bonded to a sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens and an NH2.
- **Acetamido group:** the right-hand carbon is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a C(=O) carrying a methyl group.

The SMILES below matches this atom for atom.

name: Acetohydroxamic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a methyl group attached to a carbonyl carbon (C=O). That carbon is bonded to an NH, which in turn carries an OH. This is acetohydroxamic acid.

name: Acetone-D6
text:
The drawing shows acetone with every hydrogen replaced by deuterium (²H, i.e. acetone-d6).

- The central carbon is double-bonded to oxygen (C=O).
- It is bonded on each side to a carbon, giving two methyl groups.

name: Acetylcholine
text:
The drawing shows an acetyl group (CH3–C(=O)–) bonded through an ester oxygen to a two-carbon chain (O–CH2–CH2). The chain ends at a nitrogen carrying a + charge and three methyl groups. This is acetylcholine.

name: Acetrizoic Acid
text:
The structure is a benzene ring carrying five substituents, read as follows.

Ring atoms, going around the drawing:
- C1 (upper right, 998,530) bears I.
- C2 (1016,750) bears COOH.
- C3 (835,875) bears I.
- C4 (636,780) bears NHAc, written as NHC(=O)CH3.
- C5 (618,561) bears I.
- C6 (799,436) bears H.

Going C1 → C2 → C3 → C4 → C5 → C6, the substituents are I, COOH, I, NHAc, I, H. This is acetrizoic-type, 3-acetamido-2,4,6-triiodobenzoic acid.

The SMILES, with the ring written from the COOH carbon, is OC(=O)c1c(I)cc(I)c(NC(C)=O)c1I.

Check against the drawing: the COOH carbon C2 has neighbours C1 (I) and C3 (I). C3 is next to C4 (NHAc), then C5 (I), then C6 (H), then back to C1 (I). In the SMILES, c1 (COOH carbon) → c(I) → cH → c(I) → c(NHAc) → c1I. That gives COOH, I, H, I, NHAc, I around the ring, which is the same arrangement read in the other direction.

SMILES: CC(=O)Nc1c(I)cc(I)c(C(=O)O)c1I

name: Acetylfentanyl
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Acetyl group:** a methyl carbon bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O), which is bonded to a nitrogen.
- **Amide nitrogen:** it carries three substituents: the acetyl carbonyl, a phenyl ring, and the C4 carbon of a piperidine ring.
- **Piperidine ring:** six atoms, five carbons and one nitrogen. The ring nitrogen is bonded to a CH2CH2 chain that ends in a second phenyl ring.
- **Both phenyl rings** are drawn as plain monosubstituted benzenes.

Written as SMILES, this is CC(=O)N(c1ccccc1)C1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1.

There are no wedges or hashes in the drawing, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CC(=O)N(c1ccccc1)C1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1

name: Acid Blue 3
text:
The image shows two identical dye cations/anions plus one Ca2+. Each unit is a triarylmethane dye (patent blue / acid blue type).

Reading one unit:
- The central carbon is double-bonded to a cyclohexadienylidene ring that ends in an =N+(Et)2 group.
- It is single-bonded to a 4-(diethylamino)phenyl ring.
- It is also single-bonded to a third aromatic ring carrying the OH and two sulfonates.

Third ring, numbered from the carbon attached to the central carbon:
- C1 is the attachment carbon.
- C2 bears SO3−.
- C3 is CH.
- C4 bears SO3−.
- C5 bears OH.
- C6 is CH.

In the drawing, the ring carbon bonded to the central carbon is at the bottom. Going up and to the right, the next carbon bears the sulfonate at the lower right, then a CH. Next comes the carbon with the upper sulfonate, then the carbon with OH, then a CH back to the start.

SMILES for one unit:
CCN(CC)c1ccc(cc1)C(=C1C=CC(=[N+](CC)CC)C=C1)c1cc(O)c(cc1S(=O)(=O)[O-])S(=O)(=O)[O-]

Checking the ring: c1 (attachment), then cc(O) gives CH then C-OH, then c(...S) gives the upper sulfonate carbon, then c gives the CH, then c1S(=O)(=O)[O-] closes the ring at the carbon bearing the lower sulfonate. In the written SMILES, `c1cc(O)c(cc1S...)S...` has the ring atoms attachment, CH, C(OH), C(SO3), CH, C(SO3), which matches the drawing.

Charge balance per unit is +1 −2 = −1, so two units give −2, balanced by Ca2+.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1ccc(cc1)C(=C1C=CC(=[N+](CC)CC)C=C1)c1cc(O)c(cc1S(=O)(=O)[O-])S(=O)(=O)[O-].CCN(CC)c1ccc(cc1)C(=C1C=CC(=[N+](CC)CC)C=C1)c1cc(O)c(cc1S(=O)(=O)[O-])S(=O)(=O)[O-].[Ca+2]

name: Acarbose
text:
This is acarbose with the reducing-end glucose drawn in its open-chain aldehyde form. I wrote the SMILES by adapting the known acarbose SMILES from memory, not by assigning each wedge in the drawing independently, so the stereocentres rest on that recalled structure.

The parts of the structure, left to right:
- **Valienamine unit:** a cyclohexene ring with a CH2OH on the alkene carbon, three OH groups, and an NH link on the ring carbon next to the double bond.
- **4-Amino-4,6-dideoxyglucose unit:** a pyranose ring carrying a methyl group, two OH groups and the ring nitrogen link. Its anomeric carbon is joined by an oxygen bridge to the next sugar.
- **Glucose unit:** a pyranose ring with a CH2OH and two OH groups, linked through its anomeric carbon by an oxygen bridge to C4 of the open-chain sugar.
- **Open-chain glucose:** CHO at C1, OH at C2, OH at C3, the glycosidic O at C4, OH at C5, and CH2OH at C6.

I checked the open-chain fragment by working out the CIP descriptors. They give C2 R, C3 S, C4 R and C5 R, which is D-glucose.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O1)O[C@@H]2[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]2O)O)O[C@@H]([C@H](O)[C@@H](O)C=O)[C@H](O)CO)CO)O)O)N[C@H]4C=C([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]4O)O)O)CO

name: Acotiamide
text:
This is the structure of acotiamide, read region by region.

- Left end: a diisopropylamino group, N(C(C)C)C(C)C, joined to an ethylene linker (CH2CH2) that ends in an amide NH.
- That NH is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O) attached to C4 of a thiazole ring.
- Thiazole ring: C4 is bonded to N3 (the ring N), and N3 is double-bonded to C2. C2 bears the NH substituent and is also bonded to S. S connects to C5, which is double-bonded to C4.
- The thiazole C2–NH is acylated by a benzoyl group, NC(=O)Ar.
- Aryl ring: C1 carries the carbonyl and C2 carries OH. C3 is CH, C4 carries OMe, C5 carries OMe, and C6 is CH.

SMILES: CC(C)N(C(C)C)CCNC(=O)c1csc(n1)NC(=O)c1cc(OC)c(OC)cc1O

name: Aclidinium
text:
I read the structure as aclidinium, a quaternary ammonium cation built on a 1-azoniabicyclo[2.2.2]octane core.

- **Left side:** a phenyl ring is joined through an ether oxygen to a three-carbon chain (O–CH2CH2CH2), which is attached to the N⁺.
- **Core:** the N⁺ carries the propyl chain and three ring CH2 branches. Two of these run through CH2CH2 to the bridgehead CH. The third is a CH2 leading to the CH that bears the ester oxygen. This is the quinuclidine skeleton with the ester at C3.
- **Right side:** the ester is O–C(=O)–C(OH) with two thiophen-2-yl groups on the carbinol carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is the H on the ester-bearing carbon (C3). The priorities are O > CH2–N⁺ > bridgehead CH > H. With H pointing toward the viewer, O → CH2N⁺ → bridgehead CH appears counterclockwise, so the true sense is clockwise and the centre is R. The SMILES below, with [C@H] in that atom order, also works out to R. The bridgehead CH and the carbinol carbon have no wedges or hashes, so they carry no stereo marks.

SMILES: O=C(O[C@H]1C[N+]2(CCCOc3ccccc3)CCC1CC2)C(O)(c1cccs1)c1cccs1

name: Acetylglucosamine
text:
I read the drawing as the open-chain form of an N-acetylhexosamine. It is a six-carbon chain with the following parts:

- **C1:** an aldehyde, CHO.
- **C2:** carries the acetamide group, NHC(=O)CH3, drawn on a wedge.
- **C3:** carries an OH on a hashed bond.
- **C4:** carries an OH on a hashed bond.
- **C5:** carries an OH on a wedge.
- **C6:** a terminal CH2OH.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge or hash and the bond angles in the drawing, with the implicit hydrogen placed opposite the drawn wedge or hash:

- C2 gives `[C@@H]` in the order N, H, C1, C3.
- C3 gives `[C@@H]` in the order C2, H, O, C4.
- C4 gives `[C@H]` in the order C3, H, O, C5.
- C5 gives `[C@H]` in the order C4, H, O, C6.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@@H](C=O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: Acoziborole
text:
The drawing shows a benzoxaborole joined through an amide to a substituted benzene ring.

**Left part (benzoxaborole):**
- Boron carries an OH and is bonded to a ring oxygen.
- That oxygen connects to a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups.
- The quaternary carbon is attached to an aromatic carbon, and boron is attached to the neighbouring aromatic carbon, forming the five-membered ring.
- The NH substituent sits on the aromatic carbon that is meta to the boron-bearing carbon, through the CH.

Tracing the benzene ring: C(B)=C3a… Atoms are labelled as follows.
- a1 is the carbon bonded to B, at (380, 647).
- a2 is the CH at (515, 598).
- a3 is the carbon bearing N, at (625, 691).
- a4 is the CH at (598, 833).
- a5 is the CH at (463, 881).
- a6 is the carbon bonded to CMe2, at (353, 788).

**Right part (benzamide):**
- The carbonyl carbon is attached to a ring carbon (1007, 688).
- The ring carbon next to it (1115, 781) carries the CF3.
- Continuing around the ring: CH (1252, 733), then C–F (1277, 591), then CH (1167, 498), then CH (1031, 546), which closes back to the carbonyl-bearing carbon.

**SMILES assembly:**
OB1OC(C)(C)c2ccc(NC(=O)c3ccc(F)cc3C(F)(F)F)cc21

Checking the benzoxaborole ring: B1, O, C(C)(C), then c2 (a6), c (a5), c (a4), c(N…) (a3), c (a2), c21 (a1), which closes the aromatic ring and bonds to B. This matches the drawing.

Checking the right ring: c3 (carbonyl-bearing), c (1031, 546), c (1167, 498), c(F) (1277, 591), c (1252, 733), c3 with CF3 (1115, 781). I wrote "c3ccc(F)cc3C(F)(F)F", which gives c3, c, c, c(F), c, c3(CF3). This matches.

name: Acridine Orange Base
text:
The drawing shows acridine orange: a tricyclic acridine core with a dimethylamino group on each outer ring.

**Core.** The central ring contains one N (bottom) and one CH (top). It is fused to a left benzene ring and a right benzene ring.

**Substituents.** Each outer ring carries an N(CH3)2 group at the position meta to the ring fusion, on the carbon adjacent to the CH at the bottom of that ring.

**Coordinates.** Left ring atoms: (480,517), (345,595), (345,750) bearing NMe2, (480,827), (615,750) fused, (615,595) fused. Central ring: (615,595), (750,517) CH, (885,595), (885,750), N (750,827), (615,750). Right ring: (885,595), (1020,517), (1155,595), (1155,750) bearing NMe2, (1020,827), (885,750).

- Left ring: c1 (NMe2 carbon), c (345,595), c (480,517), c2 (615,595, fused), then the CH (750,517).
- Then c3 (885,595, fused), c (1020,517), c (1155,595), c(NMe2) (1155,750), c (1020,827), c3 (885,750, fused).
- Then n (750,827), c2 (615,750, fused), and c1 (480,827) closes the left ring.

name: Actarit
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is an acetamido group (CH3-C(=O)-NH-) attached to the ring through nitrogen. The other is a CH2-COOH group, so the molecule is 4-acetamidophenylacetic acid.

Reading the structure atom by atom:
- Left side: a methyl carbon, then a carbonyl carbon with a double-bonded O, then NH, then the ring carbon.
- Ring: six aromatic carbons, with the NH-bearing carbon and the CH2-bearing carbon opposite each other.
- Right side: a CH2 attached to the ring, then a carboxylic acid carbon with a C=O and an OH.

There are no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CC(=O)Nc1ccc(CC(=O)O)cc1

name: Acyclovir
text:
This is acyclovir, a guanine with a (2-hydroxyethoxy)methyl group on N9.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Side chain:** HO–CH2–CH2–O–CH2– is attached to N9, the ring nitrogen at the lower left.
- **Imidazole ring:** N9 is bonded to a CH carbon, which has a double bond to N7. N7 is bonded to C5. C5 is double-bonded to C4, and C4 is bonded back to N9.
- **Pyrimidine ring:** C4 is bonded to N3, which is double-bonded to C2. C2 carries the NH2 group and is bonded to N1H. N1H is bonded to C6, which carries the C=O. C6 is bonded to C5.

Writing this as SMILES: OCCOCn1cnc2c1nc(N)[nH]c2=O

Atom-by-atom check against the drawing:

- n1 is N9.
- c is the CH carbon.
- n is N7.
- c2 is C5.
- c1 is C4, closing the five-membered ring back to N9.
- n is N3.
- c(N) is C2 with the amino group.
- [nH] is N1.
- c2=O is C6, closing the six-membered ring back to C5.

Bond orders also fit the drawing. The imidazole CH=N7 is aromatic, C4=C5 is aromatic, and C2=N3 is aromatic. The C=O carbon is aromatic in this SMILES, which RDKit accepts for this kind of ring.

SMILES: OCCOCn1cnc2c1nc(N)[nH]c2=O

name: Adapalene
text:
This is adapalene: 6-[3-(1-adamantyl)-4-methoxyphenyl]-2-naphthoic acid.

Adamantane check: the drawing shows a quaternary carbon at (289,735) bonded to the aryl ring and to three CH2 groups, which gives the adamantane cage. The cage atoms read as follows:

- Quaternary carbon C1 (289,735) bonds to CH2 (175,782), CH2 (404,687) and CH2 (305,612).
- CH2 (175,782) bonds to CH (75,707).
- CH (75,707) bonds to CH2 (92,583) and to CH2 (345,662).
- CH2 (92,583) bonds to CH (207,537).
- CH (207,537) bonds to CH2 (322,489) and to CH2 (305,612).
- CH2 (322,489) bonds to CH (420,565).
- CH (420,565) bonds to CH2 (404,687) and to CH2 (345,662).

The three CH atoms are at (75,707), (207,537) and (420,565). Each is bonded to two CH2 groups, and each CH2 links one CH to the quaternary carbon or to another CH, which is consistent with adamantane.

SMILES for the adamantyl group: C12(CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2) with the aryl attached to the quaternary carbon.

Full SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1C12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2)-c1ccc2cc(C(=O)O)ccc2c1

name: Adefovir Dipivoxil
text:
The drawing shows adefovir dipivoxil.

- **Adenine:** attached through N9 to a CH2CH2O chain, with an NH2 on C6.
- **Linker:** the chain continues O–CH2–P(=O).
- **Phosphonate esters:** the phosphorus carries two O–CH2–O–C(=O)–C(CH3)3 groups (pivaloyloxymethyl).

Writing the SMILES starting from the pivaloyl group:

CC(C)(C)C(=O)OCOP(=O)(COCCn1cnc2c(N)ncnc12)OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C

Checking the adenine ring against the drawing: n1 (N9) – c (C8) – n (N7) – c2 (C5) – c(N) (C6) – n (N1) – c (C2) – n (N3) – c12 (C4), which closes back to N9. In the image, N9 connects to C4, which bears N3. C4 is bonded to C5, which bears N7, and C5 is bonded to C6 carrying NH2. This matches the SMILES.

name: Adenosine Monophosphate
text:
The drawing shows adenosine 5'-monophosphate (AMP). It has three parts:

- **Base:** an adenine unit with an NH2 on the six-membered ring, joined to the sugar through N9.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ribose ring (four carbons and one oxygen). The base and the CH2 group are both on wedge bonds, and the two OH groups are both on hashed bonds. This is the β-D-ribose arrangement.
- **Phosphate:** the 5'-CH2 is bonded to O–P(=O)(OH)2.

I did not derive the stereo descriptors atom by atom. The wedge/hash pattern matches natural β-D-ribose, so I used the recalled PubChem SMILES for natural AMP and checked its connectivity against the drawing.

SMILES: C1=NC(=C2C(=N1)N(C=N2)[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)COP(=O)(O)O)O)O)N

name: Adagrasib
text:
I read the molecule as a tetrahydropyrido[3,4-d]pyrimidine core carrying four groups.

- **Core:** a pyrimidine fused to a tetrahydropyridine. The ring nitrogen of the saturated ring bears an 8-chloronaphthalen-1-yl group. The CH2 next to that nitrogen is attached to the ring-fusion carbon beside a pyrimidine nitrogen, and the CH2CH2 side is attached to the fusion carbon next to the piperazine-bearing carbon.
- **Pyrimidine C2:** an O–CH2 link to the C2 of an N-methylpyrrolidine. The hashed bond on that CH2 and the implicit hydrogen give the S configuration (CIP priorities N > CH2O > ring CH2 > H).
- **Pyrimidine C4:** a piperazine attached through one nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries a 2-fluoroacryloyl group, C(=O)C(F)=CH2. The adjacent ring carbon bears a CH2C≡N group on a hashed bond, which also gives S (priorities N(acyl) > CH2N > CH2CN > H).

I assigned each stereocentre by CIP priorities and then chose the @@ symbol that reproduces S in the SMILES atom order.

SMILES: C=C(F)C(=O)N1CCN(C[C@@H]1CC#N)c1nc(OC[C@@H]2CCCN2C)nc2c1CCN(C2)c1cccc2cccc(Cl)c12

name: Afamelanotide
text:
I read this as the 13-residue peptide Ac-Ser-Tyr-Ser-Nle-Glu-His-D-Phe-Arg-Trp-Gly-Lys-Pro-Val-NH2 (NDP-α-MSH-like, with norleucine at position 4 and D-Phe at position 7). The stereochemistry is partly an assumption. I assigned all residues as L except Phe as D. I did not verify each wedge or hash against the drawing, since hash direction depends on how the chain is oriented.

Region by region, from the N-terminus:
- **Ac-Ser-Tyr-Ser:** an N-acetyl cap, then serine, tyrosine (para-hydroxyphenyl) and serine.
- **Nle:** a norleucine with a plain n-butyl side chain.
- **Glu-His:** glutamic acid with a free carboxylic acid, then histidine with an imidazole.
- **D-Phe:** phenylalanine with a hashed bond to the benzyl group, drawn as the D form.
- **Arg-Trp-Gly:** arginine with a guanidine, tryptophan with an indole, then glycine.
- **Lys-Pro-Val-NH2:** lysine with a free amine, proline in a five-membered ring, and valine ending in a primary amide.

For the proline centre, I checked the written ring-closure order against L-proline and used `[C@H]` for it.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(=N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(N)=O

name: Afatinib
text:
The drawing shows afatinib. Reading it region by region:

- **Side chain:** a dimethylamino group (NMe2) is attached to a CH2, then a trans CH=CH, then a C(=O)NH amide.
- **Core:** the amide NH sits on a quinazoline, at the benzo-ring carbon next to the carbon bearing the ether oxygen.
- **Position 4 of the quinazoline:** an NH links to a 3-chloro-4-fluorophenyl ring.
- **Ether substituent:** the benzo-ring oxygen is attached to the 3-position of a tetrahydrofuran ring, with a wedge bond on the C–O bond.

For the tetrahydrofuran stereocentre, the wedged O points toward the viewer, so the implicit H is at the back. The priorities are O > CH2–O > CH2–C > H. Going from O (down) to CH2O (upper right) to CH2C (left) is counterclockwise, which gives S. The trans double bond is written with `/C=C/`.

SMILES: CN(C)C/C=C/C(=O)Nc1cc2c(Nc3ccc(F)c(Cl)c3)ncnc2cc1O[C@H]1CCOC1

name: Afloqualone
text:
The drawing is a quinazolin-4(3H)-one with these substituents:

- **Position 2:** a CH2F group (the F label is attached through one CH2 to the ring carbon).
- **Position 3:** an N-aryl group, a benzene ring carrying a methyl on the carbon adjacent to the attachment point (2-methylphenyl, o-tolyl).
- **Position 4:** a C=O.
- **Fused benzo ring:** an NH2 group attached to the ring carbon that is para to C8a, the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N1. Following the ring atoms in the drawing: C8a (933,721) connects to C8 (1105,670), then C7 (1236,794), then C6 (1193,968) bearing the NH2, then C5 (1022,1019), then C4a (892,897). So the NH2 sits at position 6.

SMILES, written in the order: FCC1=Nc2ccc(N)cc2C(=O)N1c1ccccc1C

Check on the fused ring: C1(CF)=N–c2 (C8a) c (C8) c (C7) c(N) (C6) c (C5) c2 (C4a), then C(=O) N1. This gives C8a–C8–C7–C6(N)–C5–C4a, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: FCC1=Nc2ccc(N)cc2C(=O)N1c1ccccc1C

name: Aficamten
text:
I read the structure in three parts and then assigned the stereocentre from the hashed bond.

**Fragments**
- **Left:** an ethyl group on C5 of a 1,2,4-oxadiazole (O, N, C, N, C in the ring). Its C3 is bonded to the benzene ring of the indane.
- **Centre:** a 2,3-dihydro-1H-indene (indane). The oxadiazole sits on the benzene ring, and the five-membered ring carries an NH on its benzylic carbon.
- **Right:** an amide, NH–C(=O), linked to C4 of a 1-methylpyrazole.

**Stereochemistry**
The indane C1 (the NH-bearing carbon) has a hashed bond to N, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.

Seen from the viewer's side, the other three substituents go CH2 (down), then aromatic C (upper left), then N (upper right). That is clockwise.

In the SMILES `CC[C@H]3N...`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2, H, aromatic C (ring closure 3), N. Moving H to the front takes one swap, and the order (H, CH2, aromatic C, N) is clockwise, which is `@@`. Undoing the swap flips it back, so the original order is `@`, giving `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CCc1nc(-c2ccc3c(c2)CC[C@H]3NC(=O)c2cnn(C)c2)no1

name: Afegostat
text:
I read the drawing as a piperidine ring: N–CH2–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(CH2OH)–CH2 back to N. It has three stereocentres, each drawn with a wedge or hash:

- The ring carbon bearing the hashed CH2OH.
- The ring carbon bearing the wedged OH.
- The ring carbon bearing the hashed OH.

I wrote the SMILES starting from the CH2OH carbon and assigned each @/@@ from the wedge or hash direction and the 2D positions of the neighbours. I did not independently re-check the final string against the image.

SMILES: OC[C@H]1CNC[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Agomelatine
text:
This is agomelatine: an N-acetyl group on an ethylamine chain attached to a naphthalene ring that carries a methoxy group.

**Chain:** CH3–C(=O)–NH–CH2–CH2– is attached to the ring carbon at about (858, 608).

**Ring system:** The right-hand ring has vertices (1183, 516), (1372, 564), (1424, 751), (1289, 890), (1100, 844) and (1047, 656). The left-hand ring has vertices (858, 608), (806, 421), (941, 282), (1130, 329), (1183, 516) and (1047, 656). The two rings share the bond between (1183, 516) and (1047, 656).

**Substituents:** The methoxy group is on (1289, 890). The ethyl chain is on (858, 608), which is adjacent to the fusion carbon (1047, 656).

**SMILES:** Start with CC(=O)NCCc1cccc2ccc(OC)cc12.
- c1 is (858, 608).
- The next three c atoms are (806, 421), (941, 282) and (1130, 329).
- c2 is the fusion carbon (1183, 516).
- The next two c atoms are (1372, 564) and (1424, 751).
- c(OC) is (1289, 890).
- The following c is (1100, 844).
- The last c12 is the fusion carbon (1047, 656), which closes both rings.

This matches the drawing: the methoxy carbon is two atoms from the fusion carbon (1047, 656), via (1100, 844), and the substituents sit on a 1,7-pattern, as in agomelatine.

SMILES: CC(=O)NCCc1cccc2ccc(OC)cc12

name: Albendazole
text:
The drawing shows albendazole: a benzimidazole core carrying a methyl carbamate at C2 and a propylthio group on the benzene ring.

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Carbamate:** a methyl group is attached to O, which connects to C(=O), which connects to NH. This gives COC(=O)N.
- **Imidazole ring:** the NH links to C2, which is double-bonded to N (no H, drawn at upper left) and single-bonded to NH (drawn at lower right). The N= connects to the ring-fusion carbon at upper right, and the NH connects to the other fusion carbon.
- **Benzene ring:** it has six carbons, and the one bearing S sits at the far right of the ring.
- **Propylthio chain:** S is followed by three carbons, CCC.

Tracing the SMILES from the carbamate: COC(=O)NC1=Nc2ccc(SCCC)cc2N1.

Checking the ring placement: the upper fusion carbon (bonded to N=) leads up to the top-left CH, then the top-right CH, then the C–S carbon, then the bottom CH, then the lower fusion carbon (bonded to NH). In the SMILES, c2 is the fusion carbon bonded to N=, followed by c, c, c(S), c, and then c2 bonded to NH. The ring has six atoms: c2, c, c, c(S), c, c2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COC(=O)NC1=Nc2ccc(SCCC)cc2N1

name: Alcaftadine
text:
The drawing is an azatadine/loratadine-like tricycle, specifically the imidazo[2,1-b][3]benzazepine of the type found in the compound related to Bilastine/Rupatadine. I read it region by region.

**Imidazole ring.** The atoms are N (top left, bonded to the CH2 chain), C (bonded to the exocyclic C=C carbon), N (=N, lower right), CH, and C bearing the CHO. The ring bonds are C(CHO)=CH, CH–N=, N=C, and C–N(ring). The N at the upper left is bonded to CH2, to C(CHO) and to the C= carbon.

**Seven-membered ring.** It contains N, CH2, CH2, the aromatic C, the aromatic C, the C(=piperidinylidene) carbon, and the imidazole C (C2).

**Piperidine ring.** The exocyclic double bond runs from the ring-junction carbon to the piperidine C4, and the nitrogen carries a methyl group.

**SMILES.** Starting from the aldehyde:
O=CC1=CN=C2N1CCc1ccccc1C2=C1CCN(C)CC1

Check on ring closures:
- C1 is C(CHO); =C is CH; N= is the imine N; C2 is the imidazole carbon bonded to N.
- N1 is the ring N closing to C1; CC are the two CH2 groups; c1ccccc1 is the benzene ring, with the first aromatic carbon attached to the CH2 and the last aromatic carbon attached to C2.
- C2=C1CCN(C)CC1 closes the seven-membered ring and the piperidine.

The seven-membered ring is N, CH2, CH2, c, c, C(=), C2, which is 7 atoms and matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=CC1=CN=C2N1CCc1ccccc1C2=C1CCN(C)CC1

name: Albaconazole
text:
The drawing matches albaconazole, a quinazolinone antifungal. I read it region by region:

- **Quinazolin-4-one core:** a benzene ring fused to a pyrimidinone. The ring carries Cl on the benzo carbon para to the carbonyl-bearing ring fusion carbon. It has a C=O, and the ring N–CH=N sits at the bottom, with the ring nitrogen bonded to the side chain.
- **Side chain on that ring N:** a CH carrying a hashed methyl, then a quaternary carbon bearing a hashed OH, a 2,4-difluorophenyl ring, and a CH2 linked to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole.
- **Stereochemistry:** I worked out both centres from the hashed bonds in the drawing. The methyl-bearing CH comes out as `C[C@H]` when written with the quaternary carbon before N. The quaternary carbon comes out as `[C@]` when its substituents are written in the order CH2, aryl, OH.

I checked the atom connectivity and both stereocentres against the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H]([C@](Cn1cncn1)(c1ccc(F)cc1F)O)n1cnc2cc(Cl)ccc2c1=O

name: Alarelin
text:
I read this as a linear decapeptide with a pyroglutamyl N-terminus and an ethylamide C-terminus: pGlu-His-Trp-Ser-Tyr-D-Ala-Leu-Arg-Pro-NHEt.

- **Residue sequence:** pyroglutamic acid lactam, histidine (imidazole with the NH next to the attachment carbon), tryptophan (indole), serine (CH2OH), tyrosine (para-hydroxyphenyl), alanine, leucine (isobutyl), arginine (guanidine side chain), and proline. The C-terminal proline carries a C(=O)NHCH2CH3 group.
- **Stereochemistry:**
  - The pyroglutamic acid wedge corresponds to the L configuration.
  - The alanine methyl is drawn hashed. Working through the CIP priorities (N > C(=O) > CH3), I get R at that carbon, so it is D-alanine.
  - I took the remaining residues as L-amino acids and did not check each wedge against the drawing, so these are an assumption based on the peptide identity.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1[nH]cnc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC

name: Alclometasone Dipropionate
text:
The structure is a pregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione steroid. I identified these features from the drawing:

- Ring A is a cross-conjugated 1,4-dien-3-one, with the ketone at the far right.
- There is a chlorine on C7 (wedge bond) and an OH on C11 (hashed bond).
- There are methyl groups at C10 and C13, and a methyl at C16.
- C17 carries a propionate ester (O–C(=O)CH2CH3) and the C20 ketone side chain.
- The side chain ends in C21 bearing a second propionate ester.

This matches alclometasone dipropionate. The molecule is drawn mirrored left-to-right compared with the usual steroid orientation, so the wedges and hashes look inverted. Read that way, they correspond to 7α-Cl, 11β-OH, 16α-methyl and the natural steroid ring fusion. I took the stereochemical SMILES from that known structure rather than assigning each centre independently from the drawing.

SMILES: CCC(=O)OCC(=O)[C@@]1([C@@H](C[C@@H]2[C@@]1(C[C@@H]([C@H]3[C@H]2[C@H](CC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]34C)Cl)O)C)C)OC(=O)CC

name: Aldosterone
text:
I read the drawing as aldosterone, the 18-aldehyde (open-chain) form. I did not derive the stereo descriptors atom by atom, so the stereochemistry comes from my recall of the known aldosterone SMILES.

- **Ring A:** an enone, with C3 as a ketone conjugated to the C4=C5 double bond.
- **C10:** a wedged methyl group.
- **C11:** a wedged hydroxyl group.
- **C13:** a wedged aldehyde (CHO) group.
- **Ring D:** a five-membered ring carrying the 2-hydroxyacetyl side chain, C(=O)CH2OH, as a wedged bond at C17.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** wedged at C8, hashed at C9 and hashed at C14.

These features match natural aldosterone.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2[C@H](C[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@H]4C(=O)CO)C=O)O

name: A47934
text:
I read the drawing as a sulfated, chlorinated, cross-linked heptapeptide (a vancomycin-type glycopeptide aglycone) and wrote it residue by residue along the peptide backbone.

**Backbone and residues (N- to C-terminus)**
1. Residue 1 is an amino-aryl-glycine (free NH2, hashed bond). Its ring carries an OSO3H group and an aryl ether to residue 3's ring.
2. Residue 2 is a CH(CH2-aryl) unit. Its ring has a Cl ortho to the ether oxygen that links to residue 4's ring.
3. Residue 3 is an aryl-glycine on a 3,5-dioxygenated ring: one oxygen is the ether to ring 1 and the other is a free OH.
4. Residue 4 is an aryl-glycine whose ring has two ether oxygens and a central free OH. One ether goes to ring 2 and the other to ring 6.
5. Residue 5 is an aryl-glycine on a ring with Cl and OH. This ring is joined by a biaryl bond to the ring of residue 7.
6. Residue 6 is a β-hydroxy-tyrosine type unit, CH(NH)–CH(OH)–aryl. Its ring carries Cl ortho to the ether oxygen that links to residue 4's ring.
7. Residue 7 is an aryl-glycine with a free COOH (hashed bond). Its dihydroxy ring is the biaryl partner of residue 5's ring.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash. These are a1 (residue 1) through a7 (residue 7), plus b6, the β-OH carbon of residue 6. Where a wedge or hash points to a drawn H, I used that H as the reference. The a4 hash overlaps the NH label, so I read it as pointing to its H, which is the least certain call.

I wrote the macrocycle links as ring-closure labels and checked that each opening label is matched by one closing label.

SMILES: N[C@H](c1ccc(OS(=O)(=O)O)c(c1)O

name: Alectinib
text:
This is alectinib. I read it region by region.

- **Ethyl group:** CH2CH3 sits on the upper-left aromatic carbon.
- **Left benzene ring:** it carries the ethyl group and, on the adjacent carbon, the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** the ring nitrogen is attached to the benzene, and the carbon at position 4 bears the morpholine nitrogen.
- **Morpholine:** a standard six-membered ring with one N and one O.
- **Central ring:** the left benzene ring is fused to a six-membered ring containing a C=O and a C(CH3)2 group.
- **Indole portion:** the central ring is fused to an indole-type ring (NH adjacent to the CMe2 carbon). The right benzene ring carries the C≡N group.

SMILES, written in order:
- Ethyl-bearing carbon: CCc1cc2c(cc1N1CCC(CC1)N1CCOCC1)C(C)(C)c1[nH]c3cc(C#N)ccc3c1C2=O
- Left ring: c1 (ethyl-bearing), then cH, then c2 (bonded to C=O), then c (bonded to CMe2), then cH, then c1 (bearing the piperidine N).
- Central ring: C(C)(C) is bonded to c1[nH]. The next atom is c3 (indole C7a), then cH, then c(C#N), then cH, then cH, then c3 (C3a), and finally c1 (indole C3) bonded to C2=O.

Checking the nitrile position against the drawing: the nitrile carbon is attached to the ring atom that is one removed from the carbon bonded to the N-bearing carbon (C7a). In the drawing, C7a connects to a CH, which connects to C(CN). So C7a–CH–C(CN) is correct, and the ring then continues C(CN)–CH–CH–C3a, which matches my SMILES.

SMILES: CCc1cc2c(cc1N1CCC(CC1)N1CCOCC1)C(C)(C)c1[nH]c3cc(C#N)ccc3c1C2=O

name: Aculeacin A
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic hexapeptide lipopeptide of the echinocandin type, with a palmitoyl (C16 acyl) chain on the 4,5-dihydroxyornithine amine. The SMILES below was assembled residue by residue around the ring.

- **Acyl chain:** the zigzag chain has 16 carbons counting the carbonyl, so it is a palmitoyl group.
- **Dihydroxyornithine:** an NH-acylated alpha carbon, then CH2 (drawn as "C"), CH(OH), and a CH(OH) that is bonded to the next amide NH.
- **Methylproline unit:** a pyrrolidine with a hydroxyl and a methyl, both on wedges.
- **Dihydroxy-homotyrosine unit:** CH(OH)–CH(OH)–C6H4–OH, with the phenol para-substituted.
- **Hydroxy-asparagine-type unit:** CH(OH)–CH2–C(=O)NH2.
- **Hydroxyproline unit:** a pyrrolidine with a wedged OH.
- **Threonine unit:** CH(CH3)OH on the alpha carbon.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond and the angular order of its neighbours as drawn. The parity of the chirality tags was worked out by hand and not checked with software, so some tags could be wrong.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)N[C@H]1C[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)NC(=O)[C@@H]2[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)CN2C(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)[C@@H](O)c3ccc(O)cc3)NC(=O)[C@@H]4C[C@@H](O)CN4C(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC1=O

name: Alendronic Acid
text:
The image shows alendronic acid (4-amino-1-hydroxybutane-1,1-diyl bisphosphonic acid).

Reading the structure:
- A central carbon carries an OH group and two phosphonic acid groups, each written P(=O)(O)O.
- A three-carbon chain runs from the central carbon to an NH2 group: the central carbon bonds to CH2, then CH2, then CH2, then NH2.

The central carbon is bonded to the OH, both P atoms and the first CH2, so it has four substituents. Two of them are identical phosphonates, so it is not a stereocentre.

SMILES: NCCCC(O)(P(=O)(O)O)P(=O)(O)O

name: Allantoin
text:
The drawing is allantoin: a five-membered hydantoin ring carrying a urea group (–NH–C(=O)–NH2) on one ring carbon.

Reading the structure atom by atom:

- **Ring atoms:** a CH carbon at the bottom left of the ring, an NH at the top, a C(=O) at the upper right, an NH at the right, and a C(=O) at the bottom, which closes back to the CH carbon.
- **Urea side chain:** the CH carbon bonds to an NH, which bonds to a C(=O) that ends in NH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

name: Allicin
text:
The drawing shows two allyl groups joined through a sulfur–sulfur bond, with one of the sulfurs carrying a double-bonded oxygen. This is allicin, a thiosulfinate.

Reading the chain from left to right:
- The left allyl group is CH2=CH–CH2, drawn as a terminal double bond followed by a single bond to a CH2.
- That CH2 bonds to the first sulfur (S).
- The first sulfur bonds to the second sulfur, which carries the double-bonded oxygen (S=O).
- The second sulfur bonds to the right allyl group, CH2–CH=CH2.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: C=CCSS(=O)CC=C

name: Alflutinib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Acrylamide:** CH2=CH–C(=O)–NH–, attached to the central pyridine.
- **Central pyridine:** the ring atoms are C(NHC(=O)C=C), C(N(C)CCN(C)C), N, C(OCH2CF3), C(NH-pyrimidine) and CH.
  - The carbon bearing the acrylamide NH is bonded to the carbon bearing N(Me)CH2CH2NMe2.
  - That carbon is bonded to the ring N, which is bonded to the carbon bearing OCH2CF3.
  - That carbon is bonded to the carbon bearing NH-pyrimidine, which is bonded to the CH that closes the ring back to the acrylamide-bearing carbon.
- **Pyrimidine:** C2 carries the NH, N3 sits at the bottom, C4 and C5 are CH, and C6 carries the indole. In the drawing, the C bearing the indole is bonded to N (top), which is bonded to C2 (NH), then to N (bottom), then CH, CH, and back to the substituted carbon.
- **Indole:** 1-methylindol-3-yl, attached to the pyrimidine through C3.

SMILES for the pyridine: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OCC(F)(F)F)nc1N(C)CCN(C)C

Check of the pyridine ring: c1 (NHacryl), c (CH), c(NH-pyr), c(OCH2CF3), n, c1 (N(Me)...). This is six atoms and matches the drawing.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OCC(F)(F)F)nc1N(C)CCN(C)C

name: Alfentanil
text:
I read the drawing region by region.

**Tetrazolinone ring (left).** The ring has an ethyl group on N1, then N=N, then N bearing the CH2CH2 chain, then a C=O carbon that closes back to N1. The connectivity is N1(Et)–N=N–N(CH2CH2…)–C(=O)–N1, which is 1-ethyl-4-substituted-tetrazol-5-one. The SMILES fragment is CCn1nnn(CC...)c1=O.

**Linker and piperidine.** The chain runs from the ring nitrogen through CH2CH2 to the piperidine nitrogen. The piperidine's 4-position carbon carries two substituents: CH2OCH3 and N(Ph)C(=O)CH2CH3.

**Full SMILES.** In the drawing the ring bonds are N1–N=N, with N=N drawn as a double bond. N–N=N–N(R)–C(=O)–N1(Et) is valid, so the SMILES is:

CCN1N=NN(CCN2CCC(COC)(CC2)N(C(=O)CC)c2ccccc2)C1=O

**Check.** The ring atoms are N1, N, N, N and C(=O), which makes five. The valences are consistent: N1 is bonded to Et, N and C; the second N is double-bonded to the third; the fourth N is bonded to N, CH2 and C. This is correct.

SMILES: CCN1N=NN(CCN2CCC(COC)(CC2)N(C(=O)CC)c2ccccc2)C1=O

name: Alminoprofen
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is a CH(CH3)COOH group (a propanoic acid attached at the alpha carbon). The other is an NH–CH2–C(CH3)=CH2 group (a 2-methylallylamino group).

The alpha carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CC(C(=O)O)c1ccc(NCC(C)=C)cc1

name: Allopurinol
text:
Reading the drawing atom by atom, I get a bicyclic system: a six-membered ring fused to a five-membered ring.

**Six-membered ring** (going around from the top):
- N at the top, double-bonded to a CH on its left.
- That CH is bonded to HN on the left.
- HN is bonded to C(=O) at the bottom left.
- C(=O) is bonded to fusion carbon C3a.
- C3a is double-bonded to fusion carbon C7a.
- C7a is bonded back to the top N.

**Five-membered ring:**
- C7a is bonded to NH.
- NH is bonded to N.
- N is double-bonded to a CH.
- That CH is bonded to C3a.

**SMILES:**
- Starting at the C=O carbon: O=C1NC=NC2=C1C=NN2
- Ring 1 runs C1, N, C, =N, C2, then C1 closes through the "=C1" atom (C3a).
- C3a is written as "=C1", so C2=C1 is the C7a=C3a double bond.
- Next comes C=N (the CH double-bonded to N), then N2 (the NH), which closes to C7a.

**Check on the five-membered ring:** C7a, C3a, CH, N and NH are five atoms. The bonds are C7a=C3a, C3a–CH, CH=N, N–NH and NH–C7a, which matches the drawing.

**Hydrogens:** the top N is double-bonded to CH, so it has no H. The six-membered ring N–H is the HN on the left, written as N in the SMILES (valence 3: C(=O), CH, H). That works.

SMILES: O=C1NC=NC2=C1C=NN2

name: Almitrine
text:
The drawing shows a 1,3,5-triazine ring with three substituents:

- Two of the ring carbons each carry an NH–CH2–CH=CH2 (allylamino) group.
- The third ring carbon is bonded to a piperazine nitrogen.
- The other piperazine nitrogen is bonded to a CH that carries two 4-fluorophenyl groups (a bis(4-fluorophenyl)methyl group).

Writing the SMILES from this: C=CCNc1nc(NCC=C)nc(n1)N1CCN(CC1)C(c1ccc(F)cc1)c1ccc(F)cc1

Atom-by-atom check against the drawing:

- The triazine ring has three N and three C, alternating.
- Both allyl chains are present, each attached through NH.
- The piperazine has four CH2 groups and two N atoms.
- The central CH bears two aryl rings, each with F para to the attachment point.

The central CH is not drawn as a stereocentre, and it is not one by connectivity either, since its two aryl groups are identical.

SMILES: C=CCNc1nc(NCC=C)nc(n1)N1CCN(CC1)C(c1ccc(F)cc1)c1ccc(F)cc1

name: Almotriptan Malate
text:
The image shows two components: almotriptan and malic acid, drawn as a salt or co-crystal.

**Malic acid:** O=C(O)C(O)CC(=O)O. The central carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereochemistry.

**Almotriptan:**
- Indole core, with the NH at the top left.
- C3 carries a CH2CH2N(CH3)2 chain.
- C5 carries a CH2–SO2–N(pyrrolidine) group.

Indole SMILES, written from the NH: c1(CCN(C)C)c[nH]c2ccc(CS(=O)(=O)N3CCCC3)cc12

Checking the ring positions against the drawing:
- The NH is bonded to the fused carbon C7a, which is bonded to the top CH (C7).
- C7 is followed by the next CH (C6), then the substituted carbon (C5).
- C5 is followed by the CH (C4), then C3a.
- C3a is bonded to C3, which carries the chain, and C3a is also bonded to C7a.

This is consistent with the SMILES above.

SMILES: O=C(O)C(O)CC(=O)O.CN(C)CCc1c[nH]c2ccc(CS(=O)(=O)N3CCCC3)cc12

name: Alogliptin
text:
This structure is alogliptin, a 6-(3-aminopiperidin-1-yl)-uracil bearing an N-methyl and an N-(2-cyanobenzyl) group. I read it region by region:

- **Pyrimidinedione ring:** N1 carries the methyl (the line at the bottom right) and sits between two carbonyl carbons (the two C=O groups). The ring also contains a C=C. Its other nitrogen carries the benzyl CH2. The ring carbon next to that nitrogen carries the piperidine.
- **Benzyl group:** The CH2 leads to a benzene ring with a nitrile (C≡N) on the adjacent (ortho) carbon.
- **Piperidine ring:** It is attached through its nitrogen to the pyrimidinedione. The ring carbon at position 3 bears an NH2 drawn with a hashed bond.

For the stereocentre at piperidine C3, the hashed NH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are NH2, then C2 (the CH2 bonded to N), then C4, then H. On the screen the sequence NH2 → C2 → C4 runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is (R).

I wrote the SMILES with `[C@@H]` for the order C4, H, NH2, C2 and checked that this gives R.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)C=C(N2CCC[C@@H](N)C2)N(Cc2ccccc2C#N)C1=O

name: Alpelisib
text:
This structure is alpelisib, (2S)-N1-[4-methyl-5-[2-(1,1,1-trifluoro-2-methylpropan-2-yl)pyridin-4-yl]thiazol-2-yl]pyrrolidine-1,2-dicarboxamide. I read it region by region:

- **Pyrrolidine:** a five-membered ring with one N. The ring carbon next to N carries a primary amide (H2N–C=O) on a wedge bond.
- **Urea link:** the ring N is acylated by a C=O that connects through an NH to the thiazole.
- **Thiazole:** the NH-bearing carbon is C2, between S and N. The ring carbon beside that N carries a methyl, and the carbon beside S is bonded to the pyridine.
- **Pyridine:** it is attached to the thiazole at C4. At C2, next to the ring N, it carries a C(CH3)2CF3 group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedge is the only stereo marker. With H pointing back, the substituents run N → C(=O)NH2 → CH2 counterclockwise, so the centre is S. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` written after the amide carbon encodes S.

SMILES: NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)Nc1nc(C)c(s1)-c1ccnc(c1)C(C)(C)C(F)(F)F

name: Aldrin
text:
I read the drawing as a chlorinated bis-methano-bridged naphthalene core (the aldrin/isodrin skeleton), and the SMILES below describes it atom for atom.

**Skeleton**
- The left half is a norbornene unit. A C=C (the left vertical bond) sits between two bridgehead carbons that each carry a wedged H. A CH2 bridges those two bridgeheads.
- The two central ring-fusion carbons are joined by a vertical bond, and each carries a hashed H.
- The right half is a second bicyclic unit. Its C=C bears one Cl on each carbon.
- The right bridge carbon carries two Cl.
- The two right bridgeheads each carry a hashed Cl.

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned `@`/`@@` from the wedge and hash bonds on the six stereocentres: the two H-bearing bridgeheads on the left, the two H-bearing fusion carbons, and the two Cl-bearing bridgeheads on the right.
- Each assignment came from the 2D positions of the neighbours together with whether the H or Cl is drawn toward or away from the viewer.
- I worked these out by hand and did not run them through a toolkit.

SMILES: C1=C[C@@H]2C[C@H]1[C@@H]3[C@H]2[C@]4(Cl)C(Cl)=C(Cl)[C@@]3(Cl)C4(Cl)Cl

name: alpha-Tocopherol
text:
This is α-tocopherol (vitamin E). I read it as a 6-hydroxy-chromane whose aromatic ring carries three methyls, with a C2 quaternary stereocentre (methyl plus a saturated 16-carbon side chain). The side chain has two further methyl-bearing stereocentres and ends in an isopropyl group.

I worked out the CIP configuration only at C2. The methyl there is drawn on a wedge, and the priorities are O > ring CH2 > chain CH2 > CH3. This gives R. I did not derive the two side-chain centres (the hashed and wedged methyls) separately. I assumed they match natural RRR-α-tocopherol and wrote the SMILES from memory of the PubChem entry.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=C2CC[C@@](OC2=C1C)(C)CCC[C@H](C)CCC[C@H](C)CCCC(C)C)C)O

name: Alpha-Cyclodextrin
text:
The drawing shows a macrocycle of six glucopyranose rings joined through ring oxygens, so it is α-cyclodextrin. I identified the six rings by their ring-oxygen labels, which sit at about (718,292), (1092,558), (1182,930), (790,1200), (357,998) and (317,522). Each unit carries a CH2OH group and two free OH groups.

I did not derive the wedge and hash stereochemistry atom by atom. The stereodescriptors come from the known isomeric SMILES for α-cyclodextrin, which I recalled from memory rather than checking against the drawing. I did confirm that the ring closures, branches and the six CH2OH groups are consistent with the drawn connectivity.

SMILES: C([C@@H]1[C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O1)O[C@@H]3[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]3O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]4O)O)O[C@@H]5[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]5O)O)O[C@@H]6[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]6O)O)O[C@@H]7[C@H](O[C@H](O2)[C@@H]([C@H]7O)O)CO)CO)CO)CO)CO)O)O)O

name: Alphaxalone
text:
I read this as a pregnane steroid skeleton: 3-hydroxy-pregnane-11,20-dione, which matches alfaxalone (3α-hydroxy-5α-pregnane-11,20-dione).

**Skeleton and substituents**
- The acetyl group (CH3–C=O) on the five-membered ring is attached at C17.
- There is a ketone at C11 in the ring-C position.
- There is a hydroxyl on C3 of ring A, drawn with a hashed bond.
- There are two angular methyl groups at C13 and C10, both drawn as wedges.

**Stereochemistry as drawn**
- The C17 acetyl group, the C13 methyl (C18) and the C10 methyl (C19) are wedged, so they are β.
- H at C8 is wedged, so it is β.
- H at C5, C9 and C14 are hashed, so they are α.
- The C3 OH is hashed, so it is α.

I did not derive every @/@@ symbol from the drawing's coordinates. I took the SMILES from alfaxalone's known configuration, matched it to the wedge pattern above, and used the allopregnanolone pattern for the C3 centre, since both have 3α-OH.

SMILES: CC(=O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC(=O)[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)C

name: Alprenolol
text:
The drawing shows alprenolol: an isopropylamine linked through a 2-hydroxypropyl chain and an ether oxygen to a benzene ring that carries an ortho allyl group.

- **Left side:** an isopropyl group, CH(CH3)2, is bonded to NH.
- **Chain:** NH connects to CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2, then the ether O.
- **Ring:** the ether O is attached to a benzene carbon. The adjacent ring carbon carries an allyl group, CH2-CH=CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is included.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccccc1CC=C

name: Alpha-Galactosylceramide
text:
I read this as an α-galactosyl ceramide of the KRN7000 type. The stereochemistry is taken from the known compound, not derived from the wedges, so it is the least certain part.

- **Sugar:** a pyranose ring with a CH2OH group, three ring OH groups and an O-glycosidic link at the anomeric carbon. The ring OH groups match galactose and the linkage is α.
- **Sphingoid base:** the glycosidic oxygen sits on a CH2 (C1). C2 carries the amide nitrogen. C3 and C4 each carry an OH, which gives a phytosphingosine core. From the picture I counted a tail of 14 further CH2/CH3 carbons after C4, which makes the base C18.
- **Acyl group:** the amide carbonyl is followed by a long straight chain. Counting zigzag vertices gave 25 carbons beyond the carbonyl carbon, so the acyl group is C26 (cerotoyl).

I counted the chain lengths from the zigzag spacing and bond length in the image, which is approximate.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)N[C@@H](CO[C@@H]1[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H]([C@H](O1)CO)O)O)O)[C@@H]([C@@H](CCCCCCCCCCCCCC)O)O

name: Alprazolam
text:
This structure matches alprazolam: a triazolobenzodiazepine with a methyl on the triazole, a chlorine on the benzo ring, and a phenyl group on the diazepine ring.

**Triazole ring:** The methyl-bearing carbon (C) is bonded to N (the bridgehead N) and double-bonded to N (the left N). That N connects to the lower N, which is double-bonded to the carbon at the ring fusion. This carbon is also bonded to the bridgehead N. The ring is therefore C(C)=NN=C–N.

**Diazepine ring:** The bridgehead N bonds to an aromatic carbon. The fusion carbon at the ring fusion connects through CH2 to N, which is double-bonded to C(Ph). C(Ph) attaches to the other aromatic fusion carbon.

**Benzo ring:** The carbon attached to the bridgehead N is aromatic, followed by CH, CH, then C(Cl), CH, and the fusion carbon bonded to C(Ph).

SMILES: Cc1nnc2CN=C(c3ccccc3)c3cc(Cl)ccc3-n12

SMILES: Cc1nnc2CN=C(c3ccccc3)c3cc(Cl)ccc3-n12

name: Aluminum Clofibrate
text:
The drawing shows several separate components: two identical clofibrate-type carboxylate anions, a hydroxide anion, and an Al³⁺ cation (aluminium clofibrate-like salt).

Each carboxylate anion is 2-(4-chlorophenoxy)-2-methylpropanoate: the carboxylate carbon carries a C=O and an O⁻, and is bonded to a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups and an ether oxygen. That oxygen is attached to a benzene ring with Cl at the para position.

The SMILES for one anion is CC(C)(Oc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)[O-].

The charges balance: Al³⁺ (+3) against two carboxylates (−2) and one hydroxide (−1).

SMILES: CC(C)(Oc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)[O-].CC(C)(Oc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)[O-].[OH-].[Al+3]

name: Altiratinib
text:
I read the structure region by region, from left to right.

- **Left end:** a cyclopropyl group attached to a C(=O) that is bonded to NH. This is a cyclopropanecarboxamide.
- **Pyridine:** the NH is on C2 of the pyridine ring, and the ring nitrogen is adjacent to that carbon. The ring atoms run C2, then C3 (CH), then C4 (bearing O), then C5 (CH), C6 (CH), and N1.
- **Central benzene:** the pyridine C4 is linked through an ether O to the central benzene. The benzene carries two fluorines and an NH.
  - Ring atoms: C1 (O), C2 (F, lower left), C3 (CH), C4 (NH), C5 (F, upper right), C6 (CH).
  - Going around from C(O) at the top left: C(O) is bonded to C(F) at the lower left and to CH at the top. The top CH is bonded to C(F) at the upper right. That C(F) is bonded to C(NH) on the right, then CH at the bottom, then back to C(F) at the lower left.
  - So the ring is c1(O)cc(F)c(N)cc1F, with O and N para to each other, and F ortho to each.
- **Right side:** the NH is bonded to C(=O), which is bonded to a cyclopropane quaternary carbon. That carbon also carries a second C(=O)NH-aryl group, where the aryl is 4-fluorophenyl.

Assembled SMILES:

O=C(C1CC1)Nc1cc(Oc2cc(F)c(NC(=O)C3(CC3)C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2F)ccn1

Check of the central ring: c2 (O attached), then c (CH), then c(F), then c(N...), then c (CH), then c2F. The ring closure atom bears F and is adjacent to the O-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(C1CC1)Nc1cc(Oc2cc(F)c(NC(=O)C3(CC3)C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2F)ccn1

name: Aluminum Hydroxide
text:
The image shows an aluminium cation labelled Al³⁺ and three hydroxide anions, so this is aluminium hydroxide drawn as separate ions.

- Two hydroxides are labelled "HO⁻", one at the top left and one at the right.
- The third is split across two labels, with "H⁻" stacked directly above "O". I read these as one hydroxide, with the charge written on the H. This also balances the charge: three OH⁻ against one Al³⁺.

SMILES: [OH-].[OH-].[OH-].[Al+3]

name: Alverine
text:
The drawing shows a tertiary amine: a central N carrying three substituents.

- One substituent is an ethyl group (CH2CH3), drawn as the two-carbon chain below the N.
- The other two are identical 3-phenylpropyl chains. Each runs N–CH2–CH2–CH2 and ends on a benzene ring.

Counting the left chain: from N up to the carbon at (695,783), then (553,767), then (497,637), which is attached to the ring carbon at (355,622). That is three CH2 carbons before the phenyl ring.

Counting the right chain: from N to (891,929), then (975,815), then (1116,830), which is attached to the ring carbon at (1200,716). That is also three CH2 carbons before the phenyl ring.

The molecule is N-ethyl-3-phenyl-N-(3-phenylpropyl)propan-1-amine. No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: CCN(CCCc1ccccc1)CCCc1ccccc1

name: Alvelestat
text:
The drawing shows a 2-pyridone core with these substituents:

- **N1:** attached to a 3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.
- **C2:** carbonyl (C=O).
- **C3:** carboxamide, C(=O)NH-CH2-pyridyl.
- **C4:** CH.
- **C5:** attached to a 1-methylpyrazol-5-yl group.
- **C6:** methyl.

**Pyrazole:** N(Me) is bonded to N=CH-CH=C, and the ring carbon attached to the pyridone is next to the NMe. This gives c1(ccnn1C), where the ring carbon bonded to the pyridone is adjacent to N-Me.

**Pyridine side chain:** the CH2 is attached to a pyridine C2. The ring runs C2, N, CH, C(SO2Me), CH, CH. The N is adjacent to C2. From N the path goes to CH, then to the C bearing SO2Me, so the sulfone sits at position 5 (para to C2).

**Aryl group:** the CF3 is meta to the N attachment.

SMILES for the core: O=C1N(Ar)C(C)=C(pyrazolyl)C=C1C(=O)NCc1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cn1

Full SMILES: Cn1nccc1C1=CC(C(=O)NCc2ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cn2)=C(O)... — rather than the hydroxy form, I write the pyridone directly:

Cn1nccc1C1=C(C)N(c2cccc(C(F)(F)F)c2)C(=O)C(C(=O)NCc2ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cn2)=C1

SMILES: Cn1nccc1C1=C(C)N(c2cccc(C(F)(F)F)c2)C(=O)C(C(=O)NCc2ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cn2)=C1

name: Amantadine
text:
The drawing is 1-aminoadamantane (amantadine): an adamantane cage with an NH2 group on one bridgehead carbon.

Reading the atoms from the image, with approximate coordinates:
- C1 (535,757) bears the NH2 and bonds to C2, C3 and C4.
- C2 (680,497) bonds to C1 and C5.
- C3 (790,604) bonds to C1 and C6.
- C4 (687,1012) bonds to C1 and C7.
- C5 (975,493) bonds to C2, C8 and C9.
- C6 (1425,742) bonds to C3, C9 and C10.
- C7 (985,1005) bonds to C4, C8 and C10.
- C8 (830,752) bonds to C5 and C7.
- C9 (1272,487) bonds to C5 and C6.
- C10 (1280,1001) bonds to C6 and C7.

That gives 10 carbons: 4 bridgehead CH (C1, C5, C6, C7) and 6 CH2 (C2, C3, C4, C8, C9, C10), with N attached to C1.

SMILES: NC12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2 would be the usual form, so I checked that it matches this connectivity. In that string, C1 is the quaternary carbon, C3 is a bridgehead and the next bridgehead closes ring 2, which is consistent with the adamantane cage.

The standard amantadine SMILES is NC12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2.

SMILES: NC12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2

name: Ambenonium Chloride
text:
This is ambenonium chloride, drawn as a dication with two chloride counterions.

Reading the structure region by region:
- Each end has a 2-chlorobenzyl group (a benzene ring with Cl ortho to the CH2) attached to a quaternary N+.
- Each N+ also carries two ethyl groups and a CH2CH2 linker to an amide NH.
- The centre is an oxalamide, NH–C(=O)–C(=O)–NH.
- Two Cl⁻ ions are shown separately.

SMILES: CC[N+](CC)(CCNC(=O)C(=O)NCC[N+](CC)(CC)Cc1ccccc1Cl)Cc1ccccc1Cl.[Cl-].[Cl-]

name: Alpha-Amanitin
text:
