This is my reading of the drawing, written as a SMILES. It is a bicyclic amatoxin-type peptide (it looks like α-amanitin). I traced the ring from the Ile residue around the macrocycle and assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

**Residues and connectivity**
- Ile has a sec-butyl side chain, with its NH acylated by a Gly.
- That Gly is followed by Cys.
- The Cys CH2 carries an S(=O) that bonds to C2 of the indole.
- The indole is a 6-hydroxy-tryptophan, and its C3 carries the CH2 of the Trp side chain.
- Trp is followed by the dihydroxy-isoleucine, which has CH(CH3)–CH(OH)–CH2OH on the alpha carbon.
- Next come 4-hydroxyproline and then Asn, which carries a CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain.
- The Asn NH closes the ring onto the Cys carbonyl.
- A second Gly links the Trp carbonyl back to the Ile carbonyl.

**Stereochemistry**
I derived the @/@@ marks for each centre from the drawn wedges and hashes and checked them against the L-amino-acid configurations.

The sulfoxide sulfur is the least certain centre. The drawing is ambiguous there, so I assigned the R configuration known for α-amanitin.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H]2C[S@@](=O)c3[nH]c4cc(O)ccc4c3C[C@H](NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)[C@@H](O)CO)NC(=O)[C@@H]5C[C@@H](O)CN5C(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC2=O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N1

name: Alprostadil
text:
I read the structure as a prostaglandin E1-type molecule: a cyclopentanone ring carrying a hydroxyl, a heptanoic acid chain and a hydroxyoctenyl chain.

**Skeleton**
- The carboxylic acid carbon is followed by 6 CH2 groups, which reach the ring carbon next to the ketone.
- The ring has 5 carbons: C=O, a ring CH bearing the acid chain, a ring CH bearing the alkenyl chain, a CH(OH), and a CH2.
- The alkenyl chain is CH=CH, then CH(OH), then a pentyl group. The double bond is drawn trans.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing, using the atom order of the SMILES below:
- Ring carbon bearing the acid chain (wedge to the chain): `[C@H]1`.
- Ring carbon bearing OH (wedged OH): `[C@@H](O)`.
- Ring carbon bearing the alkenyl chain (hashed bond to the chain): `[C@@H]1`.
- Side-chain carbon bearing OH (wedged OH): `[C@@H](O)`.
- Double bond: `/C=C/` for trans.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCCCC[C@H]1C(=O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/[C@@H](O)CCCCC

name: Alvocidib
text:
I read this as flavopiridol: a chromone core with two ring hydroxyls, a 2-chlorophenyl group, and an N-methyl-3-hydroxypiperidin-4-yl substituent.

**Chromone core**
- The benzene ring carries two OH groups. One sits peri to the C=O carbon and the other is meta to it.
- The carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon bearing the ring oxygen carries the piperidine substituent.
- The pyranone ring contains a C=O, a CH=, and a C(Ar)–O unit, where Ar is 2-chlorophenyl.

**Piperidine ring**
- It is N-methylated.
- C4 is attached to the aromatic carbon by a hashed bond.
- C3 carries an OH, also drawn with a hashed bond.

**Stereochemistry**
- For both hashed carbons I took the implicit H to point toward the viewer. I then worked out the chirality from the 2D positions of the neighbours.
- C4 comes out as `[C@H]` with the neighbour order CH2, H, aryl, C3.
- C3 comes out as `[C@H]` with the neighbour order C4, H, O, CH2.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@H](c2c(O)cc(O)c3c(=O)cc(-c4ccccc4Cl)oc23)[C@H](O)C1

name: Amdinocillin
text:
The drawing shows the penicillin-type bicyclic core of mecillinam (6-amidino-penicillanic acid type). I read it as follows:

- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring. The β-lactam carbonyl is C=O, with N bonded to the ring-fusion carbon (drawn with a wedged H) and to the carbon bearing COOH. S is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon and to the gem-dimethyl carbon.
- **Substituents on the thiazolidine ring:** two methyls on the carbon next to S, and a wedged carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) on the carbon next to N.
- **Side chain:** the hashed bond on the β-lactam carbon goes to N=CH–N, where that last N is part of a saturated seven-membered ring (azepane, six CH2 groups plus N).
- **Stereochemistry:** only the three stereocentres on the bicyclic core are marked (wedge, wedge-H, hash). I took their configuration from the natural penicillin core (2S,5R,6R), which I wrote from memory of the standard penicillin SMILES rather than deriving it from the wedges. The C=N double bond has no cis/trans geometry drawn, so I left it unspecified.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H](N2[C@H](S1)[C@@H](C2=O)N=CN3CCCCCC3)C(=O)O)C

name: Ambrisentan
text:
This molecule is ambrisentan, (S)-2-(4,6-dimethylpyrimidin-2-yloxy)-3-methoxy-3,3-diphenylpropanoic acid.

**Reading the structure**
- The left ring is a pyrimidine with methyl groups at positions 4 and 6, joined through its C2 to an ether oxygen.
- That oxygen is attached by a wedge bond to the central CH carbon.
- This CH carbon also carries a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) and a quaternary carbon.
- The quaternary carbon bears two phenyl rings and an OCH3 group.

**Stereochemistry**
- The wedge oxygen points toward the viewer, so the implicit hydrogen points away.
- The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are O > COOH (O,O,O) > C(Ph)2OMe (O,C,C) > H.
- With H at the back, O (upper left) → COOH (down) → quaternary C (upper right) runs counterclockwise on the page, so the centre is S.

**SMILES check**
- In the SMILES below, the stereocentre's neighbours are written in the order quaternary C, H, O, COOH.
- I worked out that `[C@@H]` in this order would give R, so `[C@H]` is needed for S.

SMILES: COC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)[C@H](Oc1nc(C)cc(C)n1)C(=O)O

name: Amfenac
text:
The drawing shows amfenac: a central benzene ring with three substituents on adjacent carbons.

- A benzoyl group (C=O attached to a phenyl ring) sits on one ring carbon.
- An NH2 group sits on the next carbon.
- A CH2COOH group sits on the carbon after that.

Writing the central ring from the benzoyl-bearing carbon, I get c1(C(=O)c2ccccc2)c(N)c(CC(=O)O)ccc1. The ring has six atoms: the benzoyl carbon, the NH2 carbon, the CH2COOH carbon, then three CH carbons. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(c1ccccc1)c1cccc(CC(=O)O)c1N

name: Alvimopan
text:
I read the structure as alvimopan, a glycine amide of a 2-benzyl propanoic acid carrying a 3,4-dimethyl-4-(3-hydroxyphenyl)piperidine.

**Connectivity**
- The left side is a carboxylic acid, HOOC–CH2–NH–C(=O)–, i.e. a glycine amide.
- The amide carbonyl is attached to a CH bearing a benzyl group (CH2–phenyl) and a CH2 that links to the piperidine nitrogen.
- The piperidine ring is N, CH2, CH2, a quaternary C, a CH, and a CH2 closing back to N.
- The quaternary carbon carries a methyl and a 3-hydroxyphenyl group.
- The adjacent ring CH carries a methyl.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned CIP priorities at each drawn centre and converted them to SMILES chirality tags.
- The side-chain CH has a hashed bond to the CH2N group. This gives S, which corresponds to `[C@@H]` in the SMILES atom order used.
- The quaternary ring carbon has a hashed methyl. This gives R, written `[C@@]`.
- The ring CH has a wedged methyl. This gives R, written `[C@@H]`.

This matches (2S)-side chain and (3R,4R)-piperidine, consistent with alvimopan.

SMILES: OC(=O)CNC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)CN1CC[C@@](C)(c2cccc(O)c2)[C@@H](C)C1

name: Aminoglutethimide
text:
The drawing shows aminoglutethimide, which has three parts.

- **Piperidine-2,6-dione ring:** a quaternary carbon is bonded to a C=O carbon, which is bonded to NH, then a second C=O carbon, then two CH2 groups that close the ring back to the quaternary carbon.
- **Ethyl group:** attached to the quaternary carbon.
- **Aryl group:** a 4-aminophenyl ring, also attached to the quaternary carbon.

The quaternary carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCC1(CCC(=O)NC1=O)c1ccc(N)cc1

name: Amenamevir
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Oxadiazole ring (left):** The atoms are O, then CH, then N, then C (attached to the phenyl), then N, closing back to O. Going round the ring: O1–C(H)=N–C(Ar)=N–O1. The O is bonded to a CH and to an N, and the N is bonded to the C bearing the aryl group. So the ring is c1ncon1 style, which is a 1,2,4-oxadiazole with the aryl at position 3.

SMILES for the ring and phenyl: c1nc(-c2ccc(...)cc2)no1.

**Para-substituted phenyl:** One end carries the oxadiazole and the other carries NH–C(=O)–CH2–N.

**Central amide nitrogen:** This N carries three groups: the CH2, a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring, and a C(=O) attached to the thiane ring.

**Thiane ring:** The carbonyl carbon is attached to a ring CH. The ring is CH, CH2, CH2, S(=O)(=O), CH2, CH2, back to CH, so it is a 1,1-dioxothian-4-yl group.

Full SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1ncon1)CN(c1c(C)cccc1C)C(=O)C1CCS(=O)(=O)CC1

I checked the oxadiazole connectivity. In the drawing, C(H) is bonded to O and double-bonded to N. That N is bonded to C3, which is bonded to the aryl group. C3 is double-bonded to the second N, which is bonded to O. In c1ncon1 notation, c1 (attached to aryl) – n – c – o – n1 would give the aryl carbon between two N atoms. That is the wrong order for this ring. The correct ring is c1(aryl)noc n1: the aryl carbon is bonded to N (which bonds to O) and to the other N (which bonds to CH). Written out: c1(-Ar)noc n1, which is c1(-Ar)nocn1.

Corrected SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1nocn1)CN(c1c(C)cccc1C)C(=O)C1CCS(=O)(=O)CC1

SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1nocn1)CN(c1c(C)cccc1C)C(=O)C1CCS(=O)(=O)CC1

name: Amiloride
text:
This is amiloride. The drawing shows a pyrazine ring with these substituents:

- C–NH2 (top left of the ring)
- N (top)
- C–NH2 (right)
- C–Cl (bottom right)
- N (bottom)
- C bearing the carbonyl (left)

The carbonyl carbon is C(=O), attached to N=C(N)N, a guanidine group.

I wrote the SMILES by walking around the ring from the carbonyl-bearing carbon: C(=O)(N=C(N)N) is attached to c1, then c(N) (the top-left NH2 carbon), then n, then c(N), then c(Cl), then n closing the ring.

SMILES: NC(N)=NC(=O)c1nc(Cl)c(N)nc1N

Checking the ring order: c1 (bearing C=O), then the top-left carbon with NH2 (c(N)), then N (top), then the right carbon with NH2, then the carbon with Cl, then N (bottom), back to c1. Written this way the ring is c1(C=O) c(N) n c(N) c(Cl) n, which gives c1c(N)nc(N)c(Cl)n1.

Rewriting with that order: NC(N)=NC(=O)c1nc(Cl)c(N)nc1N. The ring runs c1, n, c(Cl), c(N), n, c1(N). That means c1 is bonded to the bottom N, then to C-Cl, then to the right C-NH2, then to the top N, then to the top-left C-NH2, which closes back to c1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(N)=NC(=O)c1nc(Cl)c(N)nc1N

name: Aminorex
text:
The drawing shows a 2-amino-oxazoline ring bearing a phenyl group, which is the structure of 4,5-dihydro-5-phenyloxazol-2-amine (aminorex).

- **Ring:** C2 carries the NH2 group and is bonded to the ring O and, by a double bond, to the ring N. The ring N connects to a CH2, which connects to the CH bearing the phenyl group. That CH is bonded back to the ring O.
- **Phenyl:** a benzene ring with alternating double bonds, attached at the CH carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: NC1=NCC(c2ccccc2)O1

name: Amiodarone
text:
The drawing shows amiodarone.

- **Benzofuran core:** the furan O is bonded to C2, which carries an n-butyl chain (4 carbons). C3 is bonded to the carbonyl carbon, and the fused benzene ring completes the bicycle.
- **Ketone:** a C=O links benzofuran C3 to the substituted phenyl ring.
- **Phenyl ring:** it carries two iodines at the positions flanking the carbon that bears the O–CH2CH2–N(Et)2 chain.
- **Side chain:** the oxygen is followed by two CH2 groups and a diethylamino group.

SMILES: CCCCc1oc2ccccc2c1C(=O)c1cc(I)c(OCCN(CC)CC)c(I)c1

name: Amikacin
text:
I read this as amikacin, a kanamycin A derivative. It has a central 2-deoxystreptamine ring with two sugar rings and an acylated amine:

- The left sugar is a 6-amino-6-deoxyglucose, with an aminomethyl group at its ring carbon next to O.
- The upper-right sugar is a 3-amino-3-deoxyglucose, with a CH2OH group.
- The central cyclohexane carries a free NH2, an OH, and two glycosidic O-links.
- The central ring's NH is acylated by a 4-amino-2-hydroxybutanoyl chain (the L-HABA side chain).

I did not independently assign each wedge or hash to an @/@@ label. The stereo descriptors below come from recalling the standard amikacin isomeric SMILES, not from tracing every bond in the drawing.

SMILES: C1[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]1NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)O)O[C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O2)CO)O)N)O)O)O[C@@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CN)O)O)O)N

name: Amlodipine
text:
This structure is amlodipine, a 1,4-dihydropyridine with these substituents:

- The ring NH sits between C2 and C6.
- C2 carries the CH2-O-CH2CH2-NH2 chain.
- C3 carries the ethyl ester (CO2Et).
- C4 carries the 2-chlorophenyl group.
- C5 carries the methyl ester (CO2Me).
- C6 carries the methyl group.

Reading the drawing:
- The ethyl ester is on the carbon bonded to the ring carbon that bears the CH2O chain, which is the lower ring carbon. This carbon sits next to the CH that holds the aryl group.
- The methyl ester is on the upper-right ring carbon.
- The methyl group is on the carbon next to NH.
- The sp3 CH has no wedge or hash, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1=C(COCCN)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC)C1c1ccccc1Cl

name: Amisulpride
text:
The drawing is amisulpride. The structure reads as follows:

- **Pyrrolidine side:** an N-ethylpyrrolidine ring, with the ring carbon next to N bearing a CH2 that links to the amide NH. The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.
- **Amide:** NH–C(=O) joins the CH2 to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring**, going around from the carbonyl-bearing carbon (C1):
  - C1 carries the C(=O)N group.
  - C2 carries OMe, which is at the upper left.
  - C3 is CH.
  - C4 carries NH2.
  - C5 carries the SO2Et group.
  - C6 is CH.

SMILES: CCN1CCCC1CNC(=O)c1cc(S(=O)(=O)CC)c(N)cc1OC

name: Amitraz
text:
This is the amitraz structure: N,N'-bis(2,4-dimethylphenyl)-N-methylformamidine, drawn as a central N-methyl nitrogen flanked by two CH=N–aryl arms.

**Left arm.** The imine N (at 465,650) is bonded to the aromatic carbon at (368,750). That ring carbon is adjacent to a carbon at (230,716) bearing a methyl (the ortho position). The ring continues through (133,818), then (172,954), which carries a methyl (the para position), then (310,987) and (406,885), and back to (368,750). The ring is therefore 2,4-dimethylphenyl.

**Right arm.** The imine N (at 877,748) is bonded to the ring carbon at (1014,781). Its neighbor at (1053,917) bears a methyl (ortho), and the carbon at (1287,849) bears a methyl (para). This is also 2,4-dimethylphenyl.

**Centre.** The central N carries a methyl and is bonded to two carbons, each double-bonded to an imine N (CH=N–aryl).

SMILES: Cc1ccc(N=CN(C)C=Nc2ccc(C)cc2C)c(C)c1

name: Ammonium Sulfate
text:
The drawing shows ammonium sulfate: a central sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens (O=) and two single-bonded O⁻ groups, plus two separate NH4⁺ cations.

Written as a multi-component SMILES, each part is its own fragment: `[NH4+].[NH4+].[O-]S(=O)(=O)[O-]`.

The charges balance: two NH4⁺ give +2 and the sulfate gives −2.

SMILES: [NH4+].[NH4+].[O-]S(=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Amitriptyline
text:
The image shows the tricyclic antidepressant skeleton of amitriptyline:

- A dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) is attached to a propylidene chain: N–CH2–CH2–CH=C.
- The double-bond carbon is the ring carbon of a central seven-membered ring. That ring is fused to two benzene rings and contains an –CH2–CH2– bridge.
- The two aryl branches on the exocyclic alkene carbon are constitutionally equivalent, because each leads through the ethylene bridge to the other ring. The double bond therefore has no E/Z designation, and I added no stereo marks.

SMILES: CN(C)CCC=C1c2ccccc2CCc2ccccc12

name: Amphetamine
text:
The drawing shows a methyl group on the left, attached to a carbon that carries an NH2 group. That carbon connects through a CH2 to a benzene ring, with three double bonds drawn in the ring. The bonds around the NH2-bearing carbon are all plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so I add no stereochemistry.

The molecule is amphetamine (1-phenylpropan-2-amine).

SMILES: CC(N)Cc1ccccc1

name: Amosulalol
text:
The drawing is read in three parts.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying a sulfonamide (S(=O)(=O)NH2), a methyl group, and the side chain. Going around the ring, the sulfonamide-bearing carbon at about (317,770) is adjacent to both the methyl-bearing carbon at (300,885) and the carbon at (425,728). The carbon at (425,728) is adjacent to the side-chain-bearing carbon at (514,798). So the sulfonamide and the side chain are meta to each other, and the methyl is ortho to the sulfonamide and para to the side chain.

**Side chain:** CH(OH)CH2NHCH2CH2O–, ending at the aryl ether oxygen. The CH(OH) carbon has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo.

**Right ring:** a benzene ring with an ortho-methoxy group next to the aryl ether oxygen (2-methoxyphenoxy).

SMILES for the left ring: Cc1ccc(cc1S(N)(=O)=O)C(O)CNCCOc1ccccc1OC

Check on the left ring: c1 (methyl-bearing), c, c, c(side chain), c, c1 (sulfonamide-bearing). The sulfonamide carbon is adjacent to the methyl carbon through the ring closure, and it is also adjacent to the CH between it and the side-chain carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1S(N)(=O)=O)C(O)CNCCOc1ccccc1OC

name: Amodiaquine Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing is amodiaquine dihydrochloride dihydrate, so I wrote it as one SMILES with each component separated by dots.

**Main molecule**
- The left part is a diethylaminomethyl group, CH2N(Et)2, attached to a benzene ring.
- On that ring, the CH2 group sits ortho to the OH, and the NH sits para to the OH.
- The NH links to C4 of a 7-chloroquinoline. In the drawing, the ring nitrogen is at the top, the carbon bearing the NH is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon, and Cl is on the benzo ring.

**Quinoline numbering check**
- N1 is the ring nitrogen, C2 and C3 follow, and C4 carries the NH.
- C4a is the fusion carbon next to C4. From C4a the benzo ring runs C5, C6, C7 (bearing Cl), C8, then C8a, which bonds to N1.
- In the drawing, C8a connects to C8 at the upper right, and C8 connects to C7, which carries Cl. This matches 7-chloro.

**SMILES for the amodiaquine core**
CCN(CC)Cc1cc(Nc2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23)ccc1O

The quinoline part reads c2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23: c2 is C4, then c (C3), c (C2), n (N1), c3 (C8a), c (C8), c(Cl) (C7), c (C6), c (C5), c23 (C4a). This is correct.

**Salt and hydrate components**
The drawing also shows two HCl and two H2O, which I added as separate fragments.

SMILES: CCN(CC)Cc1cc(Nc2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23)ccc1O.Cl.Cl.O.O

name: Amorolfine
text:
I read the molecule as amorolfine, which has a cis-2,6-dimethylmorpholine ring.

- **Left end:** a tert-amyl group (CCC(C)(C)–) sits on a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Linker:** from the ring, a CH2 leads to a CH(CH3), then a CH2, then the morpholine nitrogen.
- **Morpholine ring:** N, CH2, C(CH3), O, C(CH3), CH2, closing back to N. Both ring methyls are drawn with hashed bonds, so each carbon bearing a methyl is a stereocentre.
- **Stereo assignment:** I worked out each hashed centre from the 2D coordinates, with the methyl pointing away from the viewer and the hydrogen towards it. Written as N–CH2–C–O–C–CH2, both centres come out as `@`. Both methyls point the same way, so the ring is cis.
- **Unmarked centre:** the CH(CH3) in the linker is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: CCC(C)(C)c1ccc(CC(C)CN2C[C@H](C)O[C@H](C)C2)cc1

name: Ampicillin
text:
I read this as ampicillin: a penicillin core (a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring) carrying a gem-dimethyl group, a carboxylic acid, and a 2-amino-2-phenylacetamide side chain.

- **Side-chain stereocentre:** I checked this one against the drawing. The NH2 is on a hashed bond, and the CIP priorities are N > C(=O) > phenyl > H. That gives R, which matches natural ampicillin.
- **Ring stereocentres:** I did not check these from the wedges. I took the stereo from the known ampicillin SMILES, assuming the drawing is the natural (2S,5R,6R) isomer.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H](N2[C@H](S1)[C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)[C@@H](C3=CC=CC=C3)N)C(=O)O)C

name: Amphotericin B
text:
This is amphotericin B, a heptaene macrolide, and I wrote the SMILES by recognising that scaffold and checking it against the drawing rather than deriving every centre from the wedges. The checks I made:

- **Polyene:** I counted seven conjugated C=C bonds running along the bottom of the macrocycle, which matches a heptaene. I wrote all of them as E (trans); the drawing's zig-zag geometry is consistent with that.
- **Hydroxylated chain:** going from the ketal carbon toward the lactone C=O, the chain is CH2, CH(OH), CH2, CH(OH), CH(OH), CH2, CH2, CH(OH), CH2, CH(OH), CH2, C(=O)O. This matches the drawing.
- **Ketal ring:** it is a tetrahydropyran with a hemiketal OH, a ring OH and a COOH.
- **Sugar:** the mycosamine (3-amino-3,6-dideoxymannose) is attached through an O-glycosidic link to the CH just after the polyene.
- **Lactone end:** the ring closes through the ester O onto a CH(CH3), which is followed by CH(CH3), CH(OH) and CH(CH3), the last of which is attached to the diene.

I took the stereodescriptors from the known amphotericin B structure rather than re-deriving each one from the wedges and hashes.

SMILES: C[C@H]1/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](C[C@H]2[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@@](O2)(C[C@H](C[C@H]([C@@H](CC[C@H](C[C@H](CC(=O)O[C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]1O)C)C)O)O)O)O)O)O)O)C(=O)O)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)C)O)N)O

name: Amoxicillin
text:
This is amoxicillin: a penicillin core (a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring carrying two methyl groups and a carboxylic acid) with a 4-hydroxyphenylglycyl amide side chain.

I read the stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes at each centre:

- **C5 (S–CH–N ring fusion):** the H is drawn as a wedge, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- **C6 (carbon bearing the amide N):** the amide N is hashed, so the implicit H is toward the viewer, which gives `[C@H]`.
- **C3 (carbon bearing COOH):** the COOH is a wedge, so the implicit H is away from the viewer, which gives `[C@H]`.
- **Side-chain α-carbon:** the NH2 is hashed, which gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CC1(C)S[C@@H]2[C@H](NC(=O)[C@H](N)c3ccc(O)cc3)C(=O)N2[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: Amprolium
text:
The drawing shows a pyrimidine ring joined through a CH2 linker to an N-substituted pyridinium ring, with a chloride counterion.

**Pyrimidine ring.** The ring atoms are C2, N3, C4, C5, C6 and N1.
- C2 carries a propyl chain (CH3-CH2-CH2-).
- C4 carries the NH2 group.
- C5 carries the CH2 linker.
- Bond orders: C2=N1 is double, C4=N3 is double, and C5=C6 is double. In the image, N(top)–C(top, CH)=C5 is double and C5–C4 is single.

**Pyridinium ring.** The positively charged N is bonded to the CH2 linker and to a ring carbon bearing a methyl group.
- Ring atoms: N+, C(CH3), CH, CH, CH, CH.
- Double bonds: N+=CH, C(CH3)=CH, and CH=CH, which gives the aromatic pyridinium.

**Assembled SMILES.** Written aromatic, the pyrimidine is CCCc1ncc(C[n+]2ccccc2C)c(N)n1, with the chloride as a separate ion.

Check on the ring: c1 (C2, propyl-bearing), n (N1), c (C6), c(...) (C5), c(N) (C4), n1 (N3) closes back to C2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCc1ncc(C[n+]2ccccc2C)c(N)n1.[Cl-]

name: Amprenavir
text:
This drawing is amprenavir, the HIV protease inhibitor. I identified it from its fragments, and my own CIP check of the drawing covered only the hydroxyl-bearing carbon. The other two stereocentres, and the SMILES string itself, rely on my recall of amprenavir's published structure rather than being re-derived from the image.

**Fragments read from the drawing:**
- A 4-aminophenyl ring carries a sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)–N, with the sulfonamide nitrogen also bearing an isobutyl group.
- From that nitrogen the chain runs N–CH2–CH(OH)–CH(NH–)–CH2–Ph. The hydroxyl is drawn with a hashed bond, and the carbon carrying NH is drawn with a wedge to the benzyl CH2.
- The NH is part of a carbamate, NH–C(=O)–O, whose oxygen is bonded to the 3-position of a tetrahydrofuran ring. That ring carbon is drawn with a wedge.

**Stereochemistry:** At the hydroxyl carbon, the priorities are OH, then CH(N), then CH2N, then H. With OH hashed and H toward the viewer, I get R, which matches the published (2S,3R) assignment for the hydroxy-bearing carbon in amprenavir. The other two centres are written to match the known structure.

SMILES: CC(C)CN(C[C@H]([C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)O[C@H]1CCOC1)O)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(N)cc1

name: Anagrelide
text:
This drawing matches the structure of quazinone-type compounds (anagrelide). Anagrelide is 6,7-dichloro-1,5-dihydroimidazo[2,1-b]quinazolin-2-one.

Reading the drawing atom by atom:
- The carbonyl carbon (C=O) bonds to NH and to a CH2.
- That CH2 bonds to the ring N.
- The ring N bonds to the amidine carbon and to a second CH2, which attaches to the aromatic ring.
- The NH bonds to the amidine carbon, which is double-bonded to the N=.
- That N= attaches to an aromatic carbon.
- The benzene ring carries two adjacent Cl atoms. One Cl is on the carbon next to the carbon bearing the CH2, and the other is on the following carbon.

SMILES: O=C1CN2Cc3c(ccc(Cl)c3Cl)N=C2N1

Checking the ring: c3 (attached to CH2), then c(...) bearing N=, which is the other fusion carbon. The path "Cc3c(ccc(Cl)c3Cl)N=C2N1" places the first aromatic atom c3 as the CH2-bearing carbon. The next atom, c(, is the N-bearing carbon, and its branch runs c, c, c(Cl), c3Cl. That makes the ring c3, c(N), c, c, c(Cl), c(Cl) closing back to c3, which is six atoms. The Cl-bearing carbon c3Cl is adjacent to the CH2-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1CN2Cc3c(ccc(Cl)c3Cl)N=C2N1

name: Anastrozole
text:
This is anastrozole. The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents in a 1,3,5 pattern.

- Two of the substituents are C(CH3)2–C≡N groups, one at the upper left and one at the bottom.
- The third is a CH2 group attached to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole.
- In the triazole, N1 is bonded to the CH2, to an adjacent N (the lower N), and to a CH carbon (top). That top CH is double-bonded to the right N. The right N connects to a CH, which is double-bonded to the lower N.

So the ring is n1cncn1 with the substituent on N1, which gives Cn1cncn1 style connectivity for the triazole.

The SMILES is N#CC(C)(C)c1cc(Cn2cncn2)cc(C(C)(C)C#N)c1.

Check on the triazole ring: N1 (attached to CH2), then C, N, C, N, closing back to N1. In the drawing, N1 is bonded to the top CH and to the lower N. The top CH is bonded to the right N, the right N to the lower-right CH, and that CH to the lower N, which closes to N1. In my SMILES, n2 c n c n2 gives N1–C–N–C–N–N1. That matches: N1, CH, N, CH, N, back to N1.

SMILES: N#CC(C)(C)c1cc(Cn2cncn2)cc(C(C)(C)C#N)c1

name: Anagliptin
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-methylpyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine-6-carboxamide whose amide nitrogen carries a CH2–C(CH3)2–NH–CH2–C(=O)– chain ending in a 2-cyanopyrrolidine amide.

**Fused bicycle (left).** The pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine has a methyl on the pyrazole carbon next to the ring nitrogen. The carboxamide C(=O)N sits on the pyrimidine carbon between the CH= next to the left-hand ring N and the CH= next to the bridgehead N.

**Linker (centre).** The amide NH is followed by CH2, then a quaternary carbon with two methyls, then a secondary NH. That NH is followed by CH2 and a C(=O) that acylates the pyrrolidine nitrogen.

**Pyrrolidine (right).** It is a five-membered ring (N plus four carbons). The carbon next to N bears a nitrile on a wedge bond, so it is the only stereocentre drawn with stereochemistry.

**Stereochemistry.** With H pointing away, the substituents run N → CH2 → CN clockwise. The priorities are N > C#N > CH2, so N → CN → CH2 runs counterclockwise, which makes the centre S. Written as N3CCC[C@H]3C#N, the neighbour order is CH2, H, N, CN, and this corresponds to @.

SMILES: Cc1cc2ncc(C(=O)NCC(C)(C)NCC(=O)N3CCC[C@H]3C#N)cn2n1

name: Anacetrapib
text:
I read this as anacetrapib, an oxazolidinone carrying a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group and an N-benzyl biaryl.

- **Oxazolidinone core:** the ring is N–C(=O)–O–C5–C4. The hashed methyl is on C4 and the hashed aryl bond is on C5.
- **C5 substituent:** a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.
- **N substituent:** a CH2 linked to a benzene ring that carries a CF3 para to the biaryl bond. Its neighbouring carbon bears a second aryl ring.
- **Second aryl ring:** it carries OMe ortho to the biaryl bond, F, and an isopropyl group.

**Stereochemistry from the hashed bonds:**
- C4: with the methyl pointing away and the neighbours ordered N, C5, CH3, I get S.
- C5: with the aryl pointing away and the neighbours ordered O, C4, aryl, I get R.
- Written as `C[C@H]1[C@H](...)`, the SMILES encodes (4S,5R), matching the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@H](OC(=O)N1Cc1cc(ccc1-c1cc(C(C)C)c(F)cc1OC)C(F)(F)F)c1cc(cc(c1)C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F

name: Androgen receptor antagonist 2
text:
This is an enzalutamide-like structure with an extra fluorine on the left aryl ring.

**Left aryl ring.** Reading from the ring carbon bonded to N: C1 is attached to N, C2 (above) carries F, C3 carries CF3, C4 carries C#N, and C5 and C6 are CH.

**Central ring.** This is a thiohydantoin. N(left) is bonded to C(=O) and to C(=S). The C(=O) is bonded to C(CH3)2, which is bonded to N(right). N(right) is bonded to C(=S) and to the right aryl ring.

**Right aryl ring.** Reading from the ring carbon attached to N: the next carbon is CH, then C–F, then C bearing C(=O)NHCH3, then CH, then CH, which closes the ring. In the drawing, the carbon bonded to N sits at (918, 723). Its neighbours are (993, 633) and (960, 834). The carbon at (960, 834) is CH and connects to (1077, 852), which carries F. That carbon connects to (1152, 762), which carries the amide, and the ring then continues through (1110, 652) and (993, 633).

**SMILES.** Left ring: c1(N2...)c(F)c(C(F)(F)F)c(C#N)cc1. Right ring: c1ccc(C(=O)NC)c(F)c1, starting at the ring carbon attached to N.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(C(F)(F)F)c1F

name: Andarine
text:
I read the structure as a 4-acetamidophenoxy group joined through a CH2 to a quaternary carbon. That carbon carries a methyl group, an OH and a C(=O)NH link to a 4-nitro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring.

- **Stereocentre:** The methyl is drawn with a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. Seen from the front, the other three substituents run OH (up), CH2 (lower right), C=O (lower left), which is clockwise. Seen from the methyl side (behind the plane), the same order is counterclockwise. With the neighbour order methyl, O, CH2, C(=O) in the SMILES, that is `@`.
- **Left ring:** The NH-bearing carbon, a CF3 carbon next to it, and a nitro carbon next to that give 4-nitro-3-(trifluoromethyl)aniline substitution.
- **Right ring:** The ring is para-substituted, with the ether O on one side and NHC(=O)CH3 on the other.

SMILES: C[C@](O)(COc1ccc(NC(C)=O)cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])c(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Androstenedione
text:
The drawing is a steroid skeleton (four fused rings), which I read as androst-4-ene-3,17-dione.

- **Ring A:** a six-membered ring with a ketone (C=O) at the right-hand end, conjugated to a C=C double bond (C4=C5).
- **Ring D:** a five-membered ring with a ketone at the far left (C17).
- **Methyl groups:** two methyls drawn with wedge bonds, one at C10 and one at C13.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** three explicit H atoms. The top H at C8 is a wedge. The H at C9 and the H at C14 are hashed.

These wedges and hashes match the natural steroid configuration. I took the stereo SMILES from my memory of the known androstenedione string rather than deriving each @/@@ from the drawing, so the chirality marks are the least-checked part of the answer.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CCC2=O)CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]34C

name: Anamorelin
text:
I read the structure as anamorelin: a tryptophan-derived amide carrying a 2-amino-2-methylpropanamide cap, linked to a 3-benzylpiperidine-3-carbonyl trimethylhydrazide.

**Fragments**
- Top right: H2N–C(CH3)2–C(=O)–NH–, an α-aminoisobutyryl amide.
- Centre: a CH bearing the NH, a C=O and a CH2–indol-3-yl group (a tryptophan unit). The CH2 bond is hashed.
- The tryptophan C=O is bonded to the nitrogen of a piperidine ring.
- Piperidine C3 is quaternary. It carries a wedged benzyl group and a C(=O)–N(CH3)–N(CH3)2 group.

**Stereochemistry**
- Tryptophan carbon: the hashed CH2 points away, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Working through the neighbour order gives `[C@@H]` when written as `C(=O)[C@@H](Cc…)N`.
- Quaternary piperidine carbon: the wedged benzyl points toward the viewer. Viewed from the benzyl side, the C=O, ring CH2–N and ring CH2 neighbours run clockwise. In the order I wrote them, `C(=O)[C@@]1(Cc2ccccc2)CCCN(C1)…`, this gives `@@`.

I checked the SMILES against the drawing atom by atom.

SMILES: CN(C)N(C)C(=O)[C@@]1(Cc2ccccc2)CCCN(C1)C(=O)[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)C(C)(C)N

name: Aniline
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three alternating double bonds, and an H2N label attached to one ring carbon through a single bond. This is aniline (phenylamine).

The ring has 6 vertices, and the amino group is the only substituent.

SMILES: Nc1ccccc1

name: Ansamitocin P-3
text:
This drawing matches the ansamitocin P-3 / maytansinoid skeleton, and I wrote the SMILES from that match. I did not re-derive every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the stereo marks come from the known natural-product configuration.

Features I read from the image:
- **Aromatic ring:** it carries OMe, Cl and an N-methyl amide nitrogen.
- **Macrocycle:** it contains a diene, a methyl-substituted alkene, a methoxy-bearing carbon, an epoxide, and an amide C(=O)CH2.
- **Carbinolamine carbamate:** a carbon bearing OH and NH sits in a cyclic carbamate (NH–C(=O)–O).
- **Ester:** an isobutyrate (OC(=O)CH(CH3)2) is attached to the macrocycle.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@@H]2C[C@]([C@@H](/C=C/C=C(/CC3=CC(=C(C(=C3)OC)Cl)N(C(=O)C[C@@H]([C@]4([C@H]1O4)C)OC(=O)C(C)C)C)\C)OC)(NC(=O)O2)O

name: Ansamitocins
Anidulafungin
text:
I wrote this SMILES from the drawing's overall structure, which looks like an echinocandin lipopeptide (an anidulafungin-type cyclic hexapeptide with a pentyloxy-terphenyl side chain). I did not derive each stereocentre independently from the wedges and hashes. The stereo descriptors come from my recollection of the known anidulafungin SMILES and may not match the drawing exactly.

The parts I read directly from the image:

- **Side chain:** a pentyloxy group on a para-linked terphenyl, ending in an amide C(=O)–NH to the ring.
- **Ornithine residue:** a 4,5-dihydroxyornithine unit, so the ring runs NH–CH(C=O)–CH2–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–NH, with the second CH(OH) attached to the amide NH.
- **Proline residues:** one 3-hydroxy-4-methylproline and one 4-hydroxyproline.
- **Threonine residues:** two threonines.
- **Aryl residue:** one residue carrying a CH(OH)–CH(OH)–(4-hydroxyphenyl) side chain.

SMILES: CCCCCOc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)N[C@H]4C[C@H]([C@H](NC(=O)[C@@H]5[C@H]([C@H](CN5C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@@H]6C[C@H](CN6C(=O)[C@@H](NC4=O)[C@@H](C)O)O)[C@H]([C@@H](c7ccc(O)cc7)O)O)[C@@H](C)O)C)O)O)O

name: Anthracene
text:
The drawing shows three fused six-membered rings in a linear arrangement, which is anthracene (C14H10). All 14 vertices are carbons, and there are no heteroatoms, charges or stereo marks.

I read the Kekulé bond pattern from the drawing as follows:
- Left ring: a double bond on the left vertical edge, plus double bonds at the upper right (top-left vertex to the fusion carbon) and the lower right (bottom-left vertex to the fusion carbon).
- Middle ring: the top vertex is double-bonded to the right fusion carbon, and the bottom vertex is double-bonded to the right fusion carbon. The two left fusion carbons are each double-bonded within the left ring.
- Right ring: a double bond from the top vertex to the upper right vertex, and a double bond from the bottom vertex to the lower right vertex.

The aromatic SMILES is c1ccc2cc3ccccc3cc2c1, which is the standard anthracene string and is valid.

SMILES: c1ccc2cc3ccccc3cc2c1

name: Anserine
text:
The drawing shows anserine (β-alanyl-N(π)-methyl-histidine). I read it in four parts:

- **Left chain:** H2N–CH2–CH2–C(=O)–NH, a β-alanine unit joined through an amide.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries the amide NH, the carboxylic acid (HO–C=O), a CH2 drawn on a wedge bond, and an implicit H.
- **Ring:** the CH2 leads to an imidazole. The ring carbon bearing the CH2 sits next to the N–CH3 nitrogen, and the other ring nitrogen is the unsubstituted =N–.
- **Stereo assignment:** the wedged CH2 points toward the viewer, so H is at the back. Going from NH to CH2 to COOH is then clockwise with H pointing away. That corresponds to `N[C@@H](C…)C(=O)O` in SMILES, the L-histidine configuration.

SMILES: NCCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1cncn1C)C(=O)O

name: Angiotensin Ii
text:
This is angiotensin II (Asp‑Arg‑Val‑Tyr‑Ile‑His‑Pro‑Phe), drawn as a linear octapeptide from the N‑terminal Asp to the C‑terminal Phe.

**Residues, N‑ to C‑terminus:**
- Asp has a free NH2 and a CH2COOH side chain.
- Arg has a propyl chain ending in a guanidine drawn as N=C(NH2)NH2.
- Val has an isopropyl side chain.
- Tyr has a 4‑hydroxybenzyl side chain.
- Ile has a sec‑butyl side chain.
- His has an imidazol‑4‑ylmethyl side chain.
- Pro is the five‑membered ring that links His and Phe.
- Phe has a benzyl side chain and a free COOH.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each wedge or hash centre by its drawn geometry. All eight α‑carbons are S, which is the natural L configuration. The Ile β‑carbon (hashed methyl) is also S, giving the usual (2S,3S) isoleucine.

I then converted this to SMILES and checked each centre's @/@@ against the standard L‑amino‑acid patterns, which required correcting Val and Ile from my first draft.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: Anthralin
text:
The drawing is an anthracenone skeleton: a central six-membered ring fused to two benzene rings, with a CH2 at the top and a C=O at the bottom. This is dithranol (anthralin).

Reading the central ring: the top vertex is CH2, bonded to two aromatic fusion carbons. The bottom vertex is C=O, bonded to the other two fusion carbons. Each outer ring carries an OH on the carbon adjacent to the fusion carbon next to the carbonyl, so both OH groups sit at the peri positions beside the C=O (positions 1 and 8).

I wrote the SMILES by starting at the carbonyl carbon and going around the left ring:

O=C1c2c(O)cccc2Cc2cccc(O)c21

Atom check:
- C1 is the carbonyl carbon.
- c2 is the left fusion carbon next to the carbonyl.
- c(O) is the aromatic carbon bearing OH.
- ccc are the three aromatic CH carbons.
- c2 is the left fusion carbon next to the CH2, which closes the left aromatic ring.
- C is the CH2.
- The second c2 is the right fusion carbon next to the CH2, opening a new ring-closure 2.
- ccc are the three right-ring CH carbons.
- c(O) is the right aromatic carbon bearing OH.
- c21 is the right fusion carbon next to the carbonyl; it closes ring 2 (the right aromatic ring) and ring 1 (the central ring back to the carbonyl).

Each benzene ring has six carbons: fusion, C-OH, three CH and fusion. The SMILES is valid and matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1c2c(O)cccc2Cc2cccc(O)c21

name: Apalutamide
text:
This structure is apalutamide.

**Pyridine ring.** The ring atoms are N, C(CN), C(CF3), CH, C(N-attached) and CH. The nitrile carbon sits on the carbon next to the ring N. The CF3 carbon is adjacent to that one. The thiohydantoin N attaches at the carbon between a CH and another CH, which is the 3-position relative to the ring N.

**Thiohydantoin core.** A five-membered ring: N1 (attached to the pyridine), C(=O), spiro C (part of a cyclobutane), N (attached to the aryl ring), and C(=S) bridging the two N atoms.

**Aryl ring.** The ring N attaches at one carbon. The ring then runs CH, CH, C(C(=O)NHMe), C(F), CH back to the start. The carbon bearing the amide is para to the ring N-attached carbon, and F is ortho to the amide carbon and meta to the N-attached carbon.

**SMILES.**
- Pyridine: c1(C#N)ncc(cc1C(F)(F)F)N...
- Core: N2C(=O)C3(CCC3)N(C2=S)...
- Aryl: c4ccc(C(=O)NC)c(F)c4

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C12CCC2)c1cnc(C#N)c(c1)C(F)(F)F

name: Apigenin
text:
The drawing is a flavone with three hydroxyl groups, which matches apigenin (5,7,4'-trihydroxyflavone).

- **B ring:** a benzene ring with an OH at the para position, attached to C2 of the pyranone ring.
- **C ring:** a pyranone ring containing the ring O, C2, C3 (CH), and C4 (C=O).
- **A ring:** the fused benzene ring, with OH at C5 (next to the carbonyl-bearing ring fusion carbon) and OH at C7 (the upper right, meta to C5).

I wrote the SMILES by tracing the drawing: the ring O is bonded to C2 and to C8a. C8 (CH) leads to C7(OH), then C6 (CH), then C5(OH), then C4a, which bonds to C4 (C=O) and back to C8a.

SMILES: O=C1C=C(c2ccc(O)cc2)Oc2cc(O)cc(O)c12

name: Apilimod
text:
The drawing shows these parts:

- **Pyrimidine core:** the ring atoms are C4 (bearing the hydrazone NH), C5 (CH), C6 (bearing the morpholine), N1, C2 (bearing the O-CH2CH2-pyridyl group) and N3.
- **Morpholine:** attached through its nitrogen to C6 of the pyrimidine.
- **Pyridine side chain:** a 2-pyridyl group joined by CH2CH2 to an O on C2 of the pyrimidine.
- **Hydrazone:** the pyrimidine C4 carries NH–N=CH–, linked to a 3-methylphenyl ring (the methyl sits meta to the CH=N attachment).

The C=N double bond is drawn with plain bonds and no explicit cis/trans cue, but the layout looks like the usual E form. I have written it as E, since the chain appears to zigzag across the double bond.

Checking the geometry: the NH sits at the lower left of the N=C bond and the aryl group at the right, with N at the upper left and CH at the lower right. N(H) is below-left of the =N, and the aryl is above-right of the CH, so they are on opposite sides, which is trans (E).

SMILES, written from the pyrimidine C4: `c1(N/N=C/c2cccc(C)c2)cc(N3CCOCC3)nc(OCCc3ccccn3)n1`

SMILES: Cc1cccc(/C=N/Nc2cc(N3CCOCC3)nc(OCCc3ccccn3)n2)c1

name: Apixaban
text:
This structure is apixaban. I read it region by region and then assembled the SMILES.

- **Methoxyphenyl:** a para-substituted benzene bearing OCH3, attached through its other para carbon to N1 of the pyrazole.
- **Pyrazole core:** N1 (bonded to the methoxyphenyl) is bonded to N2, which is double-bonded to C3. C3 carries the C(=O)NH2 carboxamide. C3 is bonded to C3a, and C3a is double-bonded to C7a, which closes the ring back to N1.
- **Fused lactam ring:** C7a is bonded to a C(=O), which is bonded to N. That N is bonded to the second benzene ring and to CH2–CH2, which returns to C3a.
- **Second benzene ring:** para-substituted, with its other para position bonded to the N of a piperidin-2-one. That ring is N–C(=O)–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH2, closing back to N.

SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)-n1nc(C(N)=O)c2CCN(c3ccc(cc3)N3CCCCC3=O)C(=O)c12

name: Amphotericin B monomethyl ester
text:
I read this as an amphotericin B-type macrolide. It has a 7-double-bond polyene, a methyl ester on the hemiketal ring, and a mycosamine-type amino sugar on the allylic oxygen. The chain carries more hydroxyl groups than amphotericin B and has no ketone.

I read the ring atoms and chain carbons one at a time and assigned each centre from the wedges and hashes. I assumed all seven polyene double bonds are trans. The two bonds I measured came out trans, and I did not check the other five individually.

SMILES: O=C1C[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)CC[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)C[C@]2(O)C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C(=O)OC)[C@H](O2)C[C@@H](O[C@H]3[C@@H](O)[C@@H](N)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)O3)/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@H](C)O1

name: Apomorphine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region gives a tetracyclic aporphine skeleton, which matches apomorphine.

- **Catechol ring (left):** an aromatic ring carrying two adjacent OH groups.
- **Linking CH2:** this ring connects through a CH2 to the stereocentre, which is drawn with a hashed bond to H.
- **N-methyl piperidine ring (right):** the stereocentre bonds to N, which carries a methyl group. The N continues through two CH2 groups to an aromatic carbon of the lower benzene ring.
- **Lower benzene ring:** its other ring-fusion carbon is bonded directly to the stereocentre.
- **Biaryl bond:** the lower benzene ring is also bonded directly to the catechol ring.

For the stereocentre, the hashed bond puts H at the back. Viewed from the front, the sequence N → CH2 → aromatic C runs counterclockwise. In the SMILES below, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is aromatic C, H, N (ring closure 1), CH2. That order corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: CN1CCc2cccc3c2[C@H]1Cc1ccc(O)c(O)c1-3

name: Antimony Potassium Tartrate
text:
The drawing shows these components, which I wrote as separate fragments joined with dots:

- Two Sb³⁺ ions and two K⁺ ions.
- Two identical tartrate tetraanions. Each is ⁻O₂C–CH(O⁻)–CH(O⁻)–CO₂⁻, with both alkoxide oxygens on wedge bonds.
- Three water molecules. Two are labelled H₂O. The third label is garbled, with H₂ above an O and a superscript, and I read it as a third water. This also balances the charge: 2 × (+3) + 2 × (+1) = +8 against 2 × (−4) = −8, so no extra O²⁻ is needed.

For the stereochemistry I assigned CIP priorities at each stereocentre as O > COO⁻ > C > H. With the hydrogen pointing away from the viewer, the order O → COO⁻ → C runs clockwise at both carbons, so both centres are R. This is the (R,R), or L-tartrate, form. The corresponding SMILES for each tartrate is `[O-]C(=O)[C@H]([O-])[C@@H]([O-])C([O-])=O`.

SMILES: [Sb+3].[Sb+3].[K+].[K+].[O-]C(=O)[C@H]([O-])[C@@H]([O-])C([O-])=O.[O-]C(=O)[C@H]([O-])[C@@H]([O-])C([O-])=O.O.O.O

name: Aprocitentan
text:
This is the macitentan-like scaffold, so I read it region by region.

- **Central pyrimidine ring:** The ring atoms are C(NHSO2NH2), C(aryl), C(OCH2...), N, CH, N. The carbon bearing the sulfamide NH is bonded to ring N, and the carbon bearing the O-chain is bonded to the other ring N, with a CH between the two nitrogens.
- **Substituents on that ring:** The 4-bromophenyl group sits on the carbon between the NHSO2NH2-bearing carbon and the O-bearing carbon. The NH–S(=O)(=O)–NH2 group is on the left.
- **Linker:** The ring carbon on the right carries O–CH2–CH2–O, which connects to the second pyrimidine.
- **Second pyrimidine:** It is attached at C2 and carries Br at C5, giving 5-bromopyrimidin-2-yl.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)Nc1ncnc(OCCOc2ncc(Br)cn2)c1-c1ccc(Br)cc1

name: Apraclonidine
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents, plus a five-membered imidazoline ring.

**Benzene ring.** Going around the ring from the top:
- The top-left carbon carries Cl.
- The next carbon, bottom-left, carries the NH link to the imidazoline.
- The bottom carbon carries Cl.
- The right-bottom carbon is CH.
- The right-top carbon carries NH2.
- The top carbon is CH.

So the NH-bearing carbon sits between two Cl-bearing carbons, and the NH2 is para to the NH. This is 4-amino-2,6-dichlorophenyl attached to the imidazoline through NH, which is the clonidine analog with a 4-amino group (apraclonidine).

**Imidazoline ring.** The ring is C(=N–CH2–CH2–NH), with the exocyclic NH attached to the C2 carbon.

**SMILES.** Writing the aryl ring first: Nc1cc(Cl)c(NC2=NCCN2)c(Cl)c1. Reading it back against the drawing:
- N is the NH2.
- c1 is the ring carbon bearing NH2.
- c is the CH.
- c(Cl) is the carbon bearing Cl.
- c(NC2=NCCN2) is the carbon bearing the NH–imidazoline.
- c(Cl) is the second Cl-bearing carbon.
- c1 is the final CH, closing the ring.

This matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: Nc1cc(Cl)c(NC2=NCCN2)c(Cl)c1

name: Arachidonic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a 20-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid at one end (C=O and OH labelled), so it is a C20 fatty acid.

Counting from the carboxyl carbon (C1) along the chain, the four C=C double bonds sit at C5=C6, C8=C9, C11=C12 and C14=C15. Each is separated by a single CH2, and the chain ends in a pentyl group (C16–C20).

All four double bonds are drawn with cis (Z) geometry. This is arachidonic acid, (5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z)-eicosa-5,8,11,14-tetraenoic acid.

SMILES: CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\C/C=C\C/C=C\CCCC(=O)O

name: Apremilast
text:
This is apremilast, the (S)-enantiomer.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carries an ethoxy group (OCH2CH3) and a methoxy group (OCH3) on adjacent carbons.
- **Side chain:** the ring is attached to a stereocentre. That carbon bears a CH2–S(=O)(=O)–CH3 (methylsulfonylmethyl) group, a hydrogen, and the imide nitrogen.
- **Right fragment:** the imide nitrogen is part of an isoindoline-1,3-dione (phthalimide). The benzo ring of this unit carries an NH–C(=O)CH3 acetamide on the carbon next to one of the imide carbonyl carbons.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH2 bond to the stereocentre is drawn as a hashed wedge, so the CH2 points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - The CIP priorities are N, then CH2S, then aryl, then H.
  - Seen from the front, N → CH2S → aryl runs clockwise.
  - Because H points toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving S.
  - In the SMILES below, the atom order around the stereocentre is aryl, H, CH2S, N, and `[C@@H]` in that order corresponds to S.

SMILES: CCOc1cc(ccc1OC)[C@@H](CS(C)(=O)=O)N1C(=O)c2cccc(NC(C)=O)c2C1=O

name: Aranidipine
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine (nifedipine-type) core with these parts:

- **Ring:** the NH is bonded to C2 (bearing a methyl), which is double-bonded to C3. C3 carries an ester and is bonded to C4, the sp3 carbon. C4 is bonded to C5, which is double-bonded to C6. C6 carries a methyl and is bonded back to the NH.
- **C4 substituent:** a 2-nitrophenyl group, with the nitro group ortho to the attachment point.
- **C5 ester:** a methyl ester, C(=O)OC.
- **C3 ester:** C(=O)OCC(C)=O, an acetonyl ester.

The sp3 C4 is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereochemistry.

Writing the SMILES from the ring N: N1C(C)=C(C(=O)OCC(C)=O)C(c2ccccc2[N+](=O)[O-])C(C(=O)OC)=C1C

SMILES: CC(=O)COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC)C1c1ccccc1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Arecoline
text:
This is arecoline, a tetrahydropyridine ring with an N-methyl group and a methyl ester.

**Ring.** Reading the vertices around the six-membered ring:
- N is at the lower left and carries a methyl group.
- Going around from N: CH2 (left, upper), then CH2 (top left), then CH (top right) double-bonded to C (right), which carries the ester, then CH2 (bottom) back to N.

**Substituents.**
- The N-methyl group is attached to N at the lower left.
- The ester is on the ring carbon at the right: C(=O)OC.

**SMILES.** Starting from the N-methyl group: CN1CCC=C(C1)C(=O)OC

This has six ring atoms: N1, C, C, C=, C(, C1). It matches the drawing atom for atom, and no stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: CN1CCC=C(C1)C(=O)OC

name: Aprepitant
text:
This structure is aprepitant. I read it region by region and worked out the stereochemistry from the three wedged bonds.

**Connectivity**
- The left ring is a 1,2,4-triazol-3-one: C(=O) between two NH groups, with C=N–NH closing the ring. Its ring carbon carries a CH2 that joins the morpholine nitrogen.
- The morpholine ring has N, O and two CH2 groups. The carbon next to the ring O bears an exocyclic O, and the carbon next to N bears a 4-fluorophenyl group.
- The exocyclic O is linked to a CH(CH3) carbon that carries a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring.

**Stereocentres**
- The ethyl carbon has the methyl on a wedge, which gives `@@` in the SMILES order I used.
- The morpholine carbon bearing the exocyclic O has that O on a wedge, which gives `@`.
- The morpholine carbon bearing the fluorophenyl has that aryl group on a wedge, which gives `@`.

SMILES: C[C@@H](O[C@H]1OCCN(CC2=NNC(=O)N2)[C@H]1c3ccc(F)cc3)c4cc(cc(c4)C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F

name: Aripiprazole
text:
The drawing is aripiprazole. I read it region by region:

- **Left ring system:** a lactam, with C(=O) bonded to NH, fused to a benzene ring. The two CH2 groups of the saturated ring are attached to the carbonyl carbon and to the aromatic carbon.
- **Linker:** the aromatic ring carries an O–CH2CH2CH2CH2 chain, which I counted as four carbons between O and N.
- **Piperazine:** the chain ends on one piperazine nitrogen, and the other nitrogen is bonded to the aryl group.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring bearing two adjacent chlorines. The carbon attached to N is C1, the neighbouring carbon C2 has Cl, and C3 has Cl. This is 2,3-dichlorophenyl.

The SMILES is O=C1CCc2ccc(OCCCCN3CCN(CC3)c3cccc(Cl)c3Cl)cc2N1.

Atom-by-atom check:
- The lactam is C1(=O)CCc2ccc(...)cc2N1. The aromatic carbon c2 bonded to the CH2 is followed by c, c, then c(O...), then c, then c2, which bears N. The drawing shows the O-bearing carbon adjacent to the CH that sits next to the N-bearing carbon, so the O-substituted carbon is meta to the CH2-bearing carbon and para to... this matches aripiprazole's 7-position substitution.
- The dichlorophenyl is c3cccc(Cl)c3Cl, where the ipso carbon is followed by three CH, then C(Cl), then C(Cl) closing the ring back to the ipso carbon. This puts the chlorines at positions 3 and 2, as drawn.

SMILES: O=C1CCc2ccc(OCCCCN3CCN(CC3)c3cccc(Cl)c3Cl)cc2N1

name: Ar-67
text:
This is the 7‑tert‑butyldimethylsilyl, 10‑hydroxy derivative of camptothecin, the structure known as DB‑67.

- **Core:** the pentacyclic camptothecin framework is a quinoline fused to a pyrrolo‑pyridone, which is fused to the α‑hydroxy lactone ring. The lactone has a C=O and an ring O–CH2.
- **Quaternary stereocentre:** it carries an ethyl group and a hashed OH, and is bonded to the lactone C=O and to the ring carbon on the pyridone side. From the hash and the positions of the other three substituents, I assign it `@@` in the SMILES order written below.
- **Quinoline substituents:** an OH sits on the benzo ring, and a Si(CH3)2–C(CH3)3 group sits on the quinoline carbon next to the CH2.

I traced the quinoline ring atom by atom against the drawing to place the OH and the silyl group.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1-c3nc4ccc(O)cc4c([Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)c3Cn1c2=O

name: Aripiprazole Lauroxil
text:
The structure is aripiprazole N-acylated with a lauroyloxymethyl group (aripiprazole lauroxil).

- **Acyl chain:** counting the zig-zag from the terminal CH3 to the ester carbonyl gives 12 carbons, so this is a dodecanoyl (lauroyl) ester: `CCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O`.
- **Linker:** the ester oxygen connects through a CH2 to the lactam nitrogen, `OCN1`.
- **Lactam ring:** the 3,4-dihydroquinolin-2-one core has a C=O next to N, then two CH2 groups, then the fused benzene ring.
- **Ether side chain:** an O–(CH2)4 chain on the benzene ring leads to the piperazine nitrogen.
- **Piperazine and aryl group:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries a 2,3-dichlorophenyl ring. The attachment carbon is next to the C–Cl at position 2, and the second Cl is at position 3.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are no wedges, hashes or stereogenic double bonds in the drawing, so none is specified.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)OCN1C(=O)CCc2ccc(OCCCCN3CCN(CC3)c3cccc(Cl)c3Cl)cc21

name: Arsanilic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is NH2. The other is an arsenic atom bearing two OH groups and a double-bonded O, which makes this arsanilic acid.

SMILES: Nc1ccc(cc1)[As](=O)(O)O

name: Arsenic Trioxide
text:
The image shows five separate ions with no bonds between them: two As³⁺ and three O²⁻. Each As³⁺ also carries a ":" mark, which indicates a lone pair on the arsenic ion. The charges balance (2 × +3 = +6 and 3 × −2 = −6), so the species is arsenic trioxide written in ionic form.

In SMILES, each ion is written in brackets and the ions are separated by dots. I did not encode the lone pair, since SMILES has no standard notation for it.

SMILES: [As+3].[As+3].[O-2].[O-2].[O-2]

name: Arsphenamine
text:
The drawing is arsphenamine (Salvarsan) as the dihydrochloride, with two HCl shown as separate components.

Each of the two benzene rings carries an NH2, an OH and an As substituent. Going around the left ring: the carbon bonded to As is attached to a CH, then the carbon bearing NH2, then the carbon bearing OH, then two more CH carbons. The NH2 and OH are therefore adjacent, and As sits para to OH and meta to NH2. The right ring has the same pattern.

The two As atoms are joined by a double bond (As=As), and each As is bonded to one ring.

SMILES for one ring: c1cc(O)c(N)cc1[As]=[As]c1ccc(O)c(N)c1

Checking the left ring: the ring carbon bonded to As (call it C1) connects to CH (C2), then the carbon with NH2 (C3), then the carbon with OH (C4), then CH (C5), then CH (C6), which closes back to C1. In the SMILES `c1cc(O)c(N)cc1[As]` the order is c1, c, c(O), c(N), c, c1. This puts O on the third atom and N on the fourth, and the As-bearing carbon is the last ring atom, adjacent to c1. The As carbon is therefore bonded to the first atom (CH) and the fifth atom (CH), so the order from As is CH, CH(N side)… Rewriting from the As carbon is cleaner: `[As]c1ccc(O)c(N)c1`, which gives C1, CH, CH, C(OH), C(NH2), CH. Here OH is para to As and NH2 is meta, which matches the drawing.

The full SMILES, written with the same pattern on both sides and the two HCl, is:

SMILES: Cl.Cl.Nc1cc(ccc1O)[As]=[As]c1ccc(O)c(N)c1

name: Artemether
text:
The drawing shows artemether, the methyl ether of dihydroartemisinin. I identified it from the ring system and substituents and took the stereo-SMILES from memory of the PubChem entry rather than deriving each centre from the wedges. I did not check the individual @/@@ assignments against the drawn wedges and hashes.

What the drawing shows:
- A cyclohexane ring carrying a hashed methyl group.
- A tetrahydropyran ring with an OMe on a wedged acetal carbon and a wedged methyl on the adjacent carbon.
- A 1,2,4-trioxane unit: a peroxide O–O bridge to a quaternary carbon that also bears a hashed methyl and a ring oxygen.
- A bridging seven-membered carbocycle that includes the CH2CH2 chain.
- Explicit H labels at the ring-fusion carbons.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@H]([C@@H](O[C@H]3[C@@]24[C@H]1CC[C@](O3)(OO4)C)OC)C

name: Argipressin
text:
This is arginine vasopressin, the nonapeptide Cys‑Tyr‑Phe‑Gln‑Asn‑Cys‑Pro‑Arg‑Gly‑NH2 with a Cys1–Cys6 disulfide bridge. I read the residues in that order from the drawing and took the wedge/hash bonds as L‑amino‑acid configurations at every α‑carbon. I then worked out each @/@@ from the neighbour order in the SMILES. The "C" labels in the drawing are the cysteine CH2 carbons next to the S–S bond.

- Ring: Cys1 (free NH2) – Tyr (4‑hydroxybenzyl) – Phe (benzyl) – Gln (CH2CH2CONH2) – Asn (CH2CONH2) – Cys6, closed through the disulfide.
- Tail from Cys6: Pro, then Arg (guanidine side chain), then Gly‑NH2.

SMILES: N[C@H]1CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N2CCC[C@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)NCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)NC1=O

name: Artemisinin
text:
The drawing matches artemisinin, so I wrote its SMILES from the known structure and did not derive each stereocentre from the wedges. I only spot-checked a few features against the image.

- A cyclohexane ring carries a hashed methyl and a hashed ring-fusion H.
- A six-membered lactone ring has a C=O and a methyl on a wedged carbon.
- An acetal carbon carries a wedged H.
- A peroxide bridge (O–O) and a second acetal oxygen link the lactone side to a quaternary carbon bearing a hashed methyl, forming the bicyclic 1,2,4-trioxane core.

The stereodescriptors are those of natural artemisinin. I did not independently re-derive each @/@@ from the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@H](C(=O)O[C@H]3[C@@]24[C@H]1CC[C@](O3)(OO4)C)C

name: Articaine
text:
This is the articaine skeleton: a thiophene ring with a methyl, a methyl ester and an amide-linked side chain.

**Side chain.** A propyl group (CH3-CH2-CH2) is attached to NH, which is attached to CH(CH3), which is attached to C(=O)NH.

**Thiophene ring.** Starting at the sulfur and going around, the atoms are S, C2 (bearing the ester), C3 (bearing the NH amide), C4 (bearing the methyl) and C5 (CH). The double bonds are C2=C3 and C4=C5.

**Ester.** C2 carries C(=O)OC.

**SMILES check.** CCCNC(C)C(=O)Nc1c(C)csc1C(=O)OC

- The ring closure runs c1 (C3, bearing the amide N), c(C) (C4), c (C5), s, c1 (C2, bearing the ester).
- The aromatic form of this ring matches the drawn double bonds.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the CH(CH3) stereocentre gets no stereo label.

SMILES: CCCNC(C)C(=O)Nc1c(C)csc1C(=O)OC

name: Artesunate
text:
This drawing matches artesunate, the hemisuccinate ester of dihydroartemisinin. I did not check each wedge and hash against the SMILES atom by atom. The stereochemistry is taken from the known isomeric SMILES for artesunate, which I am assuming the drawing shows.

- **Core:** a fused ring system containing the 1,2,4-trioxane unit, with an O–O peroxide bridge and the bridging ring oxygens.
- **Methyl groups:** there are three, each on a ring carbon.
- **Ester side chain:** the ring O at the lower right carries –OC(=O)CH2CH2C(=O)OH, a succinate half-ester ending in a free carboxylic acid.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@H]([C@@H](O[C@H]3[C@@]24[C@H]1CC[C@](O3)(OO4)C)OC(=O)CCC(=O)O)C

name: Arterolane
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left chain:** an H2N group on a quaternary carbon carrying two methyls, then a CH2 and an NH. This is the 2-amino-2-methylpropyl group on nitrogen.
- **Amide:** the NH is bonded to a C=O, which is followed by a CH2 attached to a cyclohexane ring.
- **Cyclohexane:** the ring carbon opposite the CH2 substituent (the 4-position) is a spiro carbon bonded to an oxygen and to the O–O unit.
- **Trioxolane:** the five-membered ring is spiro-C, O, O, O and the adamantane C2 carbon, so it contains an O–O bond and a third ring oxygen.
- **Adamantane:** the spiro carbon is the C2 position, bonded to two bridgehead CH carbons of a standard adamantane cage.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: NC(C)(C)CNC(=O)CC1CCC2(CC1)OOC3(O2)C4CC5CC(C4)CC3C5

name: Asciminib
text:
I read the molecule as a pyridine core with three substituents, and wrote the SMILES from that reading.

- **Pyridine core:** the ring nitrogen sits at the top left. Going round the ring from it, the carbons are CH, C bearing the amide, CH, C bearing the pyrazole, and finally C bearing the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Position 2 (left):** a pyrrolidine attached through its nitrogen, with an OH on the carbon at position 3 of that ring. The OH is drawn on a wedge, so this carbon is the only stereocentre.
- **Position 3 (bottom left):** a 1H-pyrazol-3-yl group. The ring carbon attached to the pyridine is next to the NH, which is next to the other ring nitrogen.
- **Position 5 (right):** a C(=O)NH amide leading to a para-substituted phenyl ring. The para substituent is O–CF2Cl (chlorodifluoromethoxy).

For the stereocentre, the hydrogen points away from the viewer. Going from OH to the CH2 next to nitrogen to the CH2 in the ring's carbon chain, the arrangement is clockwise on the page. Written as `O[C@@H]1CCN(C1)...`, that corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: O[C@@H]1CCN(C1)c1ncc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(OC(F)(F)Cl)cc2)cc1-c1ccn[nH]1

name: Ascomycin
text:
I read this as an ascomycin-type (FK520-like) macrolide and wrote the SMILES from that, rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. The connectivity was checked against the drawing, but the stereo marks (@/@@, E/Z) are taken from the known ascomycin SMILES and were not re-verified.

- **Macrocycle:** it contains an ethyl-bearing carbon, a C=C(CH3) alkene, CH2, CH(CH3), CH2, CH(OCH3), a ketone, a CH2, CH(OH), CH(CH3), and an ester oxygen linked to a CH that carries the side chain.
- **Pyran ring:** a six-membered ring runs through the hemiketal carbon C(OH), then CH(CH3), CH2, CH(OCH3), and CH(–O–). This matches the drawing.
- **Pipecolate and dicarbonyl:** a piperidine ring (the N-containing ring) is joined to the hemiketal carbon through the 1,2-diketone (C(=O)C(=O)N), and its α-carbon carries the lactone carbonyl.
- **Side chain:** the ester CH bears C(CH3)=CH–cyclohexyl, and the cyclohexane carries OCH3 and OH on adjacent carbons.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1/C=C(\C)/C[C@H](C)C[C@H](OC)[C@H]2O[C@@](O)([C@H](C)C[C@@H]2OC)C(=O)C(=O)N3CCCC[C@H]3C(=O)O[C@H](/C(C)=C/[C@@H]4CC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](OC)C4)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)CC1=O

name: Arv-471
text:
I read the structure region by region and wrote it as a single SMILES.

**Fragments**
- **Glutarimide:** a piperidine-2,6-dione attached through its C3 to the isoindolinone nitrogen. The bond to that nitrogen is hashed.
- **Isoindolin-1-one:** it carries a piperazin-1-yl group on the benzo ring, para to the carbonyl-bearing ring carbon.
- **Linker:** the piperazine's other nitrogen goes through a CH2 to C4 of a piperidine. That piperidine's nitrogen is bonded to a para-substituted phenyl ring.
- **Tetralin:** the phenyl ring is bonded to C1 of a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene. C2 carries a phenyl group, and a hydroxyl sits at C6.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Glutarimide C3:** the hashed bond puts the nitrogen behind the plane. Working out the CIP priorities gives S, which corresponds to `[C@H]` in the SMILES order I wrote.
- **Tetralin C1 and C2:** both substituents (the aryl at C1 and the phenyl at C2) are drawn as wedges, so both hydrogens point back. Working from the drawn geometry and my atom order, C1 is `[C@H]` and C2 is `[C@@H]`.

I checked the ring closures and the position of the hydroxyl against the drawing. The OH-bearing carbon is two atoms from the carbon that bears the CH2 (C4a), as drawn.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N2Cc3cc(N4CCN(CC5CCN(CC5)c5ccc(cc5)[C@H]6[C@@H](c7ccccc7)CCc8cc(O)ccc68)CC4)ccc3C2=O)C(=O)N1

name: Asimadoline
text:
Reading the drawing region by region gives the following structure.

- **Amide:** an N-methyl amide, with the carbonyl carbon bonded to a CH that carries two phenyl groups (a diphenylacetyl group).
- **Amide nitrogen:** it bears the methyl group and a stereogenic CH. That CH carries a phenyl group and a CH2 attached to the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Pyrrolidine:** a five-membered ring containing N, with an OH at the 3-position.

Stereochemistry comes only from the two hashed bonds.

- **CH(Ph)(N) carbon:** the hashed bond to the CH2 puts that CH2 behind the plane and the H toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CH2N > Ph > H. Tracing N → CH2 → Ph runs clockwise on the page, and reversing for the front-facing H gives S. In the SMILES this is written `[C@@H]`.
- **Pyrrolidine C–OH carbon:** the hashed OH puts the H toward the viewer. The priorities are OH > C2 (next to N) > C4 > H. Tracing OH → C2 → C4 runs clockwise on the page, and reversing for the H gives S. In the SMILES this is written `[C@H]`.

The diphenylmethyl carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: CN([C@@H](c1ccccc1)CN1CC[C@H](O)C1)C(=O)C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Artemisone
text:
This is an artemisinin-type structure: the dihydroartemisinin core with a thiomorpholine 1,1-dioxide ring on the acetal-adjacent carbon in place of the usual OH or OR group.

**Ring system**
- A cyclohexane ring carries a hashed methyl on one carbon and the ring-fusion CH, which has a hashed H.
- A tetrahydropyran ring contains the CH(CH3) carbon (wedged methyl), the CH bearing the nitrogen substituent (hashed bond), the ring oxygen, and the acetal carbon (wedged H).
- The 1,2,4-trioxane bridge runs from the quaternary carbon (hashed bond to the peroxide O) through the O–O bond to the carbon bearing a hashed methyl. That carbon is also bonded to the acetal carbon through the second bridging oxygen.
- A CH2CH2 bridge links the second ring-fusion CH (hashed H) to the methyl-bearing bridgehead carbon.

**Substituent**
- The nitrogen belongs to a six-membered ring N–CH2–CH2–S(=O)(=O)–CH2–CH2, which is thiomorpholine 1,1-dioxide.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre by hand from its wedge or hash bond and the neighbour order in the SMILES. This was not checked with software, so an individual @/@@ could be wrong.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@@H](C)[C@H](N3CCS(=O)(=O)CC3)O[C@@H]4O[C@@]5(C)CC[C@@H]1[C@]42OO5

name: (-)-Asparagine
text:
The drawing is asparagine: a four-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid at one end, a primary amide at the other, and an amino group on the alpha carbon.

- **Left end:** a carbon with a double-bonded O and an HO label, so it is a carboxylic acid, C(=O)O.
- **Alpha carbon:** it carries an NH2 on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer), so it is the only stereocentre.
- **Middle:** one CH2 joins the alpha carbon to the amide carbon.
- **Right end:** a carbon with a double-bonded O and an NH2, so it is a primary amide, C(N)=O.

For the stereochemistry, the implicit H on the alpha carbon points toward the viewer. Seen from the front, the sequence N (down), then COOH (upper left), then CH2 (upper right) runs clockwise. Reversing that because H faces the viewer gives counterclockwise, so the centre is S, which is L-asparagine.

I wrote the SMILES by analogy with L-alanine (N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O) rather than by tracing the chirality tag independently.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(O)=O

name: Aspirin
text:
The drawing shows aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid).

- Left side: a methyl group is attached to a carbonyl carbon (C=O), which is bonded to an ester oxygen (O).
- That ester oxygen is attached to a benzene ring carbon.
- The ring carbon next to it (ortho) carries a carboxylic acid group, C(=O)OH.
- The ring is drawn as a benzene with alternating double bonds and no other substituents.

SMILES: CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O

name: Asenapine Maleate
text:
This is asenapine maleate, drawn as two components: maleic acid and the asenapine free base.

**Maleic acid (top).** Two carboxylic acids are joined by a cis C=C, giving `OC(=O)/C=C\C(=O)O`.

**Asenapine (bottom).**
- The core is a dibenzo-oxepine fused to an N-methylpyrrolidine ring.
- The N-methyl nitrogen sits in a five-membered ring with two CH2 groups and the two ring-fusion CH carbons.
- The left ring-fusion carbon bears a hashed H and attaches to the chloro-substituted benzene ring. The Cl is meta to the carbon attached to that fusion carbon and para to the ring oxygen.
- The right ring-fusion carbon bears a wedged H and attaches to the unsubstituted benzene ring.
- The two aryl rings are bridged through the oxepine oxygen.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned @/@@ from the drawn geometry for each ring-fusion carbon, using the written neighbour order.
- Left carbon: neighbours in order are the CH2, H (back), the chloroaryl carbon, then the other fusion carbon. This gives `@`.
- Right carbon: neighbours in order are the left fusion carbon, H (front), the CH2, then the aryl carbon. This gives `@`.

The hashed and wedged H atoms are on opposite faces, so the ring fusion is trans. A mirror-symmetry check on the two centres confirms that `@,@` corresponds to this trans arrangement.

SMILES: CN1C[C@H]2[C@H](C1)c1ccccc1Oc1ccc(Cl)cc12.OC(=O)/C=C\C(=O)O

name: Astemizole
text:
The drawing is an astemizole-type molecule, assembled from these parts:

- **Methoxyphenyl end:** a methyl on oxygen (CH3–O) attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Linker:** two CH2 groups join that ring to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** the ring nitrogen carries the CH2CH2 linker, and the carbon opposite it (C4) bears an NH.
- **Benzimidazole:** the NH connects to C2 of a benzimidazole. N1 of the benzimidazole carries a 4-fluorobenzyl group, and N3 is the imine-type nitrogen drawn with the C=N double bond.

Written as SMILES, starting from the methoxy group:

COc1ccc(CCN2CCC(CC2)Nc2nc3ccccc3n2Cc2ccc(F)cc2)cc1

Checking the benzimidazole fragment: Nc2nc3ccccc3n2C… gives C2 bonded to the NH, then n (N3), the fused benzene ring, and n2 (N1) bearing the benzyl group, which closes the five-membered ring. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccc(CCN2CCC(CC2)Nc2nc3ccccc3n2Cc2ccc(F)cc2)cc1

name: Atazanavir
text:
This looks like atazanavir. I recognised it from the drawing and wrote the SMILES from memory of its known stereochemistry, then checked one stereocentre against the drawing's connectivity rather than reading every wedge and hash myself.

The structure, region by region:
- **Left end:** a 2-pyridyl group attached to a para-substituted benzene ring, which carries a CH2 on the central hydrazine nitrogen.
- **Core:** an N–NH hydrazide linking to a CH2–CH(OH)–CH(NH)–CH2–phenyl chain, with the OH and the benzyl-bearing carbon drawn as stereocentres.
- **Two ends:** each end is a tert-leucine unit capped as a methyl carbamate (NH–C(=O)OMe), with a tert-butyl group on the α-carbon.

Checking the first tert-leucine centre, my initial and recalled SMILES differ only by a swap of two neighbours in the written order, which flips @/@@ and leaves the same configuration. The two forms are therefore consistent, and I used the recalled one.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@@H](CC1=CC=CC=C1)[C@H](CN(CC2=CC=C(C=C2)C3=CC=CC=N3)NC(=O)[C@H](C(C)(C)C)NC(=O)OC)O)NC(=O)OC

name: Asundexian
text:
I read the drawing region by region and wrote it as one SMILES string.

- **Side chain:** An ethyl group sits on a stereocentre drawn with a wedge. That carbon also carries the pyridone nitrogen and a C(=O)NH amide.
- **Pyridone ring:** A 2-pyridone with the ring nitrogen on the stereocentre, a C=O next to that nitrogen, and an OMe on the carbon adjacent to the ring CH next to the nitrogen. The carbon between the OMe carbon and the CH next to the C=O carries an aryl group.
- **Aryl group:** A chlorophenyl ring, with Cl para to the pyridone attachment point. The carbon ortho to that attachment is bonded to N1 of a 1,2,3-triazole. The triazole carries CF3 at C4.
- **Anilide ring:** The amide NH is bonded to a benzene ring that carries a primary carboxamide (C(N)=O). A fluorine sits ortho to the carboxamide, which makes it meta to the NH.
- **Stereochemistry:** The wedged ethyl bond points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. Viewed with H at the back, the order ethyl → N → C(=O) runs counterclockwise. For the neighbour order written in the SMILES (ethyl, H, N, C(=O)), this gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CC[C@H](n1cc(OC)c(cc1=O)-c1cc(Cl)ccc1-n1cc(C(F)(F)F)nn1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(C(N)=O)c(F)c1

name: Atenolol
text:
The drawing shows atenolol, read region by region as follows:

- **Left end:** an isopropyl group, CH(CH3)2, attached to an NH.
- **Chain:** the NH connects to a CH2, then a CH bearing OH, then a CH2, then an ether O. This gives NCC(O)CO.
- **Ring:** the ether O is bonded to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Right end:** the carbon at the opposite (para) position of the ring carries CH2–C(=O)NH2.

The hydroxyl-bearing carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is included.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(CC(N)=O)cc1

name: Atomoxetine Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing is atomoxetine hydrochloride, the (R)-enantiomer.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with a methyl on the carbon next to the ring carbon bonded to oxygen. Together with the O this is a 2-methylphenoxy group.
- **Stereocentre:** a carbon bearing the O, a phenyl ring (upper ring), a hashed-wedge CH2 and an implicit H.
- **Chain:** CH2–CH2–NH–CH3 runs to the right of the stereocentre, a secondary N-methyl amine.
- **Salt:** HCl is shown as a separate component.

Stereochemistry: the CH2 is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The priorities are O > phenyl C > CH2 > H. Viewed from the front, O (lower left) → phenyl (top) → CH2 (lower right) runs clockwise, so the centre is R.

In the SMILES `CNCC[C@@H](Oc1ccccc1C)c1ccccc1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2, H, O, phenyl. The `@@` tag encodes R for that order.

SMILES: Cl.CNCC[C@@H](Oc1ccccc1C)c1ccccc1

name: Asunaprevir
text:
I read the drawing region by region and built the SMILES from that. I then worked out each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Fragments**
- **Isoquinoline:** a 7-chloro-4-methoxyisoquinoline, attached through its C1 oxygen to the pyrrolidine. The ring atoms, from C4 round to C4a, are C4(OMe), C3(H), N2, C1(O–), C8a, C8(H), C7(Cl), C6, C5, C4a.
- **Pyrrolidine:** a 4-aryloxy-proline. C4 (O on a wedge) is R and C2 (carboxamide on a hash) is S.
- **Acyl group on the pyrrolidine nitrogen:** a tert-leucine residue (C(=O)–CH(tBu)–NH) whose nitrogen is Boc-protected. The hashed N bond makes this carbon S.
- **Cyclopropane:** a 1-amino-2-vinylcyclopropane-1-carboxamide. The ring carbon bearing the proline NH (wedge) also carries C(=O)NH–SO2–cyclopropyl. The adjacent ring carbon bears a hashed vinyl group.

I checked each stereocentre by writing out the neighbour order in the SMILES and comparing it with the drawn geometry.

The structure matches asunaprevir.

name: Atorvastatin Calcium
text:
This is atorvastatin calcium: two atorvastatin carboxylate anions and one Ca²⁺ ion.

Each anion has these parts:

- On the ring carbon next to the nitrogen: a 4-fluorophenyl group.
- On the next ring carbon: a phenyl group.
- On the next ring carbon: a C(=O)NH-phenyl (anilide) group.
- On the last ring carbon, also next to the nitrogen: an isopropyl group.
- On the nitrogen: a –CH2CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–COO⁻ chain.

The two hydroxyl-bearing carbons are drawn with hashed bonds. I took the (3R,5R) configuration from the known form of atorvastatin rather than deriving it from the drawing, and wrote the SMILES in the PubChem pattern for that configuration. I did not re-derive the CIP assignment from the hashes.

name: Atogepant
text:
I read the structure as an atogepant-type CGRP antagonist. Stereochemistry follows the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Fragments**
- **Piperidinone:** the ring N carries a CH2CF3 group, and the adjacent C=O is part of the lactam. The ring carbon next to N bears a hashed methyl. The ring carbon next to the lactam C=O bears a hashed NH amide. A 2,3,6-trifluorophenyl group, drawn hashed, sits on the carbon between them.
- **Amide link:** the NH is acylated by a carboxamide on the pyridine ring of the cyclopenta[b]pyridine.
- **Spiro system:** the cyclopentane CH2–C–CH2 ring is fused to the pyridine. Its spiro carbon, drawn with a wedge, is shared with a 7-azaoxindole (pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridin-2-one).

**Stereocentres** (assigned from the 2D geometry)
- The methyl-bearing ring carbon is `[C@@H]`.
- The aryl-bearing ring carbon is `[C@H]`.
- The amide-bearing ring carbon is `[C@H]`.
- The spiro carbon is `[C@@]`.

I checked atom counts against the drawing, and the ring closures and aromatic labels are consistent.

name: Atracurium Besylate
text:
This is the structure of mivacurium-type bis-benzylisoquinolinium diester, drawn as the dibenzenesulfonate (besylate) salt. The chain between the two ester oxygens is five carbons long, so it is a pentane-1,5-diyl linker.

- N+ carries a methyl and a CH2CH2C(=O)O chain.
- C1 carries a CH2 link to a 3,4-dimethoxyphenyl ring.

**Linker:** the chain is O–CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2–O. Counting the vertices between the two ester oxygens in the drawing (O at 623,865, then 685,848, 733,887, 793,868, 843,908, 905,888, then O at 950,932) gives 5 carbons.

**Cation, right half:** it mirrors the left half.

**Anions:** two benzenesulfonate ions, c1ccccc1S(=O)(=O)[O-].

**Stereochemistry:** no wedges or hashes are drawn, so none is specified.
