name: Atorvastatin
text:
The drawing is atorvastatin. Reading the structure region by region:

- **Pyrrole core:** a five-membered ring with one N. Its substituents are an isopropyl group, a phenyl, a 4-fluorophenyl and a C(=O)NH-phenyl (anilide) group.
- **N-substituent:** a chain of CH2, CH2, CH(OH), CH2, CH(OH), CH2, ending in COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** both hydroxyl-bearing carbons are drawn with hashed bonds.
  - At C5, the priorities are OH > C4 > C6 > H. OH, C4, C6 runs counterclockwise on the page. With H toward the viewer, that reverses to clockwise, so C5 is R.
  - At C3, the priorities are OH > C2 > C4 > H. OH, C2, C4 again runs counterclockwise, so C3 is R.
  - The result is (3R,5R). The chirality marks in the SMILES below are the ones I recalled from the PubChem atorvastatin entry, not rederived atom by atom; I checked only that the drawn centres are 3R,5R.

SMILES: CC(C)C1=C(C(=C(N1CC[C@H](C[C@H](CC(=O)O)O)O)C2=CC=C(C=C2)F)C3=CC=CC=C3)C(=O)NC4=CC=CC=C4

name: Atrazine
text:
The drawing shows atrazine, a 1,3,5-triazine ring with three substituents.

- **Ring:** six vertices alternating C and N. The carbon at the top bears Cl. The carbon at the right bears NH–ethyl. The carbon at the lower left bears NH–isopropyl.
- **Chlorine:** attached to the top ring carbon.
- **Right substituent:** NH–CH2–CH3, an ethylamino group.
- **Lower-left substituent:** NH–CH(CH3)2, an isopropylamino group. The CH is drawn with two methyl branches and no stereo marks.

The ring bonds follow the Kekulé pattern drawn in the image: C(Cl)=N, C(NHEt)=N, and C(NHiPr)=N. Writing the ring as c1(Cl)nc(NC(C)C)nc(NCC)n1 gives an aromatic SMILES that matches the connectivity.

SMILES: CCNc1nc(Cl)nc(NC(C)C)n1

name: Aspidospermidine-3-carboxylic acid, 4-(acetyloxy)-6,7-didehydro-15-((2R,4R,6S,8S)-4-(1,1-difluoroethyl)-1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-octahydro-8-(methoxycarbonyl)-2,6-methano-2H-azecino(4,3-b)indol-8-yl)-3-hydroxy-16-methoxy-1-methyl-, methyl ester, (2beta,3beta,4beta,5alpha,12R,19alpha)-
text:
I read this as a vinflunine-type bisindole: a vindoline half joined to a catharanthine-derived half that carries a CF2CH3 group on its piperidine ring. I assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Vindoline half (bottom)**
- The lower ring system is a tetracyclic indoline fused to a cyclohexane and a piperidine ring. It has an N-methyl, an aromatic OMe, an ethyl on a wedge, a hashed OAc, a hashed OH next to a CO2Me group, and a ring C=C.
- Wedged H on the carbon next to the tertiary N, hashed H on the N-CH carbon, and a hashed CH2 on the quaternary carbon fix the stereo in this half.

**Catharanthine-derived half (top)**
- The top half has an indole (NH), a nine-membered azacycle and a piperidine ring bearing CF2CH3 on a wedge.
- The quaternary carbon carries a hashed CO2Me and links the indole C2 to the vindoline aromatic ring.
- It has a wedged H on the ring-fusion CH.

I did not run the SMILES through a checker. I traced the atom count and ring closures by hand against the drawing, and derived each @/@@ from the wedge and hash geometry.

name: Aurate(1-), (2-hydroxy-3-mercapto-1-propanesulfonato(2-))-, sodium (1:1)
text:
The drawing shows three separate species: Au⁺, Na⁺, and an organic anion.

The anion's chain, read left to right, is S⁻–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–S(=O)(=O)–O⁻. The sulfonate sulfur carries two double-bonded oxygens and one O⁻. The CH carbon bears the OH, and the CH2 on the left carries the thiolate S⁻. The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so the CH carbon gets no stereo.

[Au+].[Na+].[S-]CC(O)CS(=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Auranofin
text:
I read this as auranofin: a triethylphosphine gold(I) cation paired with a tetra-O-acetylated 1-thio-glucopyranose thiolate anion.

- **Gold and phosphine:** the drawing shows an Au⁺ ion and a triethylphosphine, P(CC)(CC)CC, drawn as separate species.
- **Sugar ring:** a six-membered pyranose ring with one ring oxygen and five ring carbons.
- **Acetyl groups:** three ring carbons carry OC(=O)C acetates, and the fifth ring carbon carries a CH₂–OC(=O)C acetate.
- **Thiolate:** the anomeric carbon next to the ring oxygen carries S⁻ on a hashed bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedges and hashes on the ring substituents give the stereocentres. I checked the anomeric carbon explicitly against the drawing. With H implicit and toward the viewer, the neighbour order C2, O, S runs counterclockwise from H. In the SMILES neighbour order (C2, H, O, S) that is `@@`, which matches the SMILES below. I did not check the other four centres individually.

name: Avacopan
text:
I read the structure as a piperidine ring with three substituents, and set the two stereocentres from the wedge bonds.

**Piperidine core**
- The ring nitrogen carries a 2-fluoro-6-methylbenzoyl group, C(=O)c1c(C)cccc1F.
- The carbon next to nitrogen (C2) carries a 4-(cyclopentylamino)phenyl group on a wedge bond.
- The next carbon (C3) carries a carboxamide on a wedge bond. Its NH is bonded to a benzene ring that has CF3 and CH3 on adjacent carbons, with CF3 meta and CH3 para to the NH.

**Stereochemistry**
- At C3, the wedged carbonyl carbon points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. From the front, the carbonyl carbon, C2 and C4 run counterclockwise, which gives [C@H] with the neighbour order I wrote.
- At C2, the wedged aryl group points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. From the front, N, C3 and the aryl carbon run counterclockwise, which gives [C@H] with the neighbour order I wrote.

name: Atropine sulfate
text:
This is atropine sulfate: two identical atropine units plus one sulfuric acid, written as three dot-separated fragments.

**Each atropine unit**
- A tropane core: a bicyclic system with an N-methyl bridge, with the 3-position carbon bearing the ester oxygen.
- The ester is O–C(=O)–CH(CH2OH)–phenyl, a tropic acid ester. Its CH is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- The two bridgehead carbons carry explicit H wedges: the top bridgehead has its H wedged up, the bottom one has its H wedged down. I assigned @/@@ from the 2D geometry of those wedges (viewed from the H, the top bridgehead's neighbours run left, right, N clockwise; for the bottom one, N, left, right run counter-clockwise). This gives `[C@@H]2` for the top bridgehead and `[C@H]1` for the bottom one in the SMILES order used below.
- The two units are drawn identically, so they get the same stereo labels.

**Counter-acid:** S(=O)(=O)(OH)2 is written as `OS(=O)(=O)O`.

name: Aurothioglucose
text:
I read the drawing as a gold(I) cation paired with a thiolate on a pyranose ring. This is the aurothioglucose pattern, with S⁻ at the anomeric carbon.

**Connectivity**
- The ring has five carbons and one oxygen.
- The anomeric carbon (C1) carries S⁻, drawn as a wedge.
- C2, C3 and C4 each carry an OH.
- C5 carries a CH2OH group, drawn as a hash.
- Au⁺ is a separate ion.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash, with the implicit H taking the opposite side.

| Ring carbon | Substituent and bond | Tag in SMILES |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | S⁻ wedge | `[C@H]1` |
| C5 | CH2OH hash | `[C@H](CO)` |
| C4 | OH wedge | `[C@@H](O)` |
| C3 | OH hash | `[C@H](O)` |
| C2 | OH wedge | `[C@H]1O` |

I derived these by hand from the 2D geometry, so the @/@@ assignments carry some risk of a slip.

name: Avanafil
text:
The structure is avanafil, read region by region from the drawing.

- **Top left:** a pyrimidin-2-yl ring (N–C–N with three CH) joined through a CH2 to an amide NH.
- **Centre:** a C(=O)NH amide on C5 of a central pyrimidine. This ring carries a benzylamino NH at C4 and a pyrrolidine nitrogen at C2.
- **Bottom left:** a benzene ring bearing the CH2NH linker, a Cl, and an OMe on adjacent carbons, with Cl meta and OMe para to the linker.
- **Right:** a pyrrolidine whose C2 carries a CH2OH on a wedge bond. This is the only stereo-marked atom.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are N, then CH2OH, then the ring CH2, then H. The wedge puts H at the back. Going N → CH2OH → ring CH2 runs counterclockwise in the drawing, so the centre is S. In the SMILES below, `[C@H]` written as `N3CCC[C@H]3CO` encodes S.

SMILES: COc1ccc(CNc2nc(N3CCC[C@H]3CO)ncc2C(=O)NCc2ncccn2)cc1Cl

name: Atosiban
text:
I read this as atosiban: a cyclic peptide with a 3-mercaptopropionic acid (Mpa) disulfide bridge, D-Tyr(Et), Ile, Thr, Asn, Cys, Pro, Orn and Gly-NH2.

**Backbone and side chains**
- The macrocycle runs Mpa (C(=O)CH2CH2–S–S–CH2) to Cys, then Asn, Thr, Ile and D-Tyr(Et), closing back onto the Mpa carbonyl.
- The D-Tyr side chain is a 4-ethoxybenzyl group.
- Off the Cys carbonyl, the tail is Pro, then Orn (free NH2 on a three-carbon chain), then Gly-NH2.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.
- Tyr is D, Ile is L with the side-chain methyl hashed, and Thr is L with its methyl hashed.
- Asn, Cys, Pro and Orn are all L.

I checked that the SMILES is valid and covers every atom in the drawing.

name: Avapritinib
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and joined them.

- **Stereocentre:** a quaternary carbon bearing NH2, a hashed methyl, a 4-fluorophenyl and a pyrimidin-5-yl group.
- **Pyrimidine and piperazine:** the pyrimidine is attached at C2 to one piperazine nitrogen.
- **Core:** the other piperazine nitrogen is attached to C4 of a pyrrolo[2,1-f][1,2,4]triazine.
- **Pyrazole:** the triazine carries a 1-methylpyrazol-4-yl group on the pyrrole carbon.

For the chirality, the methyl is hashed, so it points away from the viewer. The other three substituents then run NH2 (left), aryl (up), pyrimidine (right), which is clockwise in the drawing. In the SMILES the methyl is written first, so I look from the methyl side. From there the order N → aryl → pyrimidine is counterclockwise, which gives `@`.

SMILES: C[C@](N)(c1ccc(F)cc1)c1cnc(nc1)N1CCN(CC1)c1ncnn2cc(cc12)-c1cnn(C)c1

name: Avutometinib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left chain:** a methyl on NH, which is bonded to a sulfonyl S with two =O, then to another NH. This gives CNS(=O)(=O)N.
- **Pyridine:** the NH attaches at C2, which is next to the ring N. C3 carries F. C4 carries the CH2 linker. C5 and C6 are CH, and C6 bonds to N.
- **Coumarin core:** C3 of the coumarin bears the CH2 and C4 bears a methyl. C2 is the lactone C=O, bonded to the ring O. The benzo ring carries an O-pyrimidinyl group at C7, which is the position meta to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to O.

Assembling the SMILES:

CNS(=O)(=O)Nc1nccc(Cc2c(C)c3ccc(Oc4ncccn4)cc3oc2=O)c1F

Checking the pyridine: c1(NHSO2) n c c c(CH2) c1F. The ring atoms are C2, N, C6, C5, C4 and C3 bearing F, which closes back to C2. This is correct.

Checking the coumarin: c2 (C3) c(C) (C4) c3 (C4a) c c c(OPyr) (C7) c c3 (C8a) o c2=O. From C4a, the atoms C5, C6, C7 (bearing the O), C8 and C8a follow, and C8a bonds to the ring O. This matches the drawing, where the O-pyrimidinyl carbon is adjacent to the CH next to C8a.

name: azane;dichloroplatinum
text:
The drawing shows Cl–Pt–Cl in a line, with two separate NH3 labels below. The NH3 groups have no bonds drawn to Pt, so they are disconnected fragments. name: avermectin B1a
Azathioprine
text:
This structure is azathioprine: a purine joined through a sulfur atom to a 1-methyl-4-nitroimidazole.

**Purine part.** The six-membered ring has these atoms in order:
- C6, the carbon attached to S, at (587, 712)
- N1 at (578, 510), double-bonded to C6
- C2 at (398, 420), single-bonded to N1
- N3 at (230, 530), double-bonded to C2
- C4 at (238, 730), single-bonded to N3
- C5 at (418, 822), double-bonded to C4

The five-membered ring continues from C5 to NH, then to C8 at (187, 1052), then to N at (100, 870), which bonds back to C4. The N–C8 bond is double, as drawn, and the NH is attached to C5.

**Imidazole part.** The ring is N1(CH3)–C5(S)=C4(NO2)–N3=C2–N1. The carbon bearing S is double-bonded to the carbon bearing the nitro group. The nitro group is drawn as the charge-separated form, [N+](=O)[O-].

**SMILES, written from the purine C6:**
- C6: `c1(Sc2...)`
- Purine written with explicit bond orders: `S(C1=NC=NC2=C1NC=N2)`
- Imidazole: `C1=C([N+](=O)[O-])N=CN1C`

Putting the two together:

`Cn1cnc([N+](=O)[O-])c1Sc1ncnc2nc[nH]c12`

Check on the aromatic purine: C6 is `c1`, N1 is `n`, C2 is `c`, N3 is `n`, C4 is `c2`, then N9 is `n`, C8 is `c`, N7 is `[nH]`, and C5 is `c12`. C4 is bonded to the plain N, and C5 is bonded to the NH, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1cnc([N+](=O)[O-])c1Sc1ncnc2nc[nH]c12

name: Azamulin
text:
I read this as a dihydropleuromutilin-type skeleton: the usual tricyclic diterpene core, but with an ethyl group where pleuromutilin has a vinyl group. The C14 ester is a (5-amino-1H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thioacetate.

I did not derive the stereo tags atom by atom from the wedges and hashes. I took the known pleuromutilin stereochemistry, which the drawing appears to match, and changed only the vinyl to ethyl and the glycolate OH to the triazolylthio group.

- **Core:** the quaternary carbon carries the ethyl and a wedged methyl. The adjacent hashed CH–OH connects to the CH bearing a wedged methyl, and the five-membered ring ends in the ketone.
- **Ester:** the wedged O–C(=O)–CH2–S chain sits on the ring carbon next to the hashed methyl-bearing carbon.
- **Triazole:** the sulfur-bearing carbon is flanked by N= and N–N(H). The other ring carbon carries NH2 and sits between NH and N=, so the ring is written Sc1n[nH]c(N)n1.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(C)C[C@@H](OC(=O)CSc2n[nH]c(N)n2)[C@@]2(C)[C@H](C)CC[C@@]3(CCC(=O)[C@H]23)[C@H](C)[C@@H]1O

name: Azd-1390
text:
I read the structure as an imidazo[4,5-c]quinolin-2-one core carrying an N-isopropyl, an N-methyl, a fluorine, and a pyridyl ether side chain.

**Core.** The five-membered ring has C(=O) at the top, N-methyl on the left and N-isopropyl on the right. The two fused carbons are C3a (bonded to N-Me) and C9b (bonded to N-iPr). C3a is also bonded to a CH, which is double-bonded to the ring nitrogen (the lower N). That N connects to C4a, which is part of the benzene ring. C9b is bonded to C9a, the other fusion carbon of the benzene ring.

**Benzene ring.** Going around from C9a: C9a, CH, C(pyridyl), C(F), CH, C4a.

**Side chain.** The pyridyl group is attached at its 3-position. The ring nitrogen is adjacent to the carbon bearing the O-CH2CH2CH2-piperidin-1-yl group, which makes this a 2-alkoxypyridin-5-yl substituent.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Core with substituents: O=C1N(C)c2cnc3cc(F)c(cc3c2N1C(C)C)...
- Check of the benzene ring: c3 (C4a) is bonded to n, then cc(F) gives CH then C-F, then c(...) gives the C-pyridyl, then c is the CH, then c3 closes as C9a. C9a is then bonded to c2 (C9b), which carries N1(iPr). This is consistent.
- Pyridyl: c4ccc(OCCCN5CCCCC5)nc4

SMILES: O=C1N(C)c2cnc3cc(F)c(cc3c2N1C(C)C)-c1ccc(OCCCN2CCCCC2)nc1

name: Azacytidine
text:
I read this as azacitidine (5-azacytidine). It has a 1,3,5-triazin-2-one ring carrying an NH2 group, and the ring nitrogen is joined to a ribofuranose.

- **Base:** the ring contains three nitrogens and three carbons. One carbon is a C=O, one carries the NH2, and one is a plain CH between two nitrogens. The ring N bearing the sugar sits between the C=O carbon and the CH.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring of four carbons and one oxygen. The anomeric carbon (C1') bears the ring N on a wedge. The two ring OH groups are on hashed bonds, and the CH2OH on C4' is on a wedge. This is the β-D-ribo arrangement.
- **Stereo SMILES:** I took the known stereo SMILES for azacitidine and rewrote it starting from the amino group. I rechecked each stereocentre's @/@@ against the new neighbour order.

SMILES: Nc1ncn([C@@H]2O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H]2O)c(=O)n1

name: Azelaic Acid
text:
Counting the chain carbons from left to right using the vertex x-positions:

- Carboxyl carbon at x≈257 (C1)
- Vertices at 380, 503, 627, 750, 873, 997 and 1120 (C2 to C8)
- Carboxyl carbon at x≈1245 (C9)

That gives 9 carbons in total, with a COOH group at each end. The molecule is nonanedioic acid (azelaic acid), HOOC-(CH2)7-COOH.

The SMILES has the two carboxyl carbons plus 7 CH2 groups between them: OC(=O)CCCCCCCC(=O)O, which has 7 C's between the carbonyl carbons.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCCCCCC(=O)O

name: Azelnidipine
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine, which looks like an azelnidipine analogue with an NH2 group in place of the usual methyl. I read it region by region.

- **Dihydropyridine ring:** N1(H) is bonded to C2 and C6. C2 carries NH2 and is double-bonded to C3. C3 carries the ester C(=O)O-azetidinyl group. C4 is sp3 and carries the 3-nitrophenyl group. C5 is double-bonded to C6 and carries the isopropyl ester C(=O)OC(C)C. C6 carries a methyl group.
- **Aryl group:** the nitrophenyl is attached at the ring carbon next to the carbon that bears NO2, so the nitro group is meta to the attachment point.
- **Azetidine:** a four-membered ring with N1 bonded to CH(Ph)2, and the 3-position carbon bonded to the ester oxygen.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are drawn plain, so no stereo marks are included.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(N)=C(C(=O)OC2CN(C(c3ccccc3)c3ccccc3)C2)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Azilsartan
text:
This is azilsartan, drawn as the free acid.

**Right side:** A benzimidazole carries an ethoxy group at C2 (CCOC1=N...). N1 is attached to a CH2 that links to the biphenyl. The benzo ring carries a COOH next to N1, at the 7-position.

**Middle and left:** The CH2 is bonded to a para-substituted benzene, which is bonded to a second benzene (the ortho-substituted ring). That ring bears a 1,2,4-oxadiazol-5(4H)-one: C(=NOC(=O)N1) with the NH.

**SMILES construction:**
- Benzimidazole: CCOC1=Nc2cccc(C(=O)O)c2N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1noc(=O)[nH]1
- Checking the drawing: C3 of the oxadiazole is bonded to the aryl group and double-bonded to N, which is bonded to O, then to C(=O), then to NH, which closes back to C3. This matches c1noc(=O)[nH]1.

SMILES: CCOC1=Nc2cccc(C(=O)O)c2N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1C1=NOC(=O)N1

name: Azosemide
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring carrying four substituents, plus a thiophene and a tetrazole.

**Benzene ring.** Going around the ring from the top left carbon:
- The top left carbon bears the tetrazole.
- The top right carbon is CH.
- The right carbon bears the sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)N.
- The bottom right carbon bears Cl.
- The bottom left carbon is CH.
- The left carbon bears the NH.

**Tetrazole.** The carbon is bonded to N (drawn with a double bond), which connects to NH, then to N, then to N, and back to the carbon. The double bonds are C=N (the bottom left N) and N=N (the top N to the right N). The NH sits between the bottom left N and the top N. This is a 2H-tetrazole written as c1nn[nH]n1.

**Side chain.** The ring NH is bonded to CH2, which is bonded to thiophene C2. The thiophene is c1cccs1.

**SMILES.** Written with the ring atoms in order:
- c1(NCc2cccs2) is the ring carbon with the NH side chain.
- c(c2nn[nH]n2) is the next ring carbon, bearing the tetrazole.
- c is the CH.
- c(S(N)(=O)=O) is the sulfonamide carbon.
- c(Cl) is the chlorine carbon.
- c1 is the final CH, which closes the ring.

Result: NS(=O)(=O)c1cc(-c2nn[nH]n2)c(NCc2cccs2)cc1Cl

Checking the ring order: S carbon, then CH, then the tetrazole carbon, then the NH carbon, then CH, then the Cl carbon, which closes back to the S carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1cc(-c2nn[nH]n2)c(NCc2cccs2)cc1Cl

name: Azd8871
text:
I read the structure in four parts and joined them into one SMILES.

1. **Left end:** a 2,2-di(thiophen-2-yl)-2-hydroxyacetate ester, `OC(c1cccs1)(c1cccs1)C(=O)O…`, attached to a cyclohexane ring through the ester oxygen.
2. **Cyclohexane and linker:** the ring is 1,4-disubstituted. Its other carbon carries an N-methyl tertiary amine, which leads into a three-carbon chain, `N(C)CCC`, ending on N1 of a benzotriazole. The ring has no wedges or hashes, so I gave it no stereo.
3. **Benzotriazole:** the CH2NH side chain sits on C5 of the benzo ring, `n1nnc2cc(CN…)ccc12`.
4. **Right end:** the NH-CH2 continues to a CH(OH) stereocentre drawn with a wedge to OH. That carbon bears an 8-hydroxy-2-oxo-1,2-dihydroquinolin-5-yl group, `c3ccc(O)c4[nH]c(=O)ccc34`. Working through the wedge geometry (CH2 upper left, aryl upper right, OH wedged down, H implied behind) gives `[C@H]` for the neighbour order CH2, H, O, aryl.

SMILES: OC(c1cccs1)(c1cccs1)C(=O)OC1CCC(CC1)N(C)CCCn1nnc2cc(CNC[C@H](O)c3ccc(O)c4[nH]c(=O)ccc34)ccc12

name: Azithromycin
text:
I read this as azithromycin, a 15-membered azalide macrolide. I did not check each stereocentre against the wedges and hashes in the drawing. The stereochemistry comes from my recollection of the published azithromycin SMILES, so it is not independently verified.

- **Macrocycle:** a 15-membered lactone ring containing one ring nitrogen, which carries an N-methyl group.
- **Ring substituents:** an ethyl group on the carbon next to the lactone oxygen, several ring methyl groups, and three hydroxyl groups.
- **Sugars:** cladinose (with its methoxy group) on the left and desosamine (with its dimethylamino group) on the upper right, each attached through a glycosidic oxygen.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H](N(C[C@H](C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O1)C)O[C@H]2C[C@@]([C@H]([C@@H](O2)C)O)(C)OC)C)O[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@H](O3)C)N(C)C)O)(C)O)C)C)C)O)(C)O

name: Baclofen
text:
The drawing shows a para-chlorophenyl ring attached to a CH carbon. That carbon carries a CH2NH2 group and a CH2COOH group, so the molecule is baclofen. The bonds are all plain, so I give no stereochemistry.

SMILES: NCC(CC(=O)O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: azaline B
text:
I read the structure as the decapeptide Ac‑D‑2Nal‑D‑4Cl‑Phe‑D‑3Pal‑L‑Ser‑L‑Aph(aminotriazolyl)‑D‑Aph(aminotriazolyl)‑L‑Leu‑L‑Lys(iPr)‑L‑Pro‑D‑Ala‑NH2, which is an azaline B‑type GnRH antagonist. I read it from the N‑terminus to the C‑terminus and assigned each α‑carbon's configuration from its wedge or hash.

**Residues, N‑terminus to C‑terminus**
1. Acetyl cap on the N‑terminus.
2. 2‑Naphthylalanine, hashed CH2, R (D).
3. 4‑Chlorophenylalanine, wedged CH2, R (D).
4. 3‑Pyridylalanine, wedged CH2, R (D).
5. Serine, wedged CH2OH, S (L).
6. Phenylalanine with a para‑NH‑(5‑amino‑1,2,4‑triazol‑3‑yl) group, hashed CH2, S (L).
7. The same aminotriazolyl‑phenylalanine, wedged CH2, R (D).
8. Leucine, wedged isobutyl, S (L).
9. Lysine whose side‑chain nitrogen carries an isopropyl group, hashed chain, S (L).
10. Proline, hashed carbonyl, S (L).
11. Alanine amide (C‑terminal CONH2), wedged methyl, R (D).

I did not re‑parse the final SMILES with a tool; I checked it against the drawing residue by residue.

name: Balaglitazone
text:
The drawing shows three connected parts.

- **Thiazolidine-2,4-dione ring:** S, C(=O), NH, C(=O), and CH, closed as a five-membered ring. The CH carries a CH2 that links to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** para-disubstituted. One substituent is the CH2 from the thiazolidinedione, and the other is an O bonded to a CH2.
- **Quinazolinone:** that CH2 attaches to C2 of a 3-methylquinazolin-4(3H)-one. C2 is double-bonded to N1, N3 carries the methyl, and C4 is the C=O attached to the fused benzene ring.

The stereocentre in the thiazolidinedione ring is drawn with plain bonds, so I assign no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)c2ccccc2N=C1COc1ccc(CC2SC(=O)NC2=O)cc1

SMILES: CN1C(=O)c2ccccc2N=C1COc1ccc(CC2SC(=O)NC2=O)cc1

name: Aztreonam
text:
Reading the drawing, this is aztreonam: a monocyclic β-lactam (azetidinone) carrying an N-sulfonic acid, a 4-methyl group and a 3-acylamino group.

- **Acyl side chain:** the amide carbonyl is attached to a C=N–O oxime. The oxime oxygen carries a C(CH3)2–COOH group, and the carbon is also bonded to the 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring.
- **Ring stereocentres:** the methyl-bearing carbon has a wedge bond (toward the viewer) and the amide-bearing carbon has a hashed bond (away from the viewer). Working through the neighbour order gives `C[C@H]1[C@H](N…)C(=O)N1…`.
- **Oxime geometry:** the oxime oxygen sits on the same side of the C=N bond as the amide carbonyl, which is the Z isomer. This is written `C(=O)/C(=N\O…)`.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@H](NC(=O)/C(=N\OC(C)(C)C(=O)O)c2csc(N)n2)C(=O)N1S(=O)(=O)O

name: Bacampicillin
text:
I read this as bacampicillin, the 1-(ethoxycarbonyloxy)ethyl ester of ampicillin.

- **Core:** a penicillin bicyclic core (β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine) with a gem-dimethyl carbon next to the sulfur.
- **Side chain:** a phenylglycine amide, with the NH₂ drawn on a hashed bond.
- **Ester:** the carboxylate is esterified with CH(CH₃)–O–C(=O)–O–CH₂CH₃, and that CH carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so I left it without stereo.

For stereochemistry I assumed the natural penicillin configuration (2S,5R,6R) with the D (R) phenylglycine, which matches the wedges and hashes as I read them. I then checked each centre's CIP assignment against the SMILES. My first recalled SMILES had the wrong chirality at the carbon bearing the carboxylate ester (it came out R), so I corrected it to S.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)OC(C)OC(=O)[C@@H]1N2[C@H](SC1(C)C)[C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)[C@H](N)c1ccccc1

name: Bambuterol
text:
This is bambuterol: a benzene ring carrying two O–C(=O)N(CH3)2 carbamate groups at the 3 and 5 positions and a CH(OH)CH2NH–C(CH3)3 side chain at position 1.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- Top right: the dimethylamino carbamate N(C)C–C(=O)–O is attached to the ring.
- Bottom right: a second, identical carbamate O–C(=O)N(C)C is attached to the ring.
- Left: the ring carbon bears CH(OH)–CH2–NH–C(CH3)3, a tert-butylamino side chain.
- The CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=O)Oc1cc(cc(c1)OC(=O)N(C)C)C(O)CNC(C)(C)C

name: Balapiravir
text:
I read this as 4'-azidocytidine with all three sugar hydroxyls esterified as isobutyrates (a tri-isobutyrate prodrug).

**Reading the drawing**
- The base is cytosine, with the ring N1 attached to the sugar. C4 carries NH2 and C2 carries the C=O.
- The sugar is a five-membered ring made of one oxygen and four carbons.
- The sugar carbon next to the ring oxygen, C1', bears the cytosine on a bold wedge.
- The quaternary carbon C4' bears an azide drawn as N=N⁺=N⁻ on a plain bond. Its CH2–O–isobutyrate group is on a bold wedge.
- C3' and C2' each carry an O–isobutyrate on a hashed bond. Each isobutyrate is O–C(=O)–CH(CH3)2.

**Stereo assignment**
I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash and the 2D positions of its neighbours, giving C4' as @@, C1' as @@, C2' as @ and C3' as @@ in the SMILES order below. I did this by hand and did not run it through a toolkit to confirm.

SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)OC[C@@]1(N=[N+]=[N-])O[C@@H](n2ccc(N)nc2=O)[C@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@@H]1OC(=O)C(C)C

name: Bamifylline
text:
The drawing shows a xanthine (purine-2,6-dione) core with the following substituents:

- **Benzyl group:** a CH2 links the phenyl ring to C8, the imidazole carbon between the two ring nitrogens.
- **N7 substituent:** the imidazole nitrogen on the right carries CH2CH2N(CH2CH3)(CH2CH2OH).
- **Methyl groups:** the two ring nitrogens on the left (N1 and N3) each carry a methyl.
- **Carbonyls:** both ring C=O groups sit on the six-membered ring.

Reading around the rings:

- The six-membered ring is N(Me)–C(=O)–N(Me)–C(=O)–C5=C4, with C4 bonded to the first N(Me).
- The imidazole ring is C4–N=C8(Bn)–N7(R)–C5.

Written as SMILES, the lower-left N(Me) is N3 and bonds to C4 and to a C2=O. The other N(Me), at the bottom, is N1 and bonds to C2 and to C6=O. C6 bonds to C5.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)N(C)C(=O)c2c1nc(Cc1ccccc1)n2CCN(CC)CCO

name: Baricitinib
text:
This is baricitinib. I read it in four parts.

- **Ethylsulfonyl group:** CH3-CH2-S(=O)(=O)- is attached to the azetidine nitrogen.
- **Azetidine ring:** a four-membered ring made of N, CH2, a quaternary C and CH2. The quaternary carbon carries the CH2C#N group and the pyrazole nitrogen.
- **Pyrazole:** N1 is bonded to the azetidine carbon, N2 is the double-bonded nitrogen, then C3H, then C4, which bears the bicyclic substituent, then C5H.
- **Pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine:** the pyrimidine carbon attached to the pyrazole is bonded to the ring N and to the fused carbon. The fused pyrrole ring has NH, CH=CH, and the two shared carbons.

SMILES for the ring atoms, written in order:

- Ethyl: CC
- Sulfonyl: S(=O)(=O)
- Azetidine: N1CC(CC#N)(C1)
- Pyrazole: n1cc(cn1)
- Bicyclic system: c1ncnc2[nH]ccc12

Check of the bicyclic part: the carbon attached to the pyrazole is c1, bonded to n (the N at the top), then c (CH), then n, then c2 (the fused carbon bonded to NH), then [nH], c, c, and the fused carbon c12 closing back to c1. This matches the drawing.

Full SMILES: CCS(=O)(=O)N1CC(CC#N)(C1)n1cc(cn1)-c1ncnc2[nH]ccc12

SMILES: CCS(=O)(=O)N1CC(CC#N)(C1)n1cc(cn1)-c1ncnc2[nH]ccc12

name: Barium Sulfate
text:
The drawing shows a sulfate group and a barium ion as separate components.

- **Sulfate:** a central S with two double-bonded O atoms (neutral) and two single-bonded O⁻ atoms.
- **Barium:** a separate Ba²⁺ ion, not bonded to the sulfate.

The charges balance: two O⁻ give −2 and Ba²⁺ gives +2.

SMILES: [Ba+2].[O-]S(=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Baloxavir Marboxil
text:
I read the structure as an isomer of baloxavir marboxil, with the sulfur and the CH2 swapped between the two benzo rings.

- **Side chain:** a methyl carbonate on an O–CH2–O link, COC(=O)OCO–, attached to a pyridone ring carbon.
- **Pyridone core:** a pyridone ring carrying a C=O, fused through N–N to a triazinone ring. That ring carries a second C=O and is fused to a morpholine ring through a stereocentre.
- **Morpholine stereocentre:** the H is drawn as a wedge. Working through the neighbour order gives `[C@H]` in my SMILES.
- **Tricyclic part:** the dibenzo-thiepine CH is attached to the ring N by a hashed bond, which gives `[C@@H]`. The CH sits between the two benzo rings.
- **Sulfur and CH2:** the unsubstituted benzo ring carries the S. The 3,4-difluorobenzo ring carries the CH2.

SMILES: COC(=O)OCOC1=C2C(=O)N3CCOC[C@H]3N(N2C=CC1=O)[C@@H]1c2ccccc2SCc2c(F)c(F)ccc12

name: Barnidipine
text:
This is benidipine, a dihydropyridine bearing a 3-nitrophenyl group at C4, a methyl ester at C3, and a 1-benzylpyrrolidin-3-yl ester at C5. I read it from the drawing as follows:

- **Dihydropyridine ring:** an NH ring with methyl groups on both carbons next to nitrogen (C2 and C6), and a C3=C2 and C5=C6 double-bond pattern.
- **C3 substituent:** a methyl ester, C(=O)OC.
- **C5 substituent:** an ester C(=O)O linked to C3 of an N-benzylpyrrolidine ring.
- **C4 substituent:** a 3-nitrophenyl group with the nitro as [N+](=O)[O-], attached by a hashed bond.

Stereochemistry, assigned from the two stereo bonds in the drawing:

- **C4 of the dihydropyridine:** the aryl bond is hashed (pointing away), so the implicit H points toward the viewer. This gives `[C@H]` in the neighbour order C5, H, C3, aryl.
- **C3 of the pyrrolidine:** the C–O bond is a wedge (toward the viewer), so the implicit H points away. This gives `[C@@H]` in the neighbour order O, H, ring CH2 (C4), ring CH2 (C2, next to N).

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)O[C@@H]2CCN(Cc3ccccc3)C2)[C@H]1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Batefenterol
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and joined them into one SMILES.

- **Left end:** a biphenyl-2-yl group on a carbamate NH, written `O=C(Nc1ccccc1-c1ccccc1)O-`, with the carbamate oxygen on C4 of a piperidine.
- **Linker:** the piperidine nitrogen carries a CH2CH2C(=O)NH chain that leads to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** going round from the amide NH, the substituents are Cl, H, CH2NH, OMe, H.
- **Right end:** the CH2NH continues to CH2–CH(OH), and that carbon is attached to C5 of an 8-hydroxy-quinolin-2(1H)-one.

The only wedge is the OH on the CH(OH) carbon. Its priorities are OH > CH2N > aryl > H, with H pointing away from the viewer. The OH → CH2N → aryl sequence runs clockwise, so the centre is R. In the SMILES order I wrote (CH2, H, O, aryl), that corresponds to `[C@H]`.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccccc1-c1ccccc1)OC1CCN(CC1)CCC(=O)Nc1cc(OC)c(CNC[C@H](O)c2ccc(O)c3[nH]c(=O)ccc23)cc1Cl

name: Bacitracin
text:
I read this as a bacitracin-type cyclic peptide, and wrote the SMILES by following the backbone residue by residue.

**Residues, in order from the free amine at the lower left:**
1. An N-terminal isoleucine-derived unit whose carbonyl is cyclised into a thiazoline ring (S, C=N, CH2, CH). It carries a free NH2 and a sec-butyl group.
2. Leucine (isobutyl side chain).
3. Glutamic acid (CH2CH2COOH side chain).
4. Isoleucine.
5. Lysine, whose side chain is four CH2 groups (the four labelled "C" in the ring) ending in an amide NH.
6. Ornithine, with a free CH2CH2CH2NH2 side chain.
7. Isoleucine.
8. Phenylalanine.
9. Histidine (imidazole ring).
10. Aspartic acid (CH2COOH side chain).
11. Asparagine (CH2CONH2 side chain).

**Macrocycle:** the lysine side-chain NH acylates the asparagine carbonyl. The ring then runs Asn → Asp → His → Phe → Ile → Orn and closes onto the lysine carbonyl.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash and the positions of its neighbours in the drawing. I did not independently re-check each assignment, so the chirality tags are the least certain part.

SMILES: N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C1=N[C@@H](CS1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCNC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@@H](CC(=O)O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1cnc[nH]1)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@@H](CCCN)N%10)C%10=O

name: Barusiban
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocyclic peptide-like ring with an N-methyl amino-alcohol tail. I traced the ring atom by atom and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Tail.** An amino-alcohol chain H2N-CH2CH2CH2-CH(CH2OH)-N(CH3) is attached through the nitrogen to the ring carbonyl.

**Ring, traced clockwise from that carbonyl.**
1. The carbonyl C(=O) is bonded to the first ring stereocentre (hashed bond).
2. From that stereocentre the ring continues CH2, CH2, S, CH2, CH2, then a carbonyl C(=O).
3. That carbonyl is followed by NH and the tryptophan α-carbon, which carries a CH2–indol-3-yl side chain (hashed bond), then C(=O) and NH.
4. Next comes an isoleucine-type residue. Its α-carbon has a wedged N bond and its side-chain CH has a hashed methyl; it is followed by C(=O) and NH.
5. A second isoleucine-type residue follows. Its α-carbon has a wedged N bond and its side-chain CH has a wedged methyl; it is followed by C(=O) and NH.
6. An asparagine-type residue follows. Its α-carbon has a wedged CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain (wedged bond), then C(=O) and NH.
7. That last NH closes the ring back onto the first stereocentre.

**Stereochemistry.** I worked out each centre from the 2D geometry, treating the implicit hydrogen as pointing opposite the wedge or hash. This gives the @/@@ marks in the SMILES below.

SMILES: NCCC[C@@H](CO)N(C)C(=O)[C@@H]1CCSCCC(=O)N[C@H](Cc2c[nH]c3ccccc23)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N1

name: Bazedoxifene
text:
The drawing is bazedoxifene: an indole core with a 4-hydroxyphenyl at C2, a methyl at C3, and a hydroxyl at C5. The indole nitrogen carries a benzyl group, and that benzene ring bears a para O–CH2CH2–N-azepane chain.

Reading the regions:
- **Azepane ring:** the nitrogen and six CH2 carbons make a seven-membered ring, N1CCCCCC1.
- **Indole core:** N1 is bonded to C2, which carries the 4-hydroxyphenyl. C3 carries the methyl and is bonded to C3a. C3a connects to C4, then C5 (bearing OH), C6, C7, and C7a, which closes back to N1.
- **Benzyl linker:** the N–CH2 group leads to a para-substituted benzene ring whose far carbon bears the O–CH2CH2–N chain.

Checking the ring placement of the OH: C3a is bonded to a CH (C4), which is bonded to the C–OH (C5), then CH (C6) and CH (C7), then C7a (bonded to N). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1c(-c2ccc(O)cc2)n(Cc2ccc(OCCN3CCCCCC3)cc2)c2ccc(O)cc12

name: Baxdrostat
text:
I read the drawing as a propanamide on a chiral carbon of a tetrahydroisoquinoline, which carries a 1-methyl-3,4-dihydroquinolin-2-one substituent.

- **Left side:** an ethyl group (CH3–CH2) on a C=O, bonded to an N–H. This is a propanamide, CCC(=O)N.
- **Stereocentre:** the N–H is attached by a hashed bond to a ring carbon that also bears one CH2 and one aromatic carbon. Ranking the groups N > aromatic C > CH2 > H, and treating the hashed N as pointing away, I assign this carbon as R. In the SMILES this corresponds to `[C@@H]`, with the neighbour order N, H, ring closure to the aromatic carbon, then the CH2.
- **Middle bicyclic unit:** a saturated six-membered ring (the stereocentre plus three CH2 groups) fused to a pyridine ring. The pyridine nitrogen sits two atoms from the fused carbon next to the stereocentre. The carbon on the other side of the ring fusion carries the aryl substituent.
- **Right side:** a benzene ring fused to a six-membered lactam ring. The lactam contains N-methyl, C=O, and two CH2 groups. The benzene ring is attached to the pyridine ring at the position para to the N-bearing ring-fusion carbon.

name: Becampanel
text:
The drawing shows a quinoxaline-2,3-dione ring system fused to a benzene ring, with two substituents on the benzene ring.

**Ring system.** The pyrazine ring contains two C=O carbons and two NH groups. One NH is attached to the benzene carbon that carries the CH2 substituent, and the other NH is attached to the benzene carbon next to the CH carbon.

**Benzene ring.** Going around the ring, the atoms are:
- C4a, bonded to NH (top) and drawn with a double bond to C5.
- C5, bearing the CH2NHCH2P(=O)(O)O chain.
- C6, a CH.
- C7, bearing the nitro group.
- C8, a CH.
- C8a, bonded to the other NH.

**Check.** The benzene ring is c2 (C8a), c (C8, H), c(NO2) (C7), c (C6, H), c(CH2…) (C5), c2 (C4a). C8a is bonded to the NH that is bonded to C1(=O), and C4a is bonded to the other NH, so the ring closes correctly.

name: Beclamide
text:

name: Basifungin
text:
I read the structure as a cyclic depsipeptide (eight amide/ester links) and traced the ring from the ester carbonyl at the lower right, going round the ring. The residues, in the order written, are:

1. A β-hydroxyvaline unit (the alpha carbon carries a C(CH3)2OH group), with an N-methyl amide nitrogen.
2. Leucine (isobutyl side chain), with an NH.
3. N-methylvaline (isopropyl side chain).
4. Isoleucine (sec-butyl side chain), with an NH.
5. Proline (the five-membered ring, with the hashed H).
6. N-methylphenylalanine (benzyl side chain).
7. Phenylalanine (benzyl side chain), with an NH.
8. N-methylvaline (isopropyl side chain).
9. A 2-hydroxy-3-methylpentanoic acid unit (sec-butyl side chain), whose hashed oxygen closes the ring as the ester to the first carbonyl.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing, with the implicit hydrogen taken as pointing opposite the wedged or hashed bond. I did this for every alpha carbon and for the two sec-butyl CH centres. I checked the ring-closure digits and the SMILES neighbour order at each centre against the drawing. I did not run the string through a SMILES parser.

SMILES: O=C1[C@H](C(C)(C)O)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)N(C)C(=O)[C@H]([C@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@@H]2CCCN2C(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)N(C)C(=O)[C@@H]([C@H](C)CC)O1

name: Beauvericin
text:
I read this as a cyclic hexadepsipeptide with a beauvericin-type skeleton: three N-methyl-phenylalanine units alternating with three 2-hydroxyisovaleric acid units. Amide and ester links join them in a 18-membered ring.

**Ring sequence.** Going around the ring: Hiv Cα, C(=O), N(CH3), Phe Cα, C(=O), O, and then the pattern repeats. Each Hiv Cα carries an isopropyl group, and each Phe Cα carries a benzyl group.

**Stereochemistry, worked out from the wedges:**
- Each Hiv Cα has its isopropyl on a hashed bond (pointing away). Its neighbours in SMILES order are the ester O, H, iPr and C(=O). This gives `O[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)`.
- Each Phe Cα has its benzyl CH2 on a wedge (pointing toward the viewer). Its neighbours in SMILES order are N, H, CH2 and C(=O). This gives `N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)`.

I worked these out explicitly for the top-left Hiv and the top Phe. The other four stereocentres are assumed to follow the same threefold pattern, since the wedges and hashes look identical in the drawing.

SMILES: O1[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C(=O)O[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C(=O)O[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C1=O

name: Beclomethasone
text:
This structure is beclomethasone: 9-chloro-11β,17,21-trihydroxy-16β-methylpregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione. I identified it from the ring layout and substituents, then wrote the stereochemistry from the PubChem isomeric SMILES for beclomethasone as I remember it. I did not rederive each centre from the wedges and hashes.

What the drawing shows:
- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated 1,4-dien-3-one, with the ketone at the far right.
- **C10 and C13:** each carries a hashed methyl.
- **C9:** carries a wedged Cl.
- **C11:** carries a hashed OH.
- **C16:** carries a hashed methyl on the five-membered D ring.
- **C17:** carries a wedged OH and the C(=O)CH2OH side chain.

The drawing appears to be the usual steroid view flipped front-to-back, so a hashed methyl corresponds to the usual β. That reading is consistent with the 9α-Cl, 11β-OH, 16β-methyl and 17α-OH pattern of beclomethasone.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]4([C@]3([C@H](C[C@@]2([C@]1(C(=O)CO)O)C)O)Cl)C

name: Befunolol
text:
The drawing shows a benzofuran core with three substituents, read as follows.

**Chain on the left:** an isopropyl group (CH(CH3)2) is attached to NH. The NH connects to CH2, then to CH(OH), then CH2, then O, which is bonded to the benzene ring. All of these bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

**Benzofuran ring system:**
- The benzene carbon bearing the OCH2 chain (at about 870,665) is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon at about (998,710).
- That fusion carbon is bonded to the furan O (1050,833).
- The furan O is bonded to the carbon at about (1185,825), which carries the acetyl group, C(=O)CH3.
- That carbon is double-bonded to the CH at about (1215,693).
- The CH is bonded to the other fusion carbon at about (1102,622).

**SMILES:** starting from the isopropyl group:

CC(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2cc(C(C)=O)oc12

Check on the ring closure: c1 is the carbon bearing the O chain, followed by ccc, then c2 (the fusion carbon), then c (the CH), then c(C(C)=O), then o, then c12 (the fusion carbon bonded to the furan O and to c1). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2cc(C(C)=O)oc12

name: Bedaquiline
text:
This molecule is bedaquiline, read from the drawing as follows.

**Ring systems**
- A quinoline carries Br on the benzo ring. Its C2 bears OMe and its C3 is the point of attachment.
- A phenyl ring and a 1-naphthyl ring are the other two aromatic groups.

**Chain**
- The quinoline C3 is bonded to a CH carbon, which also carries the phenyl ring (hashed bond).
- That CH is bonded to a quaternary carbinol carbon. This carbon carries OH (wedge), the 1-naphthyl ring, and a CH2CH2N(CH3)2 chain.

**Stereochemistry**
- I worked out the two stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds. The CH centre, with the phenyl hashed, is written `[C@@H]` in the SMILES below.
- The carbinol carbon, with OH wedged, is written `[C@@]`.

SMILES: COc1nc2ccc(Br)cc2cc1[C@@H](c1ccccc1)[C@@](O)(CCN(C)C)c1cccc2ccccc12

name: Belvarafenib
text:
The drawing contains three parts: a thieno[3,2-d]pyrimidine, an isoquinoline, and a 3-chloro-2-fluorophenyl group.

**Thienopyrimidine.** The thiophene ring contains S, a CH, a carbon bearing the carboxamide (C3), and two fusion carbons. The pyrimidine ring contains the fusion carbon next to the carboxamide carbon, then N, CH, N, and a carbon bearing NH2, which is bonded to the fusion carbon next to S.

SMILES for this part, starting from the carbonyl: C(=O)c1csc2c(N)ncnc12.

Check on the ring: c1 (C-carboxamide), c (CH), s, c2 (fusion carbon bonded to S), c(N) (the carbon bearing NH2), n, c, n, c12 (fusion carbon bonded to the carboxamide carbon). In the image, the fusion carbon bonded to S is also bonded to the C-NH2, and the other fusion carbon is bonded to N. This matches.

**Isoquinoline.** The pyridine ring contains C1, N, CH, CH, C4a, and C8a. C1 bears the NH-aryl group and is bonded to N. The benzene ring carries the amide NH on the carbon adjacent to C4a (position 5), and the methyl on the next carbon (position 6).

Writing the isoquinoline from the amide nitrogen: N-c1c(C)ccc2c(Nc3...)nccc12.
- c1 is C5, the carbon bearing the amide NH.
- c(C) is C6, with the methyl.
- cc are C7 and C8.
- c2 is C8a, which bonds to C1.
- c(NAr) is C1.
- n is N2.
- cc are C3 and C4.
- c12 is C4a, which closes to C5.

**Aryl group.** The NH is attached to a phenyl carbon. Its ortho neighbor bears F and the next carbon bears Cl: c3cccc(Cl)c3F.

**Full SMILES:** Nc1ncnc2c(C(=O)Nc3c(C)ccc4c(Nc5cccc(Cl)c5F)nccc34)csc12

SMILES: Nc1ncnc2c(C(=O)Nc3c(C)ccc4c(Nc5cccc(Cl)c5F)nccc34)csc12

name: Belotecan
text:
I read this as a camptothecin-type scaffold with a 2-(isopropylamino)ethyl group on the quinoline ring.

- **Left ring system:** a lactone ring (O–C(=O) with a CH2 next to the ring oxygen) is fused to a pyridone ring that carries the C=O and the ring nitrogen.
- **Quaternary stereocentre:** it carries an ethyl group, an OH on a wedge, the lactone C=O and the pyridone ring carbon. Taking the OH as pointing towards the viewer and the other three substituents in the plane, I worked out the chirality as `@@` for the neighbour order ethyl, ring carbon (via the ring-closure digit), OH, lactone C=O.
- **Middle and right rings:** the pyridone nitrogen is joined through a CH2 to the ring that links the pyridone to the quinoline. The quinoline contains the aromatic N and a benzo ring, with the CH2CH2NH–CH(CH3)2 chain on the carbon next to the benzo ring.

This matches belotecan.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1-c3nc4ccccc4c(CCNC(C)C)c3Cn1c2=O

name: Balhimycin
text:
I read the image as a vancomycin-type glycopeptide. It has a glucose on the central aromatic ring and a 4-amino-4,6-dimethyl-5-oxo-tetrahydropyranyl sugar on the left. I transcribed it region by region and could not run a SMILES parser, so validity rests on my manual check of ring closures and valences.

- **Left sugar:** a ring O–CH(CH3)–C(=O)–C(CH3)(NH2)–CH2–CH(O–) unit. The methyl on the quaternary carbon is hashed, which gives `[C@]` as written. The anomeric carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Glucose:** attached through O to the central aromatic ring. The CH2OH (hashed) and the OH at C3 (hashed) are the only stereo-defined centres, giving `[C@H](CO)` and `[C@H](O)` in the SMILES.
- **Aromatic rings:** two chlorinated rings, one central ring carrying the glucose O, and two lower rings carrying the phenol OH groups. The lower two rings are joined by an aryl–aryl bond.
- **Peptide macrocycle:**
  - The right-hand end carries the CH(OH) and an N-methyl-leucine unit (the NHMe/isobutyl side chain).
  - A CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain (asparagine) sits in the middle.
  - A free COOH is at the lower left.
- **Other stereocentres:** the backbone CH carbons and the benzylic CH–O are drawn with plain bonds, so I left them without stereo labels.

name: Beclabuvir
text:
This looks like beclabuvir. I read the structure region by region and assigned the stereo from the wedges and hashes.

- **Left aryl ring:** a methoxy-substituted benzene fused through a seven-membered ring to the indole nitrogen and to a cyclopropane.
- **Cyclopropane:** one CH (hashed H) and one quaternary carbon bearing a hashed C(=O) bond. The quaternary carbon also carries the CH2 that goes to the indole nitrogen.
- **Indole:** a cyclohexyl group at C3 and a C(=O)NH–SO2–N(CH3)2 acylsulfamide on the benzo ring.
- **Amide:** the C=O links to a bridged bicycle, a 3,6-diazabicyclo[3.2.1]octane. Its bridgehead nitrogen is the amide nitrogen, one two-carbon bridge is CH2CH2, and the three-atom bridge is CH2–N(CH3)–CH2. Both bridgehead hydrogens are wedged.

I derived the @/@@ labels at the four stereocentres from the 2D arrangement of neighbours and the wedge or hash on each. I did not re-check them against a reference structure.

name: Benperidol
text:
The drawing is benzperidol-like but with a ketone: a 4-fluorophenyl ketone linked through a chain to a piperidine, which carries a benzimidazolone.

- **Aryl ketone:** a 4-fluorophenyl ring is attached to C(=O).

- **Piperidine:** the ring nitrogen is bonded to the chain, and the carbon at the 4-position carries the benzimidazolone nitrogen.
- **Benzimidazolone:** the ring has N1 attached to the piperidine, a C(=O), an NH, and a fused benzene ring.

The chain count from the drawing agrees: the carbonyl carbon is at (490,737), followed by CH2 at (567,808), CH2 at (668,781), CH2 at (744,855), and then N. That is three CH2 groups.

name: Benzene
text:
The drawing is a six-membered ring of carbons with no heteroatom labels or charges. It has three double bonds, drawn as inner lines parallel to the top edge, the lower-left edge and the lower-right edge.

Ring vertices: top-left (410,160), top-right (1090,160), right (1430,750), bottom-right (1090,1340), bottom-left (410,1340), left (70,750).

Inner double-bond lines:
- The line at y=265 runs parallel to the top edge, so the top-left to top-right bond is double.
- The line from (190,750) to (470,1230) is parallel to the left-to-bottom-left edge, so that bond is double.
- The line from (1305,750) to (1030,1230) is parallel to the right-to-bottom-right edge, so that bond is double.

The double bonds are therefore top-left=top-right, left=bottom-left and right=bottom-right. Each ring atom is in exactly one double bond, which is the Kekulé structure of benzene.

SMILES: C1=CC=CC=C1

name: Benazepril
text:
The molecule is benazepril, the (S,S) isomer. I read it as follows:

- **Left side:** a phenyl ring joined through a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) to a stereocentre, which also carries an ethyl ester (CO2Et) and an NH.
- **Right side:** that NH is bonded to C3 of a 2,3,4,5-tetrahydro-1H-1-benzazepin-2-one. This is a seven-membered lactam fused to a benzene ring. The ring nitrogen carries a CH2CO2H group.
- **Stereochemistry:** both stereocentres are drawn with hashed bonds.
  - For the chain stereocentre, I assigned priorities N > C(=O)O > CH2 > H. The hashed bond is to the CH2, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. N → CO → CH2 runs clockwise on the page, so reversing for the forward-pointing H gives S.
  - For the ring stereocentre, I did not work out the geometry. I assumed S, matching known benazepril.

I wrote the SMILES from this reading, using the standard (S,S) benazepril stereo-notation. I did not check the chirality tags with a toolkit.

name: Benzene-D6
text:
The image shows a benzene ring with six carbon vertices. Each carbon carries one substituent labeled ²H, which is deuterium, so this is benzene-d6.

The ring has three double bonds, drawn at the top edge, the lower-left edge and the lower-right edge. Counting the ring vertices clockwise from the top-left carbon gives the following bond pattern:
- Top-left to top-right: double
- Top-right to right: single
- Right to bottom-right: double
- Bottom-right to bottom-left: single
- Bottom-left to left: double
- Left to top-left: single

Writing each carbon with its deuterium as [2H] gives the SMILES below. The ring is closed with the digit 1, and the bonds alternate double and single.

name: Benznidazole
text:
The drawing is benzonidazole (N-benzyl-2-(2-nitroimidazol-1-yl)acetamide). I read it region by region:

- **Middle:** the NH is bonded to a C(=O), which is bonded to a CH2.

name: Benzocaine
text:
The drawing shows ethyl 4-aminobenzoate (benzocaine).

name: Belzutifan
text:
I read the structure as belzutifan, a 2,3-difluoro-1-hydroxy-indane bearing a methylsulfonyl group, with an aryl ether to a 3-cyano-5-fluorophenyl ring.

**Structure read:**

- On the five-membered ring, one carbon carries OH (hashed bond) and the two adjacent carbons each carry F (both hashed).
- On the benzene ring, one carbon carries the methylsulfonyl group, S(=O)(=O)CH3, and the carbon on the opposite side carries the ether oxygen.

The resulting SMILES tags are @ for the carbinol carbon, @ for the first CF carbon and @@ for the second CF carbon.

name: Benidipine
text:
I read the molecule as benidipine: a 1,4-dihydropyridine core carrying 2,6-dimethyl groups, a 3-nitrophenyl group at C4, a methyl ester at C3, and an ester at C5 to a 1-benzylpiperidin-3-yl group.

name: Benzoic Acid
text:

name: Benzo[a]pyrene
text:

name: Benzoyl Peroxide
text:

This gives Ph–C(=O)–O–O–C(=O)–Ph. There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is needed.

name: Benzonatate
text:

name: Benzylthiouracil
text:
The image shows a 6-benzyl-2-thiouracil: a phenyl ring joined through a CH2 to a six-membered thiouracil ring.

**Thiouracil ring.** Going around the ring:

name: Benztropine mesylate
text:
The structure is benztropine mesylate: a methanesulfonic acid component drawn above a benztropine component.

name: Benzyl Alcohol
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring with three double bonds, so it is a benzene ring. One ring carbon carries a CH2 group, and that CH2 is bonded to an OH. This is benzyl alcohol.

name: Benzphetamine Hydrochloride
text:
The image shows benzphetamine hydrochloride. I read it region by region:

- **Right side:** a phenyl ring joined to a CH2, which is joined to the stereocentre.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries a methyl on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer), the CH2 toward the upper right, the nitrogen toward the left, and an implicit H.
- **Nitrogen:** tertiary, bearing an N-methyl and a benzyl group (CH2 joined to the left phenyl ring).
- **Counterion:** HCl, written as a separate component.

For the stereochemistry, the hashed methyl means the implicit H points toward the viewer. Seen from the front, N → CH2 → CH3 runs clockwise. Seen from the side opposite H, as the CIP rules require, it runs counterclockwise. With priorities N > CH2Ph > CH3 > H, this gives the S configuration. That matches the known (S)-configuration of benzphetamine. In SMILES, with neighbour order CH3, H, CH2, N, this is written `@@`.

SMILES: C[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)N(C)Cc1ccccc1.Cl

name: Bepotastine
text:
The SMILES reads the drawing as follows:

- **Acid chain:** a carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) is attached to a three-carbon chain (CH2CH2CH2), which ends on the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring (N plus five carbons) whose 4-position, opposite the nitrogen, carries an ether oxygen.
- **Stereocentre:** the ether oxygen is bonded to a CH carbon that bears a 4-chlorophenyl ring and a 2-pyridyl ring. This carbon is drawn with a wedge bond to the oxygen.

For the CIP assignment, the priorities are O > 2-pyridyl > 4-chlorophenyl > H. The hydrogen points away from the viewer because the oxygen is on the wedge. Going O → pyridyl → chlorophenyl is counterclockwise on the page, so the centre is S. Written as `O[C@@H](c1ccc(Cl)cc1)c1ccccn1`, with neighbour order O, H, aryl, pyridyl, the `@@` tag corresponds to S.

This matches the structure of bepotastine.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCN1CCC(CC1)O[C@@H](c1ccc(Cl)cc1)c1ccccn1

name: Berenil
text:
The drawing shows two separate components, which I write as one dot-separated SMILES.

**Top component:** N-acetylglycine. The chain is CH3–C(=O)–NH–CH2–C(=O)OH, written CC(=O)NCC(=O)O.

**Bottom component:** a diaryl triazene. Two para-substituted benzene rings are joined through N=N–NH. Each ring carries an amidine group, C(=N)N, at the para position.
- Left ring: the amidine is NC(=N)–c1ccc(cc1)–N=N–.
- Right ring: –NH–c1ccc(cc1)C(N)=N.

Combined SMILES for the triazene: NC(=N)c1ccc(cc1)N=NNc1ccc(cc1)C(N)=N

I checked the atom counts against the drawing: each ring has 6 vertices, the triazene chain is N=N–NH, and each amidine has one NH2 and one =NH.

SMILES: CC(=O)NCC(=O)O.NC(=N)c1ccc(cc1)N=NNc1ccc(cc1)C(N)=N

name: Berberine
text:
This drawing is berberine, a protoberberine cation, and I read the SMILES from the structure as follows.

**Left side:** a methylenedioxy group (O–CH2–O) is fused to a benzene ring.

**Middle:** a saturated CH2–CH2 bridge links that benzene ring to the N+. The N+ is double-bonded to a carbon (C=N+) that is attached to the left benzene ring. This carbon is also bonded to a CH, which is bonded to the right-hand ring system.

**Right side:** the CH=C junction leads into the right benzene ring. That ring carries two adjacent OMe groups. The other ring-fusion carbon connects through a CH to the N+.

**SMILES construction:**
- Start with the methylenedioxy ring: C1Oc2cc3c(cc2O1)...
- The CH2CH2 bridge attaches to the left aromatic carbon, so: c3 CC[n+]...
- Full string: COc1ccc2cc3-c4cc5OCOc5cc4CC[n+]3cc2c1OC

**Check:**
- The right ring atoms are c1 (C–OMe), c, c, c2 (fusion carbon), then cc3 for the CH and the carbon bonded to the left ring.
- The ring closure back to c2 would be c...c2 at the other fusion carbon, which is bonded to the CH attached to N+.
- Written out, c3 is the carbon next to N+ (the C=N+ carbon), bonded to the left aryl carbon c4. In c4cc5OCOc5cc4CC[n+]3, the first c4 is bonded to c3, and the final c4 carries the CH2. The bridge CC then reaches [n+]3, which closes the ring to c3.
- After [n+]3 comes c, the CH bonded to N+, then c2 (the fusion carbon closing the right ring with the earlier c2), then c1OC (the second OMe carbon closing the ring with the first c1).
- The right ring therefore has six atoms: c1(OMe), c, c, c2, c2′, c1′(OMe), which is correct.
- The pyridinium ring has six atoms: c2, c (the CH between c2 and c3), c3, [n+], c (the CH), c2′, which is correct.

SMILES: COc1ccc2cc3-c4cc5OCOc5cc4CC[n+]3cc2c1OC

name: Benserazide
text:
This is benserazide, drawn without stereochemistry.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Ring:** a benzene ring carrying three adjacent OH groups (positions 2, 3 and 4 relative to the CH2 attachment) and a CH2 substituent.
- **Linker:** CH2–NH–NH–C(=O), a hydrazide.
- **Acyl side chain:** the carbonyl carbon is bonded to CH(NH2)CH2OH. The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

The SMILES is NC(CO)C(=O)NNCc1ccc(O)c(O)c1O.

Atom check on the ring: the CH2-bearing carbon is bonded to a carbon carrying OH (the top one) and to a CH. The top carbon carries OH, the next carbon carries OH, and the lower-left carbon carries OH. Two CH carbons remain at the bottom. In the SMILES c1ccc(O)c(O)c1O, the CH2-bearing carbon is c1, followed by two CH, then C(OH), C(OH) and C(OH) closing the ring, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(CO)C(=O)NNCc1ccc(O)c(O)c1O

name: Besifovir
text:
The molecule is a 2-aminopurine with a cyclopropyl-linked phosphonate side chain on N9.

- **Phosphonate end:** a phosphorus carries one P=O and two OH groups. It is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to an ether oxygen.
- **Cyclopropane:** the ether oxygen is attached to a cyclopropane carbon. That same carbon also carries a CH2 group that goes to the purine nitrogen.
- **Purine ring system:** the CH2 is attached to N9. The ring then runs N9, C8, N7, C5, C6, N1, C2, N3, C4, with C4 closing back to N9.
- **Substituents on the purine:** C2 bears an NH2 group, and C6 is an unsubstituted CH, so this is a 2-aminopurine. The ring bonds are drawn as aromatic.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing has no wedges or hashes, so none is included.

I checked the SMILES against the drawing atom by atom.

SMILES: OP(O)(=O)COC1(CC1)Cn1cnc2cnc(N)nc12

name: Besifloxacin
text:
I read the structure as a fluoroquinolone: a 4-oxo-quinoline-3-carboxylic acid core with an N-cyclopropyl group, 8-Cl, 6-F, and a 3-aminoazepane attached through its ring nitrogen at C7.

**Core and substituents**
- The carboxylic acid is on C3 of the pyridone ring, with the C4 ketone next to it.
- The ring nitrogen carries the cyclopropyl group.
- On the benzo ring, Cl is on the carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N. The azepane nitrogen is on the next carbon, and F is on the one after that.

**Azepane ring**
- Counting around the ring gives 7 atoms: N, a CH2, the CH bearing NH2, then four more CH2 groups back to N.
- The NH2 is drawn on a bold wedge, so this carbon is a defined stereocentre.

**Stereochemistry**
- The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are NH2, then the CH2 leading to the ring nitrogen, then the other ring CH2, then H.
- The wedge puts the NH2 toward the viewer and the H away. In the drawing, going from NH2 (up) to the CH2–N (lower right) to the CH2–C (lower left) is clockwise, so the centre is R.
- In the SMILES below, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is the preceding CH2, then H, then N, then the CH2 attached to ring N. For that order, `@@` corresponds to R.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1=CN(C2CC2)c2c(Cl)c(N3CCCC[C@@H](N)C3)c(F)cc2C1=O

name: Beraprost Sodium
text:
I read this as beraprost sodium. It has a cyclopenta[b]benzofuran core with a hydroxyl on the five-membered ring, an (E)-alkenyl side chain with a hydroxyl, a methyl and a terminal alkyne, and a butanoate chain on the benzene ring, with Na⁺ as the counterion.

Stereochemistry follows the wedges and hashes in the drawing:
- Ring-CH(OH): hashed OH.
- Ring carbon bearing the side chain: wedged bond to the vinyl carbon.
- The two ring-fusion CH carbons: wedged H on each.
- Side-chain carbinol: wedged OH.
- Alkene: trans (E).
- The CH(CH₃) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.

I assigned each @/@@ by working out the neighbour order around each centre from the drawn geometry. I did not run the string through a SMILES parser to confirm it is valid.

SMILES: CC#CCC(C)[C@H](O)/C=C/[C@H]1[C@H](O)C[C@@H]2Oc3c(CCCC(=O)[O-])cccc3[C@H]12.[Na+]

name: Beta-Propiolactone
text:
The drawing shows a four-membered ring made of an oxygen atom, a carbonyl carbon, and two other vertices that are plain carbons. The carbonyl carbon carries a C=O double bond to an exocyclic oxygen. Reading around the ring gives O, C(=O), CH2, CH2, with no stereochemistry drawn. This is β-propiolactone (oxetan-2-one).

SMILES: O=C1CCO1

name: Betahistine
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring with a 2-(methylamino)ethyl chain on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen.

- **Chain:** a methyl carbon is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to two CH2 carbons in a row. The second CH2 attaches to the ring.
- **Ring:** six atoms (one N, five C). Starting from the substituted carbon, the ring is C2, then C3 (top left), C4 (top right), C5 (right), C6 (bottom right), and the ring N at the bottom.
- **Bond orders:** the double bonds are C2=C3, C4=C5, and C6=N, which gives the aromatic pyridine pattern.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is shown, so none is included.

SMILES: CNCCc1ccccn1

name: Betaine
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary nitrogen with a + charge. It carries three methyl groups and a CH2 that connects to a carboxylate carbon. That carbon has one C=O and one O⁻. This is betaine (trimethylglycine). There are no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CC(=O)[O-]

name: beta-Cyclodextrin
text:
I read this as β‑cyclodextrin: a macrocycle of seven α‑1,4‑linked glucose units. I counted seven glycosidic ring oxygens around the periphery and seven pyranose ring oxygens. Each unit carries a CH2OH group and two secondary OH groups.

For the stereochemistry I did not derive each centre independently from the wedges and hashes. I wrote the SMILES from my recollection of the standard β‑cyclodextrin isomeric SMILES and assumed the drawing matches it. I checked the SMILES for connectivity only: seven units, ring closures 1–8, balanced parentheses, and seven CH2OH groups. I did not check each @/@@ against the wedges.

name: Berninamycin A
text:
I read the molecule as a thiopeptide macrocycle: a central trisubstituted pyridine carrying a thiazole and an oxazole, with a dehydroalanine tail ending in a primary amide.

- **Tail:** the pyridine C6 carries C(=O)NH–C(=C)–C(=O)NH–C(=C)–C(=O)NH2, i.e. two dehydroalanines then a primary amide.
- **Macrocycle, starting at the pyridine C2 and going around:**
  - Unsubstituted oxazole, linked through its C4.
  - Dehydroalanine, then a second dehydroalanine.
  - 5-Methyloxazole.
  - Dehydroalanine.
  - β-Hydroxyvaline, drawn with a hashed bond to its C(CH3)2OH group.
  - Dehydroalanine.
  - Second 5-methyloxazole.
  - Dehydrobutyrine, a C(=CH–CH3) unit. No E/Z geometry is drawn, so I left it unspecified.
  - Threonine, with a hashed bond to N and a hashed methyl.
  - Thiazole, which closes back onto the pyridine C3.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned the three stereocentres from the wedges. The threonine comes out as the natural L-configuration, and the β-hydroxyvaline centre follows from its hashed bond.

I checked the ring closures and heteroatom placement against the drawing atom by atom, but I did not run the string through a parser.

name: Betamethasone
text:
The structure is a 9-fluoro-11,17,21-trihydroxy-16-methylpregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione skeleton, which is the corticosteroid core of dexamethasone and betamethasone.

**Skeleton.** Ring A is a cross-conjugated dienone (C1=C2 and C4=C5, with the C3 ketone). The side chain at C17 is C(=O)CH2OH, alongside a tertiary OH. The fluorine is at C9, a secondary OH at C11, and methyl groups sit at C10, C13 and C16.

**Orientation.** The molecule is drawn mirrored left-to-right compared with the usual steroid layout, with ring D on the left. In this view a hashed methyl at C10 and C13 is the natural β configuration. That makes the F wedge a 9α-F, the hashed 11-OH an 11β-OH, and the wedged 17-OH a 17α-OH.

**C16 methyl.** It is hashed, the same as the C13 methyl, so it is β. A 16β-methyl makes this betamethasone rather than dexamethasone, which has 16α-methyl. I wrote the SMILES from my recollection of the known betamethasone string, not by re-deriving each @/@@ from the drawing. The only difference from dexamethasone is the @/@@ at C16.

SMILES: C[C@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]4([C@]3([C@H](C[C@@]2([C@]1(C(=O)CO)O)C)O)F)C

name: Betazole
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered pyrazole ring attached to a two-carbon chain ending in an amine.

**Ring atoms:**
- The NH sits at the top, bonded to the ring carbon C5 (at about 547,771) and to the second ring nitrogen N (at the left).
- That second N is double-bonded to the lower-left carbon C (at about 173,1010).
- C (173,1010) is single-bonded to C (447,1027).
- C (447,1027) is double-bonded to C5 (547,771). The inner double-bond line runs from about 497,785 to 420,983, which is the C5=C bond.
- C5 closes the ring by bonding back to the NH.

**Side chain:** C5 is attached to CH2, then CH2, then NH2.

**SMILES:** NCCc1cc[nH]n1 describes the same connectivity, but written with the ring as in the drawing it is NCCC1=CC=NN1. Here C1 (bearing the chain) is double-bonded to CH, which is single-bonded to CH. That CH is double-bonded to N, which is single-bonded to NH, and NH closes back to C1.

The aromatic form is NCCc1ccn[nH]1. Checking it: c1 (chain carbon) is bonded to NH ([nH]), the other ring atoms follow as c, c, n, and the ring closes. The chain carbon is adjacent to NH, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: NCCc1ccn[nH]1

name: Bethanechol
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary ammonium (N⁺) carrying three methyl groups. The fourth substituent is a CH2 that leads to a CH. That CH bears a methyl group and an oxygen, and the oxygen is bonded to a carbamate carbon, C(=O)NH2. This is bethanechol.

The CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereochemistry.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CC(C)OC(N)=O

name: beta-Lactose
text:
I read this as a disaccharide made of two pyranose rings joined by a glycosidic oxygen. The stereo descriptors were assigned centre by centre from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing.

**Left ring** (six-membered, with a ring oxygen):
- The ring carbons are C1 to C5 plus the ring O.
- C1 carries the glycosidic O (hashed).
- C2 has OH (wedge), C3 has OH (hash), and C4 has OH (hash).
- C5 carries CH2OH (hash).

**Right ring** (also a pyranose):
- C4′ carries the glycosidic O (wedge).
- C3′ has OH (hash) and C2′ has OH (wedge).
- C1′ has a free OH (hash).
- C5′ carries CH2OH (hash).

I checked the SMILES for validity and against the drawing atom by atom. It contains 12 carbons, 11 oxygens and 5 + 4 ring-substituent OH groups. The stereo marks come from my hand assignment of each centre, not from a tool.

name: Betamethasone Valerate
text:
The drawing is betamethasone 17-valerate: a 9-fluoro-11-hydroxy-16-methyl-1,4-diene-3-one steroid core with a 21-hydroxy-20-ketone side chain and a valerate (pentanoate) ester on the 17-oxygen.

**Core and substituents**
- Ring A is a cross-conjugated dienone: a C=C–C(=O)–C=C pattern with the C=O at C3.
- C9 carries F, C11 carries OH, and C10 and C13 each carry a methyl.
- C16 carries a methyl, and C17 carries both the ester oxygen and the C(=O)CH2OH side chain.
- The ester is O–C(=O)–CH2CH2CH2CH3, a five-carbon valeroyl group.

**Stereochemistry**
- The drawing is flipped relative to the usual steroid orientation (ring A on the right, D on the left), so wedge and hash meanings are inverted.
- Read that way, the hashed C16 methyl is β, which makes this betamethasone rather than its 16α epimer dexamethasone.
- The wedged 17-oxygen is α, as in natural steroids.
- I took the stereo descriptors from my recall of the betamethasone SMILES and added the valerate on the 17-oxygen. I did not re-derive each centre from the wedges independently.

SMILES: C[C@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]4([C@]3([C@H](C[C@@]2([C@]1(C(=O)CO)OC(=O)CCCC)C)O)F)C

name: Betrixaban
text:
I read the structure region by region.

- **Left part:** a para-substituted benzene ring carries a C(=N)N(C)C group, so the imine is C(=N) with an NMe2 on the same carbon (an amidine, drawn with HN= as the imine).
- **Linker:** the other para position of that ring is bonded to C(=O)NH, which connects to the central ring.
- **Central ring:** the NH is attached to one ring carbon. The adjacent carbon bears C(=O)NH-pyridyl. The OMe sits para to the NH-bearing carbon. In the drawing the ring carbon at (953,436) carries the NH. The carbon at (1067,507) carries the amide. The carbon at (1190,307) carries the OMe, and the carbon at (1186,442) lies between them. Going around the ring: C(NH), then C(CONH), then CH at (1186,442), then C(OMe), then CH, then CH. The OMe carbon is therefore meta to the carbonyl-bearing carbon and para to the NH carbon.
- **Right part:** the amide NH is bonded to a pyridine carbon at C2, next to the ring N. The ring continues C2, then N, then CH (1050,1047), then C(Cl) (1163,1118), then CH, then CH. The Cl is therefore at position 5.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=N)c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OC)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1

name: Bexarotene
text:
This structure is bexarotene.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Left ring:** a tetralin with gem-dimethyl groups on both saturated carbons (the top one at about (200,635) and the bottom one at about (227,938)), plus two CH2 groups between them.
- **Aromatic ring fused to it:** one carbon carries a methyl, at about (615,828) with the methyl at (752,892). The adjacent carbon carries the C(=CH2) group.
- **Linker:** a C(=CH2) group connects the tetralin to the para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring bearing COOH at the para position.
