name: Bicalutamide
text:
The drawing is bicalutamide, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is written.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Left ring:** a benzene ring bearing a nitrile (C#N) on one carbon and a CF3 group on the adjacent carbon. The NH attaches at the carbon para to the nitrile-bearing carbon (para to the CN carbon, meta to the CF3 carbon).
- **Linker:** the NH is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O). That carbonyl is bonded to a quaternary carbon carrying OH and CH3, and this carbon is also bonded to a CH2.
- **Right side:** the CH2 is bonded to a sulfonyl group (S with two =O), which is bonded to a benzene ring bearing F at the para position.

Left ring atom order: the C(CF3) carbon is next to the C(CN) carbon, and C(CN) is para to the C(NH) carbon. Going around the ring from the NH carbon: c1 (NH), c (CH, between NH and CF3), c(CF3), c(CN), c (CH), c (CH). The CN carbon is three bonds from the NH carbon, so it is para, as required.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc(NC(=O)C(C)(O)CS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(F)cc2)cc1C(F)(F)F

name: Bexagliflozin
text:
The drawing matches bexagliflozin, an aryl C-glycoside SGLT2 inhibitor. I read it as follows:

- **Left end:** a cyclopropyl ring joined through an ether oxygen to a two-carbon chain (O–CH2–CH2–O).
- **First aromatic ring:** the chain ends at a para-substituted benzene ring, which carries a CH2 bridge at the para position.
- **Second aromatic ring:** the CH2 links to a second benzene ring bearing a chlorine ortho to the CH2. The sugar is attached meta to the CH2 and para to the chlorine.
- **Sugar ring:** a pyranose ring (five carbons plus one ring oxygen) with three OH groups and a CH2OH. The anomeric carbon is bonded directly to the aryl ring, which is a C–C bond rather than a C–O glycoside bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** I did not derive the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes bond by bond. I recognised the glucose-type configuration (hashed aryl bond at the anomeric carbon, hashed CH2OH) and used the stereo-SMILES I recall for bexagliflozin.

SMILES: C1CC1OCCOc1ccc(Cc2cc([C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O)ccc2Cl)cc1

name: Binimetinib
text:
This is binimetinib, a benzimidazole carboxamide with a hydroxyethoxy amide, a 4-bromo-2-fluoroanilino group, a fluorine on the core, and an N-methyl.

**Aniline ring.** Br sits on the top carbon. Going around the ring, the carbon bearing F is meta to Br, and the carbon bearing NH lies between that F carbon and the next ring carbon. So the ring is 4-bromo-2-fluorophenyl attached to NH.

**Benzimidazole core.**
- The carbon bearing F is bonded to C3a, which is bonded to N3 (the "N=" nitrogen).
- N3 connects to CH=, then to N1(CH3), then to C7a, which is bonded to the aromatic CH.
- That CH is bonded to the carbon bearing C(=O)NH, which is bonded to the carbon bearing the NHAr group, which is bonded back to the carbon bearing F.

**Side chain.** The amide is C(=O)NHOCH2CH2OH.

**SMILES.**
Cn1cnc2c(F)c(Nc3ccc(Br)cc3F)c(C(=O)NOCCO)cc21

I checked the ring closures. Here n1 is N1 with the methyl, c is C2, n is N3, c2 is C3a, c(F) is C4, c(N...) is C5, c(C(=O)...) is C6, c is C7, and c21 is C7a, which closes both rings. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1cnc2c(F)c(Nc3ccc(Br)cc3F)c(C(=O)NOCCO)cc21

name: Bimatoprost
text:
I read this as bimatoprost, the N-ethyl amide of 17-phenyl-trinor-prostaglandin F2α. I took the stereodescriptors from the known bimatoprost SMILES rather than deriving each one from the wedges and hashes in the drawing, so they are unchecked against the image.

- **Amide end:** an N-ethyl amide, CH3CH2–NH–C(=O)–.
- **Upper chain:** four CH2/CH carbons connect the carbonyl to a cis (Z) C=C, which then leads through one CH2 to the ring. Counting from the carbonyl, that is three CH2, then CH=CH, then CH2.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentane with two OH groups (hashed bonds). The upper chain and the lower chain sit on adjacent ring carbons.
- **Lower chain:** a trans (E) CH=CH, then a CH(OH) with a hashed bond, then CH2CH2 and a phenyl ring.

SMILES: CCNC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@H](C[C@H]([C@@H]1/C=C/[C@H](CCC2=CC=CC=C2)O)O)O

name: Bis(pinacolato)diborane
text:
The drawing shows bis(pinacolato)diboron. Reading it region by region:

- Two boron atoms are joined by a single B–B bond.
- Each boron carries two oxygens, and those oxygens close a five-membered ring (B, O, C, C, O) through two adjacent carbons.
- In each ring, both carbons are quaternary and each bears two methyl groups, giving four methyls per ring.

This gives the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC1(C)OB(OC1(C)C)B2OC(C)(C)C(C)(C)O2

name: beta-Amanitin
text:
I read this as a bicyclic amatoxin-type peptide, β-amanitin-like. The residues are Ile, Gly, Cys (as a sulfoxide), Asp, 4-hydroxy-Pro, a dihydroxy-Ile and a 6-hydroxy-Trp. The Trp indole C2 is bonded to the Cys sulfur, which forms the second ring.

I traced the connectivity around the macrocycle as follows:

1. Ile Cα carries an NH that leads to Gly, then Trp.
2. Ile C=O leads to Gly, then Cys NH.
3. Cys C=O leads to Asp NH.
4. Asp C=O is bonded to the Pro nitrogen.
5. Pro C=O leads to the dihydroxy-Ile NH.
6. Dihydroxy-Ile C=O leads to the Trp NH.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash. The Ile, Cys, Trp and Asp centres give the L-amino-acid configurations expected for the natural residues.

The sulfoxide sulfur is also a stereocentre, but I left it unspecified because its wedge is hard to interpret from the drawing alone.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H]2CS(=O)c3[nH]c4cc(O)ccc4c3C[C@@H](C(=O)NCC(=O)N1)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)[C@@H](O)CO)NC(=O)[C@@H]5C[C@@H](O)CN5C(=O)[C@H](CC(=O)O)NC2=O

name: Bis(dibenzylideneacetone)palladium
text:
The image shows three dibenzylideneacetone (dba) molecules and two Pd atoms, which is Pd2(dba)3 written as separate fragments.

Each dba unit is O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1, with both alkenes drawn trans.

Checking the first alkene, which runs from the phenyl ring up to a vertex and then down to the next vertex:
- The phenyl carbon sits at (310, 287), the first alkene carbon at (420, 222), the second at (532, 287), and the carbonyl carbon at (644, 222).
- The phenyl and the carbonyl lie on opposite sides of the C=C, so the alkene is trans (E).

The right-hand alkene is also zigzag, so it is trans as well.

Each dba is written as O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1. The left arm, C(/C=C/Ph), has the carbonyl carbon before the first alkene carbon and the phenyl after the second, with "/" bonds on both sides, which gives trans. The right arm, C(.../C=C/Ph), is written the same way and is also trans.

The three dba molecules and the two Pd atoms are joined as dot-separated fragments.

SMILES: O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1.O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1.O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1.[Pd].[Pd]

name: Bisacodyl
text:
This structure is bisacodyl: a central CH bonded to a 2-pyridyl ring and to two para-acetoxyphenyl rings.

- The pyridine nitrogen is bonded to the ring carbon that carries the CH, so the attachment is at the 2-position.
- Each phenyl ring has an acetate ester (OC(C)=O) at the para position relative to the central CH.
- The central CH is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CC(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccccn1)c1ccc(OC(C)=O)cc1

name: Bismuth Subcitrate
text:
The image shows two identical citrate trianions, three potassium cations, and one bismuth(III) cation with a lone pair.

Each citrate unit has a central carbon bearing an OH group and a carboxylate, plus two CH2–COO⁻ arms. Its SMILES is [O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-].

The charges balance: the two citrates contribute 6−, and 3 K⁺ plus Bi³⁺ contribute 6+.

The bismuth is drawn as Bi³⁺ with a colon beside it, indicating a lone pair, so I write it as [Bi+3] and leave the lone pair out of the SMILES.

The components are written as separate dot-disconnected fragments.

SMILES: [O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-].[O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-].[K+].[K+].[K+].[Bi+3]

name: Bismuth Subsalicylate
text:
The image shows three separate components:

1. A bismuth cation labelled "Bi3+" with a colon beside it, which indicates a lone pair. This is written [Bi+3].
2. A hydroxide anion, written [OH-].
3. A salicylate dianion. The benzene ring carries a phenoxide O- on one carbon and, on the adjacent carbon, a carboxylate group drawn as C(=O)[O-].

The ring bonds as drawn are:
- The phenoxide carbon (top right) has a double bond to the carbon at the top left.
- The carbon at the lower left has a double bond to the carbon at the bottom.
- The carboxylate-bearing carbon has a double bond to the carbon at the bottom right.

The aromatic SMILES for the salicylate is [O-]c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].

The charges balance: Bi is +3, and the three anions (OH-, phenoxide O-, carboxylate O-) total −3.

The lone pair on bismuth is not usually written in SMILES, so I have left it out.

SMILES: [Bi+3].[OH-].[O-]c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]

name: Bismuth Subgallate
text:
The drawing shows several separate components:

- **Bismuth:** Bi³⁺ with a lone pair, written `[Bi+3]` (the ":" is a lone pair).
- **Hydroxide:** `[OH-]`.
- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring bearing a COOH group, two O⁻ groups and one OH group.

I traced the ring atom by atom. The carboxyl carbon attaches to ring carbon C1 at (573, 930). Going around the ring:

- C2 at (703, 703) is CH.
- C3 at (965, 703) carries O⁻.
- C4 at (1095, 930) carries O⁻.
- C5 at (965, 1155) carries OH.
- C6 at (703, 1155) is CH.

This is gallic acid with two deprotonated phenols, at positions 3 and 4, and the OH at position 5.

The ring SMILES is `OC(=O)c1cc([O-])c([O-])c(O)c1`.

The bond orders in the drawing are consistent with this. Double bonds are drawn at C2=C3, C4=C5, and C6=C1, which is a valid Kekulé form of the aromatic ring.

The charges balance: Bi is +3 and the three anions (two O⁻ and one OH⁻) total −3.

SMILES: [Bi+3].[OH-].OC(=O)c1cc([O-])c([O-])c(O)c1

name: Biotin
text:
The structure is biotin (a bicyclic ureido-thiophane ring with a pentanoic acid side chain).

- **Ring system:** a five-membered cyclic urea (N–C(=O)–N) is fused to a tetrahydrothiophene ring containing S. The two ring-fusion carbons are each bonded to one N.
- **Side chain:** four CH2 groups link the S-bearing ring carbon to a terminal COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the chain is drawn on a wedge, and both ring-fusion hydrogens are hashed. Assigning CIP priorities from the drawing gives S at the carbon bearing the chain, S at the ring-fusion carbon next to it, and R at the other ring-fusion carbon. This matches the (3aS,4S,6aR) configuration of natural D-biotin.

I wrote the SMILES from the known natural-biotin form, which agrees with these assignments.

SMILES: C1[C@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H](S1)CCCCC(=O)O)NC(=O)N2

name: Bisoprolol
text:
The drawing is a bisoprolol-type molecule, read from left to right:

- Isopropyl group: CH3–CH(CH3)–
- Secondary amine: –NH–
- Propanol chain: –CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–
- Aryl ether: –O– joined to a para-substituted benzene ring
- Para side chain on the ring: –CH2–O–CH2–CH2–O–CH(CH3)2

All bonds in the drawing are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so the stereocentre at the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(COCCOC(C)C)cc1

name: Bictegravir
text:
This is bictegravir, read from the drawing as follows.

**Fragments**
- The left side is a 2,4,6-trifluorobenzyl group (fluorines at both ortho positions and the para position) joined through CH2–NH to an amide C=O.
- The amide carbon is attached to a pyridinone ring: C(=CN)–C(=O)–C(OH)=C. The ring nitrogen is part of the central fused ring and carries a CH2.
- The central ring runs N–CH2–CH(acetal)–N–C(=O)–C(=C), so the acetal carbon bears both an oxygen and a nitrogen.
- The right side is a bridged bicycle: the acetal oxygen links to one cyclopentane bridgehead, and the amide-type nitrogen links to the other. A CH2 bridge connects the two bridgeheads, and the remaining two CH2 groups close the cyclopentane.

**Stereochemistry**
There are three stereocentres. The acetal CH has a hashed H, and the two bridgehead CH carbons each have a wedged H. I assigned @/@@ from the 2D positions of the neighbours and the wedge directions, in the SMILES neighbour order.
- Acetal CH: `[C@H]`
- Oxygen-bearing bridgehead: `[C@@H]`
- Nitrogen-bearing bridgehead: `[C@@H]`

I checked that the ring closures pair up and that the atom counts match the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(NCc1c(F)cc(F)cc1F)C1=CN2C[C@H]3O[C@@H]4CC[C@@H](C4)N3C(=O)C2=C(O)C1=O

name: Bithionol
text:
The drawing shows two identical aryl rings joined through a single sulfur atom (a thioether bridge). This is bithionol-type, but with 3,5-dichloro-2-hydroxyphenyl rings, so it is 2,2'-thiobis(4,6-dichlorophenol).

**Left ring.** Going around the ring from the carbon bearing the S-linkage:
- C1 (at about 605,648) is bonded to S.
- C2 (440,566) carries the OH.
- C3 (288,667) carries Cl.
- C4 (300,850) is CH.
- C5 (465,932) carries Cl.
- C6 (617,830) is CH and closes back to C1.

So the ring is 2-hydroxy-3,5-dichlorophenyl attached to S at C1.

**Right ring.** Going around the ring from the carbon bearing S:
- C1 (922,626) is bonded to S.
- C2 (934,809) carries the OH.
- C3 (1099,890) carries Cl.
- C4 (1251,789) is CH.
- C5 (1240,605) carries Cl.
- C6 (1075,524) is CH.

This is the same substitution pattern as the left ring.

SMILES for the full molecule: Oc1c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc1Sc1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1O

SMILES: Oc1c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc1Sc1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1O

name: Bivalirudin
text:
I read the drawing as a linear 20-residue peptide, from the free-amine N-terminus to the free-acid C-terminus:

Phe-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Gly-Gly-Gly-Asn-Gly-Asp-Phe-Glu-Glu-Ile-Pro-Glu-Glu-Tyr-Leu

Each residue is as follows:
- The Arg side chain ends in a guanidine group, written `CCCNC(=N)N`.
- The Asn side chain is a primary amide, `CC(N)=O`.
- The Asp and the four Glu side chains are free carboxylic acids.
- The Tyr side chain carries a para-hydroxyl on the ring.
- The two Phe residues carry benzyl side chains.
- The Ile side chain is sec-butyl.
- The Leu side chain is isobutyl.

I did not trace each wedge or hash individually. I assigned the natural L configuration to every stereocentre, and for Ile also the natural (2S,3S) configuration, which I checked against the standard L-isoleucine SMILES.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(=N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Bleomycin B2
text:
I did not derive every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I assembled this SMILES from the connectivity in the drawing, taking the stereodescriptors from my recollection of bleomycin's isomeric SMILES, so the stereo marks are unverified.

The structure reads as a bleomycin-type glycopeptide with an agmatine tail:

- **Left end:** a guanidine, N=C(N)N, joined through a four-carbon chain and an amide NH to a bithiazole.
- **Middle:** a threonine unit, then a hydroxy-methylpentanoic acid unit (the 3-hydroxy-2,4-dimethyl-5-aminopentanoyl residue). Next comes a β-hydroxyhistidine unit carrying a disaccharide, a gulose with a mannose bearing a carbamate, attached through an ether oxygen.
- **Right end:** a 5-methyl-4-amino pyrimidine bearing the side chain with the secondary amine and two primary amide groups.

I checked the sugar order against the image. The gulose, with its CH2OH, sits on the histidine oxygen, and the carbamoyl mannose is attached to the gulose.

SMILES: CC1=C(N=C(N=C1N)[C@H](CC(=O)N)NC[C@@H](C(=O)N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C2=CN=CN2)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H](O3)CO)O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O4)CO)O)OC(=O)N)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)[C@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)NCCC5=NC(=CS5)C6=NC(=CS6)C(=O)NCCCCN=C(N)N)O

name: Boceprevir
text:
I read the drawing as a boceprevir-type structure: a tert-butyl urea, a tert-leucine residue, a 6,6-dimethyl-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane (cyclopropane-fused proline), and a cyclobutylmethyl α-ketoamide.

- **Urea end:** a tert-butyl group on NH, then C(=O), then NH onto the tert-leucine α-carbon. That carbon carries a tert-butyl group and the amide C(=O) that leads to the ring nitrogen.
- **Tert-leucine stereocentre:** the hashed bond to NH gives S. I checked this against the SMILES chirality tag and they agree.
- **Bicyclic core:** the pyrrolidine nitrogen is acylated by the tert-leucine carbonyl. It is fused to a gem-dimethyl cyclopropane, and the three ring stereocentres are marked with wedges. I took their configuration from the known boceprevir pattern rather than deriving each one from the wedges.
- **Ketoamide side:** the ring α-carbon bears C(=O)NH, which links to a CH carrying CH2–cyclobutyl and C(=O)C(=O)NH2. That CH is drawn with plain bonds, so I left it without stereo.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H]2[C@H]1[C@H](N(C2)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)(C)C)NC(=O)NC(C)(C)C)C(=O)NC(CC3CCC3)C(=O)C(=O)N)C

name: Bleomycin A2
text:
I recognised this as bleomycin A2 and wrote its SMILES from that identification. I then re-derived only one stereocentre, the threonine α-carbon, from the drawing, and it matched. The other stereocentres come from my recollection of the known structure and were not checked against the wedges and hashes in the image.

The pieces I read from the drawing, from left to right:
- **Tail:** a dimethylsulfonium group on a propyl chain, joined by an amide to a bithiazole.
- **Linker and threonine:** an ethylene linker leads to a threonine.
- **Backbone:** a methyl-substituted hydroxy-valerate unit, then a β-hydroxyhistidine carrying an imidazole and a glycosidic oxygen.
- **Disaccharide:** the sugar bearing CH2OH (gulose) is attached to the histidine oxygen. The terminal sugar carries the carbamate (OC(N)=O).
- **Pyrimidine end:** a methyl- and amino-substituted pyrimidine with the asparagine-derived side chain and the terminal diamino-amide.

SMILES: CC1=C(N=C(N=C1N)[C@H](CC(=O)N)NC[C@@H](C(=O)N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C2=CN=CN2)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O4)CO)O)OC(=O)N)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)[C@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)O)C(=O)NCCC5=NC(=CS5)C6=NC(=CS6)C(=O)NCCC[S+](C)C)O

SMILES: CC1=C(N=C(N=C1N)[C@H](CC(=O)N)NC[C@@H](C(=O)N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C2=CN=CN2)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O4)CO)O)OC(=O)N)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)[C@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)O)C(=O)NCCC5=NC(=CS5)C6=NC(=CS6)C(=O)NCCC[S+](C)C)O

name: Boric Acid
text:
The drawing shows a central boron atom with three single bonds, each to an OH group. This is boric acid, B(OH)3. There are no charges or stereochemistry to record.

SMILES: OB(O)O

name: Bocodepsin
text:
I read the structure as a 16-membered macrocycle with a thiazole fused into it and a valine thioester side chain.

**Macrocycle** (going around the ring):
- The thiazole C2 carries a CH2–NH–C(=O)–CH2 link.
- That leads to the ring CH–O, which closes through the ester O–C(=O) to the ring valine α-carbon.
- The valine α-carbon carries an isopropyl group and an NH.
- The NH is bonded to C(=O)–C(CH3)2–NH–C(=O), which returns to the thiazole C4.

**Side chain:** the ring CH–O carries a CH=CH–CH2–CH2–S–C(=O)–CH(NH2)–CH(CH3)2 chain. The double bond is drawn in the trans zigzag, so I wrote it as E.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned the three stereocentres from the wedges and hashes using CIP priorities.
- The side-chain valine α-carbon (hashed NH2) is S.
- The ring valine α-carbon (hashed isopropyl) is S.
- The ring CH–O carbon (wedged vinyl) is S.

I then chose the @/@@ symbols in the SMILES so that each centre comes out as S.

SMILES: CC(C)[C@H](N)C(=O)SCC/C=C/[C@@H]1CC(=O)NCc2nc(cs2)C(=O)NC(C)(C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)O1

name: Boron tribromide
text:
The drawing shows a central boron atom (B) with single bonds to three bromine atoms (Br). That is boron tribromide, BBr3. No charges or stereochemistry are shown.

SMILES: BrB(Br)Br

name: Boron trifluoride
text:
The image shows a central boron atom (B) with single bonds to three fluorine atoms (F). This is boron trifluoride, BF3. There are no charges and no stereochemistry.

SMILES: FB(F)F

name: Boldenone
text:
The drawing shows a steroid skeleton (four fused rings, 17 ring carbons), and I matched it to boldenone by reading it region by region:

- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated dienone, with C1=C2, a C3 ketone (C=O) and C4=C5.
- **C10:** a hashed methyl group, which is the 19-methyl.
- **C13:** a hashed methyl group, which is the 18-methyl.
- **C17:** a hashed OH on the five-membered ring D.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** a wedge H at C9, a hashed H at C8 and a wedge H at C14.

The molecule is drawn mirrored left to right (ring A on the right, ring D on the left), which swaps wedges and hashes. Once that is accounted for, every stereocentre matches the natural configuration: 8β-H, 9α-H, 14α-H, 10β-methyl, 13β-methyl and 17β-OH. This is 17β-hydroxyandrosta-1,4-dien-3-one.

I did not derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom from the drawing. I wrote the SMILES from the standard testosterone SMILES, changed ring A to the 1,4-dien-3-one, and relied on that to carry the natural stereochemistry.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O)CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]34C

name: Bosentan
text:
This structure is bosentan.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Central pyrimidine:** the ring atoms are C4 (bearing NH), N3, C2 (bearing the pyrimidin-2-yl group), N1, C6 (bearing the OCH2CH2OH group) and C5 (bearing the aryloxy group).
- **Left side:** C5 carries an O linked to a benzene ring, which has an OMe on the adjacent (ortho) carbon.
- **Right side:** the NH is bonded to S(=O)(=O), which is bonded to a para-tert-butylphenyl ring.
- **Bottom:** C2 is attached to a second pyrimidine ring through its 2-position, so this ring has an N on each side of the attachment carbon.

SMILES, written in order:
- Sulfonamide: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)Nc1nc(nc(OCCO)c1Oc1ccccc1OC)-c1ncccn1

Check of the central ring: c1 (C4, bearing NH), then n (N3), then c(...) (C2, bearing the pyrimidinyl group), then n (N1), then c(OCCO) (C6), then c1 (C5, bearing OAr). The ring closes properly.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)Nc1nc(nc(OCCO)c1Oc1ccccc1OC)-c1ncccn1

name: Bleomycin
text:
This is bleomycin A2, read from the drawing as follows:

- **Left end:** a dimethylsulfonium on a propyl chain, linked through an amide to a bithiazole.
- **Middle:** an ethylamine link to a threonine residue, then a methyl-hydroxy-valerate unit.
- **Histidine unit:** a β-hydroxyhistidine whose oxygen carries the two-sugar disaccharide, with a carbamate on the terminal sugar.
- **Right end:** a 4-amino-5-methylpyrimidine carrying the diamino-propionamide side chain.

Stereo is written only at the centres drawn with wedges or hashes. The sugar rings have plain bonds, so they carry no stereo marks. The imidazole is attached at the carbon next to the NH, as drawn.

SMILES: C[S+](C)CCCNC(=O)c1csc(n1)-c1csc(n1)CCNC(=O)[C@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)NC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)c1nc(nc(N)c1C)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC[C@H](N)C(N)=O)[C@@H](OC1OC(CO)C(O)C(O)C1OC1OC(CO)C(O)C(OC(N)=O)C1O)c1[nH]cnc1)[C@@H](C)O

name: Bosutinib
text:
This is bosutinib.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Quinoline core:** the ring nitrogen sits at the top and is bonded to a CH. That CH connects to the carbon bearing the nitrile (C#N), which connects to the carbon bearing NH (C4).
- **Benzo ring substituents:** the carbon at position 7 carries the OCH2CH2CH2-N-methylpiperazine chain. The adjacent carbon at position 6 carries the OMe.
- **Aniline ring:** the NH-bearing carbon is flanked by a Cl-bearing carbon on one side and a CH on the other. Going around from the NH carbon: C1 (NH), C2 (Cl), C3 (H), C4 (Cl), C5 (OMe), C6 (H). This gives the 2,4-dichloro-5-methoxyphenyl group.
- **Side chain:** propoxy linker to the piperazine N, with the other piperazine N carrying a methyl.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CCCOc2cc3ncc(C#N)c(Nc4cc(OC)c(Cl)cc4Cl)c3cc2OC)CC1

name: Bortezomib
text:
This structure is bortezomib. I read it in four parts.

- **Left chain:** an isobutyl group (CH(CH3)2–CH2) is attached to a stereocentre that carries B(OH)2 and an NH.
- **Middle:** the NH connects to a C=O, which connects to a second stereocentre bearing a benzyl group (CH2–phenyl) and an NH.
- **Right end:** that NH is acylated by a pyrazine-2-carbonyl group (a 1,4-diazine ring joined through C=O).
- **Stereochemistry:** both stereocentres have one wedge bond to the CH2 substituent, so the implicit hydrogen points away from the viewer.
  - The boron-bearing carbon has priorities N > CH2 > B, which run clockwise on the page, so it is R.
  - The benzyl-bearing carbon has priorities N > C(=O) > CH2, which run counterclockwise, so it is S.

SMILES: B([C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)c1cnccn1)(O)O

name: Bolasterone
text:
I read this as a 7,17-dimethyl-substituted testosterone-type steroid (a 4-en-3-one with a 17-hydroxy-17-methyl group), with methyl groups at C7, C10 and C13. The stereo marks come from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing.

**Skeleton**
- Ring A has the C3 ketone (C=O) and a C4=C5 double bond.
- C10 and C13 each carry a hashed methyl.
- C17 carries an OH and a wedged methyl.
- C7 carries a wedged methyl.
- The ring-fusion hydrogens are drawn explicitly: H on C9 is wedged, H on C8 is hashed, and H on C14 is wedged.

**Stereo assignment**
I worked out each centre from the 2D coordinates and the wedge or hash on its substituent, then converted to SMILES neighbour order:
- C17: @
- C13: @
- C14: @@
- C9: @
- C8: @
- C7: @
- C10: @

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closures (1 to 4) and atom count against the drawing, but I did not check the stereo marks against a reference structure.

SMILES: C[C@]1(O)CC[C@@H]2[C@]1(C)CC[C@H]3[C@H]2[C@H](C)CC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]34C

name: Boro-Scopol
text:
I read this as scopolamine: a phenyl hydroxymethyl acetate ester of a tropane-type bicycle that carries an epoxide.

**Side chain.** A phenyl ring is attached to the stereocentre. That carbon bears a CH2OH on a wedge, a plain bond to the phenyl, and a plain bond to the ester carbonyl C(=O)–O. I worked out the wedge as `OC[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)O…`.

**Bicyclic core.**
- The ester oxygen is attached to a ring carbon with no stereo marking, so it gets none.
- That carbon connects through two CH2 groups to the two bridgehead carbons.
- The bridgeheads are joined by an N–CH3 bridge.
- Each bridgehead is also bonded to one carbon of a C–O–C epoxide, and the two epoxide carbons are bonded to each other.

**Stereo marks.** The bridgehead hydrogens are on wedges. The epoxide hydrogens are on hashes. I assigned `@`/`@@` for each centre from the drawn geometry, using the neighbour order in the SMILES.

I wrote the SMILES with ring closure 1 for the ester-bearing ring, 2 for the nitrogen bridge, and 3 for the epoxide. I did not run this through a cheminformatics tool, so the validity check was done by hand.

SMILES: OC[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)OC1C[C@@H]2[C@H]3O[C@H]3[C@H](C1)N2C

name: Bradykinin
text:
I read the drawing as the linear nonapeptide Arg-Pro-Pro-Gly-Phe-Ser-Pro-Phe-Arg (bradykinin), written from the N-terminus to the free C-terminal acid.

- **N-terminus:** an arginine with a free NH2 on the wedged alpha carbon and a guanidine side chain, `N=C(N)N`.
- **Pro-Pro:** two proline rings, each with a hashed alpha carbon.
- **Gly:** a plain CH2 between the amides.
- **Phe:** a benzyl side chain on a wedged alpha carbon. I checked this centre by hand against the wedge geometry and it comes out as L-Phe.
- **Ser:** a CH2OH side chain.
- **Pro, Phe:** a third proline and a second phenylalanine.
- **C-terminus:** a final arginine ending in COOH.

I assigned the other centres as the natural L-amino-acid configuration, which is consistent with the wedges and hashes shown, but I did not check each one individually.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)O

name: Brigatinib
text:
This structure is brigatinib, and I read it region by region from the drawing.

- **Pyrimidine core:** the ring atoms are N, C(H), C(Cl), C(NH-aryl), N and C(NH-aryl). The Cl sits on the carbon next to the CH.
- **Left aryl group:** the NH at the 4-position of the pyrimidine attaches to a benzene ring that carries a P(=O)(CH3)2 group on the adjacent (ortho) carbon.
- **Right aryl group:** the NH at the 2-position attaches to a second benzene ring. That ring has an OMe ortho to the NH and a piperidin-1-yl group para to the NH.
- **Piperidine and piperazine:** the piperidine is substituted at its 4-position with a piperazine, and that piperazine carries an N-methyl group.

I wrote the SMILES in this order: Clc1cnc(Nc2ccc(cc2OC)N2CCC(CC2)N2CCN(C)CC2)nc1Nc1ccccc1P(C)(C)=O.

Checking the connectivity against the drawing:
- In the pyrimidine, c1(Cl), then c(H), n, c(N...), n, and c1 bearing the NH closes the ring. That matches.
- In the right benzene ring, c2 (bearing the NH), then c, c, c(N-piperidine), c, c2(OMe). The OMe carbon is adjacent to the NH carbon. The piperidine carbon is para to the NH carbon, which fits the drawing, where the ring carbon bearing N is opposite the NH carbon.

SMILES: Clc1cnc(Nc2ccc(cc2OC)N2CCC(CC2)N2CCN(C)CC2)nc1Nc1ccccc1P(C)(C)=O

name: Brexpiprazole
text:
This structure is brexpiprazole-like, but the quinolinone is linked through a butoxy chain and there is no vinyl group, so it is closer to a brexpiprazole analog. The pieces are:

- **Left side:** a benzothiophene attached through its 4-position to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Linker:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries a chain of 4 CH2 groups, which ends in an oxygen.
- **Right side:** that oxygen is bonded to the 7-position of quinolin-2(1H)-one.

**Benzothiophene.** The thiophene ring is S, CH, CH, then the fused carbons. The carbon next to S is a fusion carbon (C7a). The other fusion carbon (C3a) is bonded to the CH=CH. The benzene carbon adjacent to C3a bears the piperazine, so the attachment is at C4.

SMILES for this part: c1cc(N2CCN(...)CC2)c2ccsc2c1

**Linker.** Counting the chain from N: the bonds run N–C, C–C, C–C, then C–O, giving 4 carbons. This matches the picture, with vertices at 630, 705, 787 and 862 before the O.

**Quinolinone.** The ring is O=c1ccc2ccc(OR)cc2[nH]1. The oxygen-bearing carbon is bonded to a CH on one side and to a CH adjacent to the fusion carbon (C8a) bonded to N. That places it at position 7.

Combining the parts:

O=c1ccc2ccc(OCCCCN3CCN(CC3)c3cccc4sccc34)cc2[nH]1

Check on the benzothiophene: c3cccc4sccc34 starts at C4 (the attachment), then C5, C6, C7, then C7a (c4) bonded to s, then the two CH carbons, then C3a (c34), which closes to both C4 and C7a. This is correct.

SMILES: O=c1ccc2ccc(OCCCCN3CCN(CC3)c3cccc4sccc34)cc2[nH]1

name: Brimonidine
text:
This is brimonidine, a quinoxaline bearing an imidazoline ring.

**Imidazoline ring (left):** The ring is CH2–CH2–N=C(–NH)–NH, closed back to the first CH2. The carbon on the right of the ring is double-bonded to the ring N at the lower left and single-bonded to the ring NH at the top. It also carries an exocyclic NH that links to the aromatic ring.

**Quinoxaline (right):**
- The benzene ring carbon attached to the exocyclic NH is adjacent to the carbon bearing Br.
- That Br-bearing carbon is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon, which is bonded to the lower N.
- The pyrazine ring runs N–CH=CH–N between the two fusion carbons.
- The upper fusion carbon connects to the CH=CH part of the benzene ring.

**SMILES:** Starting from the Br carbon: Brc1c(NC2=NCCN2)ccc2nccnc12. Checking the ring closures:
- c1 is the Br carbon.
- c(NC2=NCCN2) is the carbon bearing the amino group.
- cc are the two benzene CH atoms.
- c2 is the upper fusion carbon.
- n, c, c, n are the pyrazine atoms.
- c12 is the lower fusion carbon, bonded to the Br carbon and closing ring 2.

Atom by atom, this matches the drawing.

SMILES: Brc1c(NC2=NCCN2)ccc2nccnc12

name: Bremelanotide
text:
Reading the drawing region by region, I get an N-acetyl-norleucine attached to a cyclic hexapeptide whose ring is closed through an Asp side chain and a Lys side chain.

- **N-terminus:** acetyl on the Nle nitrogen, then Nle (a butyl side chain). The hashed butyl bond reads as L (S).
- **Ring:** Asp, His, Phe, Arg, Trp, Lys.
  - The Asp side-chain CH2–C(=O) forms an amide with the Lys side-chain NH. The four labelled "C" atoms in the ring are the Lys (CH2)4 chain.
  - Lys carries a free COOH at the C-terminus.
- **Side chains:**
  - His is an imidazole attached at the carbon next to the NH.
  - Phe is a phenyl.
  - Arg ends in a guanidine, N=C(N)N.
  - Trp is an indol-3-yl.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned each alpha carbon from its wedge or hash bond and CIP priorities. Nle, Asp, Lys, Trp, Arg and His come out L. Phe comes out D, because its CH2 bond is hashed.

The SMILES below was written to match these assignments and checked against the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCC)C(=O)N[C@H]1CC(=O)NCCCC[C@@H](C(=O)O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2c[nH]c3ccccc23)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2cnc[nH]2)NC1=O

name: Brinzolamide
text:
This structure is brinzolamide, read as follows.

- **Ring system:** a thiophene is fused to a six-membered cyclic sulfonamide (S(=O)(=O) bonded to N). The N carries a 3-methoxypropyl chain (CCCOC).
- **Thiophene substituent:** the thiophene carbon next to the ring S carries a primary sulfonamide, S(N)(=O)=O.
- **Stereocentre:** the ring carbon bearing the ethylamino group (NHCH2CH3) has a hashed bond to N, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - Seen from the front, N (bottom), the ring-junction carbon (upper left) and the CH2 (upper right) run clockwise.
  - For the SMILES neighbour order N, H, ring-junction carbon, CH2, this gives `@`.

SMILES: CCN[C@H]1CN(CCCOC)S(=O)(=O)c2sc(S(N)(=O)=O)cc12

name: Brincidofovir
text:
I read the molecule as the hexadecyloxypropyl ester of cidofovir (HPMPC), a cytosine-based acyclic nucleoside phosphonate.

- **Alkyl chain:** counting the zigzag vertices from the left end gives 16 carbons, so a hexadecyl group. It is joined through an ether O to a three-carbon propyl linker, which ends in an O bonded to phosphorus.
- **Phosphonate:** P carries one =O, one OH, the ester O from the propyl linker, and a CH2 that leads to an ether O.
- **Stereocentre:** the ether O is attached to a stereocentre bearing CH2OH and a wedged CH2 that connects to the cytosine N1. The wedge is the only stereo marking in the drawing.
- **Base:** cytosine, with a 4-NH2, a 2-C=O, and a C5=C6 double bond.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are O > CH2OH > CH2N > H. With the implicit H pointing away, O → CH2OH → CH2N runs counterclockwise, which is S. I encoded this as `[C@H]` with the neighbours written in the order O, H, CH2OH, CH2N.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCOCCCOP(=O)(O)CO[C@H](CO)Cn1ccc(N)nc1=O

name: Brilacidin
text:
I read the molecule as a pyrimidine-4,6-dicarboxamide whose two amide nitrogens are each bonded to the same substituted aryl group.

**Core:** the pyrimidine has C4 and C6 carrying the C(=O)NH groups, with C5 as CH between them and N1/N3 flanking C2 (CH).

**Each aryl ring** has these substituents, with the ring-carbon neighbours in this order:
- the carbon bonded to the pyrimidine amide NH
- a CH
- a carbon bearing CF3
- a CH
- a carbon bonded to NHC(=O)(CH2)4–N=C(NH2)2 (a 5-guanidinopentanamide; I counted four CH2 groups between the C=O and the guanidine N)
- a carbon bearing O-pyrrolidin-3-yl, which sits between the two N-bearing carbons

**Stereochemistry:** each pyrrolidin-3-yl ether carbon is drawn with one wedge or hash bond to O (a hash on the left, a wedge on the right). The priorities are O > C2 (the CH2 next to N) > C4 > H. Working through the geometry, both centres come out as R. In the SMILES, `O[C@@H]1CCNC1` encodes R for each.

SMILES: NC(N)=NCCCCC(=O)Nc1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(NC(=O)c2cc(C(=O)Nc3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(NC(=O)CCCCN=C(N)N)c3O[C@@H]3CCNC3)ncn2)c1O[C@@H]1CCNC1

name: Brevicidine
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing as a lipopeptide with a depsipeptide ring. I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash by working out CIP priorities.

**Sequence, left to right:**
- A 4-methylhexanoyl chain acylates the N-terminus.
- Residues follow in this order: D-Asn, D-Tyr, D-Trp, D-Orn, L-Orn, Gly, D-Orn, L-Trp, L-Thr, L-Ile, Gly, L-Ser.
- The macrocycle closes through an ester between the Ser carbonyl and the Thr side-chain oxygen. The ring atoms are Thr Cα, Thr C=O, Ile, Gly, Ser, the ester O and Thr Cβ.

**Stereochemistry:**
- Thr has the L-configuration (2S,3R) and Ile has the L-configuration (2S,3S).
- The ornithine side chains are plain aminopropyl groups, so only the α-carbons carry stereo.

I checked the SMILES for ring closures (digits 1 and 2 for the indoles and the tyrosine ring, digit 3 for the macrocycle) and for the atom count against the drawing.

SMILES: CCC(C)CCC(=O)N[C@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H]3C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)O[C@@H]3C

name: Brivanib
text:
This structure is brivanib, and its single stereocentre is drawn with a hashed methyl bond.

- **Left ring system:** a 2-methylindole (N–H, methyl on the five-membered ring). The benzene ring carries fluorine next to the ring-fusion carbon, and an aryl ether oxygen on the carbon adjacent to the fluorine-bearing carbon.
- **Core:** the aryl ether oxygen links to C4 of a pyrrolo[2,1-f][1,2,4]triazine. Its pyrrole ring has a methyl at C5 and an O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH3 ether at C6.
- **Stereocentre:** the carbon bearing OH has OH drawn up, CH2 to the lower left and CH3 hashed to the lower right, so the hydrogen points toward the viewer. Priorities are OH > CH2O > CH3 > H. Going OH → CH2 → CH3 appears counterclockwise from the front, and with H toward the viewer that reverses to clockwise, giving R.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** in `C[C@@H](O)CO...` the neighbour order is CH3, H, O, CH2. The `@@` tag encodes R for this order, so that is the tag used.

SMILES: C[C@@H](O)COc1cn2ncnc(Oc3ccc4[nH]c(C)cc4c3F)c2c1C

name: Brivaracetam
text:
I read this as brivaracetam, (2S)-2-[(4R)-2-oxo-4-propylpyrrolidin-1-yl]butanamide.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- On the left is a primary amide, H2N–C(=O)–.
- Its carbonyl carbon connects to a stereocentre. That carbon carries an ethyl group drawn on a wedge and is bonded to the ring nitrogen.
- The ring is a five-membered lactam: N, C(=O), CH2, CH and CH2. The ring CH carries a propyl chain drawn on a wedge.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Side-chain carbon:** the priorities are N > C(=O)NH2 > ethyl, with H pointing back. Tracing N (upper right) to C(=O)N (upper left) to ethyl (down) runs counterclockwise, so this centre is S.
- **Ring carbon:** the priorities are CH2–N > CH2–C(=O) > propyl, with H pointing back. Tracing down-left to up-left to right runs clockwise, so this centre is R.
- I checked that `[C@H]` for the ring carbon and `[C@@H]` for the side-chain carbon in the SMILES below give R and S respectively.

SMILES: CCC[C@H]1CN(C(=O)C1)[C@@H](CC)C(N)=O

name: Brevetoxin B
text:
I read the drawing as a brevetoxin-type polyether, working ring by ring from the left.

- **Left end:** an α,β-unsaturated six-membered lactone with a methyl on the C=C, fused to a six-membered ether ring.
- **Middle:** two six-membered and two seven-membered ether rings (one seven-membered ring carries a CH-methyl), then two six-membered rings with angular methyls.
- **Eight-membered ring:** an eight-membered ether ring containing a ring CH=CH. I wrote this double bond without cis/trans marking, since it sits inside the ring.
- **Right end:** two fused six-membered ether rings, then a six-membered ring bearing the hydroxyl and a CH2–C(=CH2)–CHO side chain.

Stereochemistry is assigned from the wedges and hashes at every drawn centre. I read each centre from its 2D coordinates and converted to @/@@ by hand, so the descriptors are the part most likely to contain an error. I did not run the SMILES through a parser.

SMILES: CC1=CC(=O)O[C@H]2C[C@@H]3[C@@](C)(O[C@H]12)C[C@@H]4[C@@H](O3)C[C@@H](C)[C@@H]5[C@@H](O4)CC[C@@](C)6[C@@H](O5)C[C@@H]7[C@@](C)(O6)C[C@@H]8[C@@](C)(O7)CC=C[C@@H]9[C@@H](O8)C[C@@H]%10[C@@H](O9)C[C@@H]%11[C@@](C)(O%10)[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](CC(=C)C=O)O%11
